This instance (CVE-2019-18224): idn2_to_ascii_4i() strcpy()s the lookup result output_u8 into the caller's output buffer (documented as 64 bytes) without checking that its length is at most 63, causing a buffer overflow for long domains.

review.ground_truth: idn2_to_ascii_4i() strcpy()s the lookup result output_u8 into the caller's output buffer (documented as 64 bytes) without checking that its length is at most 63, causing a buffer overflow for long domains.
review.reasoning: The function copies output_u8 into the caller-supplied output buffer with strcpy, and it never checks the length. The documented API contract says that buffer only has room for 63 characters plus the terminator. A long domain gives an output_u8 longer than 63 bytes, which overflows the caller's buffer. The fix adds the length check, so the flaw is real and sits in this function.

description:
CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference
This instance (CVE-2021-46485): Jsi_ValueIsNumber() dereferences pv->vt without first checking that pv is non-NULL, so a caller passing a NULL value causes a segfault.

review.ground_truth: Jsi_ValueIsNumber() dereferences pv->vt without first checking that pv is non-NULL, so a caller passing a NULL value causes a segfault.
review.reasoning: The fix adds a NULL check on pv before dereferencing pv->vt. Callers can pass a NULL Jsi_Value, for example a missing argument, and that crashes the interpreter. The flaw is a NULL pointer dereference in this function, and the diff matches it. Whether a caller can actually pass NULL requires an assumption about callers.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2016-3863): convertMessageToMetaData() passes a fixed 1024-byte stack buffer avcc to reassembleAVCC(), which copies the attacker-sized csd-0 and csd-1 buffers into it without bounds, causing a stack buffer overflow.

review.ground_truth: convertMessageToMetaData() passes a fixed 1024-byte stack buffer avcc to reassembleAVCC(), which copies the attacker-sized csd-0 and csd-1 buffers into it without bounds, causing a stack buffer overflow.
review.reasoning: The function puts a fixed 1024-byte stack array avcc in place and passes it to reassembleAVCC(csd0, csd1, avcc). That callee copies the csd0 and csd1 contents, whose sizes are attacker-controlled, with no bounds limit. A crafted file with large SPS/PPS buffers therefore overflows the stack buffer. The fix sizes the buffer as csd0size + csd1->size() + 1024 on the heap. The CWE-284 label is generic; the real flaw is a stack buffer overflow (CWE-121/787).

description:
CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference
This instance (CVE-2016-7445): skip_white() dereferences its argument s in `while(*s)` without a NULL check, so the NULL returned by a prior skip_int/skip_white on malformed PNM header input crashes it.

review.ground_truth: skip_white() dereferences its argument s in `while(*s)` without a NULL check, so the NULL returned by a prior skip_int/skip_white on malformed PNM header input crashes it.
review.reasoning: skip_white() dereferences s (`*s`) without checking it for NULL. Callers in read_pnm_header chain calls like s = skip_int(s, &val), and skip_int returns NULL on malformed input. The NULL return then reaches skip_white, which crashes. The fix adds the NULL check in this function, so the flaw is here, but triggering it depends on callers passing NULL.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2016-7161): eth_rx() memcpy's the received packet of length size into &s->regs[rxbase + R_RX_BUF0] without checking size against the remaining space in the regs array, so a large packet overflows the heap buffer.

review.ground_truth: eth_rx() memcpy's the received packet of length size into &s->regs[rxbase + R_RX_BUF0] without checking size against the remaining space in the regs array, so a large packet overflows the heap buffer.
review.reasoning: eth_rx copies the packet with memcpy into s->regs starting at rxbase + R_RX_BUF0, using the attacker-controlled size and no bound against the remaining register array. A large packet writes past the end of regs and corrupts heap state in the device struct. The fix adds a check of size against (R_MAX - R_RX_BUF0 - rxbase)*4.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2016-9423): formUpdateBuffer() passes spos/epos from the anchor to form_update_line() without checking that a->start.line == a->end.line and spos <= epos, so a crafted form anchor makes form_update_line overflow the line's heap buffers.

review.ground_truth: formUpdateBuffer() passes spos/epos from the anchor to form_update_line() without checking that a->start.line == a->end.line and spos <= epos, so a crafted form anchor makes form_update_line overflow the line's heap buffers.
review.reasoning: The fix forces epos = spos when the anchor spans several lines or spos > epos. Without that check, form_update_line gets an inverted or cross-line range: epos - spos goes negative, or epos runs past the line, so lineBuf is overrun. This matches the heap overflow in the CVE. The root cause is a missing validation of the anchor range (spos/epos) before the copy, so it is best classed as an out-of-bounds write.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2016-9425): In addMultirowsForm, pos (from columnPos) and a->end.pos (pos + ecol - col) are used to write l->lineBuf[pos - 1], l->lineBuf[a->end.pos] and l->propBuf[k] without checking pos >= 1 or end.pos < l->size, causing a heap buffer overflow.

review.ground_truth: In addMultirowsForm, pos (from columnPos) and a->end.pos (pos + ecol - col) are used to write l->lineBuf[pos - 1], l->lineBuf[a->end.pos] and l->propBuf[k] without checking pos >= 1 or end.pos < l->size, causing a heap buffer overflow.
review.reasoning: The function writes l->lineBuf[pos - 1], l->lineBuf[a->end.pos] and l->propBuf[k] without checking that pos >= 1 or that end.pos < l->size. pos comes from columnPos() on a different line, and end.pos is pos + ecol - col, so a crafted multirow textarea can push both indices outside the heap line buffer. The fix adds exactly this bounds check, so the flaw is real and lives in this function.

description:
CWE-908: Use of Uninitialized Resource
This instance (CVE-2016-9756): em_jmp_far() fills old_sel/old_desc via get_segment only in 64-bit mode, but when assign_eip_far fails in another mode it passes these uninitialized stack variables to ops->set_segment for CS, leaking host kernel stack data to the guest.

review.ground_truth: em_jmp_far() fills old_sel/old_desc via get_segment only in 64-bit mode, but when assign_eip_far fails in another mode it passes these uninitialized stack variables to ops->set_segment for CS, leaking host kernel stack data to the guest.
review.reasoning: In em_jmp_far, old_sel and old_desc are filled by get_segment only when mode is PROT64. assign_eip_far can also fail outside 64-bit mode. When it does, set_segment is called with the uninitialized old_sel/old_desc stack values, which loads kernel stack contents into the guest's CS and leaks them. The fix removes this recovery path, so the flaw is real and lives in this function.

description:
CWE-416: Use After Free
This instance (CVE-2022-0487): In the err_out path of rtsx_usb_ms_drv_probe(), memstick_free_host(msh) frees the host (whose private area holds host) before pm_runtime_disable(ms_dev(host)) and pm_runtime_put_noidle(ms_dev(host)) dereference it.

review.ground_truth: In the err_out path of rtsx_usb_ms_drv_probe(), memstick_free_host(msh) frees the host (whose private area holds host) before pm_runtime_disable(ms_dev(host)) and pm_runtime_put_noidle(ms_dev(host)) dereference it.
review.reasoning: This is the probe function. Its error path calls memstick_free_host(msh), which frees msh, and host is the private data embedded inside msh. It then calls ms_dev(host) for pm_runtime_disable and pm_runtime_put_noidle, which uses the freed memory. The fix moves the free after those calls, so this is a genuine use-after-free in the shown function, even though the CVE names the remove function.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2016-6160): In rewrite_packets(), memcpy(*pktdata, pktconst, pkthdr.caplen) copies an attacker-controlled caplen from the pcap file into the MAXPACKET-sized pktdata_buff without checking caplen against MAXPACKET, causing a heap buffer overflow.

review.ground_truth: In rewrite_packets(), memcpy(*pktdata, pktconst, pkthdr.caplen) copies an attacker-controlled caplen from the pcap file into the MAXPACKET-sized pktdata_buff without checking caplen against MAXPACKET, causing a heap buffer overflow.
review.reasoning: The function does memcpy(*pktdata, pktconst, pkthdr.caplen) into pktdata_buff, which was allocated with MAXPACKET bytes. caplen comes from the pcap file and is never checked against MAXPACKET, so a large frame overflows the heap buffer. The fix adds exactly that bound check. The CWE-399 label is generic; the real flaw is a heap buffer overflow, an out-of-bounds write.

description:
CWE-416: Use After Free
This instance (CVE-2015-6789): MutationObserverInterestGroup::enqueueMutationRecord() takes raw MutationObserver* keys from m_observers and calls observer->enqueueMutationRecord() on them, even though the observer may have been freed because the group held no strong reference to it.

review.ground_truth: MutationObserverInterestGroup::enqueueMutationRecord() takes raw MutationObserver* keys from m_observers and calls observer->enqueueMutationRecord() on them, even though the observer may have been freed because the group held no strong reference to it.
review.reasoning: m_observers held MutationObserver objects as raw pointers. While mutation records were being collected, an observer could be garbage-collected, and this function would then dereference the dangling key via observer->enqueueMutationRecord. The fix makes the map hold RefPtr so the observers stay alive; this function only gains a .get(), but it is where the freed pointer is used. The race label names the trigger, while the root cause is the lifetime error leading to use-after-free.

description:
CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference
This instance (CVE-2015-8711): In dissect_nbap_E_DCH_FDD_Information_to_Modify, the return value of conversation_get_proto_data(old_conversation, proto_fp) is passed directly as the memcpy source without a NULL check, so an old conversation lacking FP data causes a NULL pointer dereference.

review.ground_truth: In dissect_nbap_E_DCH_FDD_Information_to_Modify, the return value of conversation_get_proto_data(old_conversation, proto_fp) is passed directly as the memcpy source without a NULL check, so an old conversation lacking FP data causes a NULL pointer dereference.
review.reasoning: The old conversation can exist without FP proto data attached. In that case conversation_get_proto_data() returns NULL and memcpy reads from that NULL source. This matches the CVE, which describes a NULL pointer dereference, and the fix adds a NULL check on the returned pointer. The nbap_edch_channel_info[e_dch_macdflow_id] index is a possible concern, but it is not evident from this function alone.

description:
CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference
This instance (CVE-2015-8722): In dissect_fragmented_payload(), the frame pointer returned by wmem_list_frame_next(cur) after dissect_payload() is passed to wmem_list_frame_data() without a NULL check, so a NULL pointer is dereferenced when no subsequent layer exists.

review.ground_truth: In dissect_fragmented_payload(), the frame pointer returned by wmem_list_frame_next(cur) after dissect_payload() is passed to wmem_list_frame_data() without a NULL check, so a NULL pointer is dereferenced when no subsequent layer exists.
review.reasoning: After dissect_payload(), wmem_list_frame_next(cur) can return NULL when no subdissector added a layer. That NULL frame is then passed to wmem_list_frame_data(), which dereferences it. The fix adds an if (cur) guard around this code. This matches the CVE's NULL frame pointer dereference, and the CWE-20 label is too generic; CWE-476 is the specific weakness.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2015-8723): AirPDcapPacketProcess() does memcpy(decrypt_data, data, tot_len) into the stack buffer tmp_data[AIRPDCAP_MAX_CAPLEN] (or a caller buffer of that size) without checking that tot_len does not exceed AIRPDCAP_MAX_CAPLEN, causing a stack buffer overflow.

review.ground_truth: AirPDcapPacketProcess() does memcpy(decrypt_data, data, tot_len) into the stack buffer tmp_data[AIRPDCAP_MAX_CAPLEN] (or a caller buffer of that size) without checking that tot_len does not exceed AIRPDCAP_MAX_CAPLEN, causing a stack buffer overflow.
review.reasoning: The function copies tot_len bytes into decrypt_data with memcpy(decrypt_data, data, *decrypt_len). decrypt_data is either the local stack buffer tmp_data[AIRPDCAP_MAX_CAPLEN] or a caller buffer of that size. Nothing checks that tot_len <= AIRPDCAP_MAX_CAPLEN, so a frame larger than 8KB overflows the stack buffer. The fix adds exactly that upper-bound check.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2015-8730): dissect_nbap_LogicalChannelID() writes nbap_edch_channel_info[e_dch_macdflow_id].lchId[num_items-1] without checking num_items>0, so num_items==0 gives an index of -1 and an out-of-bounds write.

review.ground_truth: dissect_nbap_LogicalChannelID() writes nbap_edch_channel_info[e_dch_macdflow_id].lchId[num_items-1] without checking num_items>0, so num_items==0 gives an index of -1 and an out-of-bounds write.
review.reasoning: The function writes to lchId[num_items-1] using the global num_items without checking it is positive. If no list item has been counted (num_items==0), the index becomes -1 and the write lands before the array, which is an out-of-bounds write. The fix adds a num_items>0 guard around the write. Whether num_items can be 0 depends on the global state set by other dissector functions, so the flaw only partly shows from this function alone.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2015-8730): dissect_nbap_E_DCH_DDI_Value() writes nbap_edch_channel_info[e_dch_macdflow_id].edch_ddi[num_items-1] without checking num_items>0, so a zero item count yields an index of -1 and an out-of-bounds write.

review.ground_truth: dissect_nbap_E_DCH_DDI_Value() writes nbap_edch_channel_info[e_dch_macdflow_id].edch_ddi[num_items-1] without checking num_items>0, so a zero item count yields an index of -1 and an out-of-bounds write.
review.reasoning: The function writes to edch_ddi[num_items-1] without checking that num_items is positive. num_items is a global set from the packet's item count, so a crafted packet with zero items makes the index -1 and the write lands before the array. The fix adds a num_items>0 guard. This is an out-of-bounds write caused by a missing check, not a generic input-validation issue.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2015-8736): In mp2t_find_next_pcr(), the stack array buffer[MP2T_SIZE] receives MP2T_SIZE+trailer_len bytes from wtap_read_bytes_or_eof, so a non-zero trailer_len causes a stack buffer overflow.

review.ground_truth: In mp2t_find_next_pcr(), the stack array buffer[MP2T_SIZE] receives MP2T_SIZE+trailer_len bytes from wtap_read_bytes_or_eof, so a non-zero trailer_len causes a stack buffer overflow.
review.reasoning: The stack buffer is declared as MP2T_SIZE bytes. wtap_read_bytes_or_eof then reads MP2T_SIZE+trailer_len bytes into it, and trailer_len is non-zero when the file has a trailer. The read therefore writes past the end of the stack buffer. The fix enlarges the buffer by TRAILER_LEN_MAX, which confirms this is the flaw.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2015-7512): In pcnet_receive(), when !s->looptest, memcpy(src, buf, size) and the following src[size..size+3] writes copy a packet of unchecked length into the fixed 4096-byte s->buffer, overflowing it for packets larger than 4092 bytes.

review.ground_truth: In pcnet_receive(), when !s->looptest, memcpy(src, buf, size) and the following src[size..size+3] writes copy a packet of unchecked length into the fixed 4096-byte s->buffer, overflowing it for packets larger than 4092 bytes.
review.reasoning: In the non-looptest path, memcpy(src, buf, size) copies the backend-supplied packet into s->buffer, a fixed 4096-byte array, and then writes 4 CRC bytes at src[size..size+3]. Nothing checks size against the buffer length first. A large packet (larger MTU) therefore overflows s->buffer. The fix truncates size to 4092 before the copy.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2016-0546): print_arrays_for() calls sprintf(buf, "%s.conf", set) with no length bound, so a long `set` name overflows the fixed-size global buffer `buf`.

review.ground_truth: print_arrays_for() calls sprintf(buf, "%s.conf", set) with no length bound, so a long `set` name overflows the fixed-size global buffer `buf`.
review.reasoning: The function writes the caller-supplied charset name `set` into the fixed-size global `buf` with an unbounded sprintf. A long name therefore overflows `buf`, and the fix replaces the call with snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), ...). This is part of the same commit's sprintf/strcpy hardening, but it sits in the conf_to_src build utility rather than the mysqlshow code the CVE describes. The overflow itself is genuine, though its security impact is limited because the input comes from the command line.

description:
CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference
This instance (CVE-2015-8630): In kadm5_modify_principal(), when mask includes KADM5_POLICY, entry->policy is passed to get_policy() and strdup() without checking that it is non-NULL, so a remote client supplying a NULL policy name causes a NULL pointer dereference.

review.ground_truth: In kadm5_modify_principal(), when mask includes KADM5_POLICY, entry->policy is passed to get_policy() and strdup() without checking that it is non-NULL, so a remote client supplying a NULL policy name causes a NULL pointer dereference.
review.reasoning: When KADM5_POLICY is set in the mask, the function uses entry->policy without first checking that it is non-NULL. The NULL value is passed to get_policy() and also to strdup(entry->policy), and strdup of NULL crashes kadmind. The fix adds a check that rejects the request when KADM5_POLICY is set but entry->policy is NULL. Of the two crash points, strdup is visible here; get_policy may also dereference the name.

description:
CWE-401: Missing Release of Memory after Effective Lifetime (memory leak)
This instance (CVE-2014-3513): In ssl_ctx_make_profiles(), when find_profile_by_name() fails the function returns 1 without freeing the allocated `profiles` stack, leaking it.

review.ground_truth: In ssl_ctx_make_profiles(), when find_profile_by_name() fails the function returns 1 without freeing the allocated `profiles` stack, leaking it.
review.reasoning: On the unknown-profile error path the function returns 1 without freeing the `profiles` stack it allocated, so the stack leaks; the fix adds sk_SRTP_PROTECTION_PROFILE_free on that path. The leak is plainly visible in this function. However, the CVE's remotely triggerable leak lives mainly in the ClientHello SRTP extension parser, while this function only parses a locally supplied configuration string. So this is a genuine leak repaired by the same commit, but not the remote attack path the CVE describes. The CWE-20 label is generic; the actual mechanism is a missing free.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2013-4534): openpic_load() reads opp->nb_cpus from the migration stream without checking it against MAX_CPU, then loops over opp->dst[i] writing incoming data, overflowing the dst[] array.

review.ground_truth: openpic_load() reads opp->nb_cpus from the migration stream without checking it against MAX_CPU, then loops over opp->dst[i] writing incoming data, overflowing the dst[] array.
review.reasoning: In openpic_load(), opp->nb_cpus is read straight from the migration stream and then used as the loop bound when writing into opp->dst[], which holds only MAX_CPU elements. Nothing checks the value, so a hostile stream can write attacker-controlled data past the end of dst[]. This is a plain out-of-bounds write caused by a missing bounds check. The max_irq loop uses a value that is not read from the stream, so it is fine.

description:
CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference
This instance (CVE-2014-5354): krb5_encode_krbsecretkey() returns NULL instead of an empty array when n_key_data is 0 (the `n_key_data <= 0` check), and the caller dereferences that NULL; additionally, after k5calloc it checks key_data_in instead of key_data, so an allocation failure leads to memcpy into a NULL pointer.

review.ground_truth: krb5_encode_krbsecretkey() returns NULL instead of an empty array when n_key_data is 0 (the `n_key_data <= 0` check), and the caller dereferences that NULL; additionally, after k5calloc it checks key_data_in instead of key_data, so an allocation failure leads to memcpy into a NULL pointer.
review.reasoning: The CVE's crash comes from krb5_encode_krbsecretkey() returning NULL when n_key_data is 0, because of the `n_key_data <= 0` short-circuit. The caller krb5_add_ber_mem_ldap_mod() then dereferences that NULL without checking it. This function also tests the wrong pointer after k5calloc: it checks key_data_in instead of key_data, so a failed allocation leads to memcpy into NULL. The fix repairs both problems in this function, so the flaw is genuine and rooted here, though the CVE's actual dereference happens in the caller.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2010-1084): rfcomm_sock_sysfs_show() appends a line per socket in rfcomm_sk_list to the one-page sysfs buf with unbounded sprintf and no PAGE_SIZE limit, so a large number of sockets overflows the buffer.

review.ground_truth: rfcomm_sock_sysfs_show() appends a line per socket in rfcomm_sk_list to the one-page sysfs buf with unbounded sprintf and no PAGE_SIZE limit, so a large number of sockets overflows the buffer.
review.reasoning: The function writes one line per RFCOMM socket into the sysfs buffer using unbounded sprintf. Nothing limits the total output to PAGE_SIZE, so with many sockets it writes past the one-page buffer. The fix switches to snprintf with a remaining-size counter and stops when the page is full. This is a heap/page overflow, which matches the CWE-119 class.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2010-1084): sco_sysfs_show() appends one line per SCO socket into the PAGE_SIZE sysfs buffer with unbounded sprintf(str, ...), so many sockets overflow the page.

review.ground_truth: sco_sysfs_show() appends one line per SCO socket into the PAGE_SIZE sysfs buffer with unbounded sprintf(str, ...), so many sockets overflow the page.
review.reasoning: The sysfs show buffer is one page (PAGE_SIZE). The loop calls sprintf once per SCO socket and never checks how much space is left, so a large number of sockets writes past the end of the page. The fix switches to snprintf with a remaining-size counter and stops when the page is full. This is a heap/page out-of-bounds write that is visible in this function, given the standard sysfs PAGE_SIZE buffer contract.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2010-2527): write_header() uses sprintf with unbounded %s to copy the font-supplied face->family_name, face->style_name and basename into the fixed-size status.header_buffer, overflowing it when the strings are long.

review.ground_truth: write_header() uses sprintf with unbounded %s to copy the font-supplied face->family_name, face->style_name and basename into the fixed-size status.header_buffer, overflowing it when the strings are long.
review.reasoning: The fixed-size status.header_buffer is filled with sprintf using unbounded %s for face->family_name and face->style_name, which come from the font file, and for basename. A crafted font with long names overflows the buffer. The fix adds precision limits to these specifiers, confirming this is the patched flaw.

description:
CWE-416: Use After Free
This instance (CVE-2022-2318): rose_idletimer_expiry() dereferences and locks sk via bh_lock_sock() without holding a socket reference for the pending timer, so a concurrent rose_release()/sock_put() can free the socket while the handler runs (del_timer does not wait for a running handler).

review.ground_truth: rose_idletimer_expiry() dereferences and locks sk via bh_lock_sock() without holding a socket reference for the pending timer, so a concurrent rose_release()/sock_put() can free the socket while the handler runs (del_timer does not wait for a running handler).
review.reasoning: The fix makes the start functions use sk_reset_timer(), which takes a sock reference, and makes the expiry handlers drop that reference with sock_put(). rose_idletimer_expiry() is one of the three handlers named in the commit. As shown, the handler runs with no reference held on sk, so it can lock and modify a socket that rose_release()/sock_put() has already freed. The flaw is a refcount/lifetime race; seeing it fully needs knowledge of how the timer is started and stopped elsewhere.

description:
CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference
This instance (CVE-2010-4242): hci_uart_tty_open() attaches the line discipline without checking that tty->ops->write is non-NULL, so a later transmit through tty->ops->write calls a NULL function pointer.

review.ground_truth: hci_uart_tty_open() attaches the line discipline without checking that tty->ops->write is non-NULL, so a later transmit through tty->ops->write calls a NULL function pointer.
review.reasoning: The fix adds a check that tty->ops->write is non-NULL before attaching the HCI UART line discipline. Without it, the ldisc attaches to a tty with no write op, and a later call to tty->ops->write in the write path (hci_uart_tx_wakeup) dereferences a NULL function pointer. The missing check belongs in this function, but the actual dereference happens in a different function.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2011-0712): snd_usb_caiaq_audio_init() uses strcpy() to copy the USB-supplied dev->product_name into the fixed-size dev->pcm->name without bounding the length, so a long device name overflows the pcm name array.

review.ground_truth: snd_usb_caiaq_audio_init() uses strcpy() to copy the USB-supplied dev->product_name into the fixed-size dev->pcm->name without bounding the length, so a long device name overflows the pcm name array.
review.reasoning: The function copies dev->product_name into dev->pcm->name with strcpy() and no length limit. pcm->name is 80 bytes, while product_name is a larger buffer filled from the USB device's product string. A long, device-controlled name therefore overflows pcm->name. The fix replaces strcpy with strlcpy bounded by sizeof(pcm->name), so this is a real stack/heap buffer overflow (write).

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2011-0712): snd_usb_caiaq_midi_init() uses strcpy to copy device->product_name, a USB-supplied name that can be longer than the destination, into the fixed-size rmidi->name array without a length bound, overflowing it.

review.ground_truth: snd_usb_caiaq_midi_init() uses strcpy to copy device->product_name, a USB-supplied name that can be longer than the destination, into the fixed-size rmidi->name array without a length bound, overflowing it.
review.reasoning: The function does an unbounded strcpy of device->product_name, which comes from the USB device, into the fixed-size rmidi->name array (80 bytes). product_name is a larger buffer (128 bytes), so a long device name overflows rmidi->name. The fix replaces it with a bounded strlcpy, which matches this code exactly.

description:
CWE-125: Out-of-bounds Read
This instance (CVE-2011-1163): osf_partition() loops up to the unvalidated on-disk label->d_npartitions while advancing the partition pointer, reading past the 8-entry d_partitions array and leaking heap memory via put_partition.

review.ground_truth: osf_partition() loops up to the unvalidated on-disk label->d_npartitions while advancing the partition pointer, reading past the 8-entry d_partitions array and leaking heap memory via put_partition.
review.reasoning: The loop bound comes straight from the on-disk label->d_npartitions and is never validated. That lets the partition pointer walk past the 8-entry d_partitions array, and past the sector buffer, into kernel heap memory. The values read there are handed to put_partition and so leak heap contents. The fix adds a check against MAX_OSF_PARTITIONS. The CWE-20 label is generic; the root cause is an out-of-bounds read.

description:
CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference
This instance (CVE-2022-34967): rel_order_by_column_exp() descends from a processed simple projection with `r = r->l` without checking that `r->l` is non-NULL, so for single-row projections `r` becomes NULL and is then used (e.g. `r->card` in the GROUP BY check loop).

review.ground_truth: rel_order_by_column_exp() descends from a processed simple projection with `r = r->l` without checking that `r->l` is non-NULL, so for single-row projections `r` becomes NULL and is then used (e.g. `r->card` in the GROUP BY check loop).
review.reasoning: The fix adds an `r->l` check before descending into a processed simple projection. Before the fix, a projection with no inner relation (a single-row/constant SELECT) makes `r = r->l` set `r` to NULL. `p` stays non-NULL, so the `e && p` branch runs. If the ORDER BY expression does not match any projection, the loop compares `ee->card > r->card` and dereferences the NULL `r`. The CVE's assertion failure is one observed symptom of handling this NULL inner relation; the root cause is the missing NULL check on `r->l`.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2017-5957): The guest-controlled nr_cbufs is never bounded to 8, so the loop in vrend_decode_set_framebuffer_state() writes past the end of the 8-element stack array surf_handle[].

review.ground_truth: The guest-controlled nr_cbufs is never bounded to 8, so the loop in vrend_decode_set_framebuffer_state() writes past the end of the 8-element stack array surf_handle[].
review.reasoning: nr_cbufs comes from guest command data and is checked only against length (length must equal 2 + nr_cbufs). It is never checked against the size of the 8-entry stack array surf_handle. The loop therefore writes past the end of surf_handle whenever nr_cbufs > 8. The fix adds exactly that bound check, so the flaw is in this function as shown.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2017-6209): The while loop in parse_identifier writes ret[i++] = *cur++ for every alphanumeric/underscore character with no bound on i, overflowing the caller's fixed-size stack buffer ret when given a long identifier.

review.ground_truth: The while loop in parse_identifier writes ret[i++] = *cur++ for every alphanumeric/underscore character with no bound on i, overflowing the caller's fixed-size stack buffer ret when given a long identifier.
review.reasoning: parse_identifier copies identifier characters into the caller's fixed-size buffer ret without any length limit. The callers pass stack buffers such as char id[64]. A long identifier in the shader text therefore overflows the stack buffer. The fix adds a len parameter and checks against it. Spotting the overflow assumes ret is fixed-size, which comes from the callers.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2017-6429): In main(), the attacker-controlled packet caplen from the pcap header is passed to read(fd, &buf, caplen) into the fixed 10000-byte stack buffer buf without bounding it to sizeof(buf), causing a stack buffer overflow.

review.ground_truth: In main(), the attacker-controlled packet caplen from the pcap header is passed to read(fd, &buf, caplen) into the fixed 10000-byte stack buffer buf without bounding it to sizeof(buf), causing a stack buffer overflow.
review.reasoning: The function reads caplen, a value taken from the file, into the 10000-byte stack buffer with read(fd, &buf, caplen). Nothing checks caplen against sizeof(buf). The code only compares caplen to snaplen, and snaplen also comes from the file and is merely flagged. The fix aborts when caplen exceeds snaplen, which shows the overflow is in this function.

description:
CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference
This instance (CVE-2017-6441): zend_compile_declare() does not verify that the declare value_ast is a literal (ZEND_AST_ZVAL), so for declare(ticks=<non-literal expr>) zend_const_expr_to_zval yields an unusable zval and zval_get_long dereferences a NULL pointer.

review.ground_truth: zend_compile_declare() does not verify that the declare value_ast is a literal (ZEND_AST_ZVAL), so for declare(ticks=<non-literal expr>) zend_const_expr_to_zval yields an unusable zval and zval_get_long dereferences a NULL pointer.
review.reasoning: zend_compile_declare passes value_ast to zend_const_expr_to_zval without checking that it is a literal ZEND_AST_ZVAL node. A non-literal expression such as a constant or a nested expression can leave value_zv as a constant-AST or otherwise unusable zval. zval_get_long() then dereferences it and crashes with a NULL dereference. The fix adds the literal check in this function, so the flaw is here, though seeing the actual crash needs callee knowledge. The vendor disputes whether this is a security issue, but the crash itself is real.

description:
CWE-125: Out-of-bounds Read
This instance (CVE-2017-9204): get_exif_tag_int_value() reads e->d[tag_pos+2], e->d[tag_pos+4] and e->d[tag_pos+8] via iw_get_ui16_e/iw_get_ui32_e without checking the offsets against the Exif buffer length, allowing an out-of-bounds read with crafted Exif tag positions.

review.ground_truth: get_exif_tag_int_value() reads e->d[tag_pos+2], e->d[tag_pos+4] and e->d[tag_pos+8] via iw_get_ui16_e/iw_get_ui32_e without checking the offsets against the Exif buffer length, allowing an out-of-bounds read with crafted Exif tag positions.
review.reasoning: The function reads e->d at tag_pos+2, +4 and +8 using raw iw_get_ui16_e/iw_get_ui32_e. It never checks these offsets against e->d_len, and tag_pos comes from attacker-controlled IFD data. The fix replaces these calls with bounds-checked get_exif_ui16/get_exif_ui32 wrappers, so the out-of-bounds read is real and sits in this function. Whether tag_pos itself can exceed the buffer depends on the caller, but the function does no checking of its own.

description:
CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference
This instance (CVE-2017-9250): lexer_process_char_literal calls jmem_heap_alloc_block(length) when has_escape is set even if length is 0, storing the resulting NULL in literal_p->u.char_p, which is later used and freed via jmem_heap_free_block causing a NULL pointer dereference.

review.ground_truth: lexer_process_char_literal calls jmem_heap_alloc_block(length) when has_escape is set even if length is 0, storing the resulting NULL in literal_p->u.char_p, which is later used and freed via jmem_heap_free_block causing a NULL pointer dereference.
review.reasoning: When has_escape is true and length is 0 (e.g. an escape sequence that produces no characters, such as a line continuation), jmem_heap_alloc_block(0) returns NULL. That NULL is stored in literal_p->u.char_p and then passed to memcpy, and later to jmem_heap_free_block, which dereferences it. The fix forces has_escape=false for zero length so no allocation happens. The flaw is visible in this function, given the known allocator behavior for size 0.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2017-9431): internal_set_time() does not check whether get_placement() returned the UINT8_MAX 'arena full' sentinel, so memcpy writes a gpr_timespec to (*err)->arena + 255, past the end of the heap arena.

review.ground_truth: internal_set_time() does not check whether get_placement() returned the UINT8_MAX 'arena full' sentinel, so memcpy writes a gpr_timespec to (*err)->arena + 255, past the end of the heap arena.
review.reasoning: get_placement() returns UINT8_MAX once the error's arena is full (it cannot grow past a uint8_t-indexable size). The pre-fix code never checks for that sentinel. It stores slot=255 and memcpy's a gpr_timespec to arena+255, which is past the allocated arena. That is the heap overflow the fix repairs by adding the check.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2017-10671): In de_dotdot(), the loop removing "/./" calls memmove(cp, cp + 2, strlen(file) - 1), sizing the copy by the whole string rather than the remainder at cp, so it reads and writes past the end of the heap buffer.

review.ground_truth: In de_dotdot(), the loop removing "/./" calls memmove(cp, cp + 2, strlen(file) - 1), sizing the copy by the whole string rather than the remainder at cp, so it reads and writes past the end of the heap buffer.
review.reasoning: In the /./ removal loop, memmove copies strlen(file)-1 bytes starting at cp+2. The correct count is based on strlen(cp). When cp lies past the start of file, the move reads and writes beyond the end of the heap buffer. The fix changes the length to strlen(cp)-1. The flaw is a wrong length computation that directly causes a heap out-of-bounds write.

description:
CWE-125: Out-of-bounds Read
This instance (CVE-2018-1000117): _is_absW() reads path[1] without first checking that path[0] is non-NUL, so an empty path string causes a read one element past its terminator.

review.ground_truth: _is_absW() reads path[1] without first checking that path[0] is non-NUL, so an empty path string causes a read one element past its terminator.
review.reasoning: The fix commit mainly addressed the wcscpy/wcscat overflows in the os.symlink helpers (_joinW/_dirnameW), which are the CVE's write overflow. But it also changed this function, which reads path[1] even when path[0] is the NUL terminator. For an empty string that reads one WCHAR past the end of the string buffer. This is a genuine but minor out-of-bounds read, distinct from the CWE-120 write overflow the label refers to.

description:
CWE-416: Use After Free
This instance (CVE-2022-3016): When an autocmd run from qf_jump_open_window() frees or changes the location list, qf_jump_newwin() still goes to theend with qi non-NULL and writes qfl->qf_ptr/qf_index into the freed qf_list_T.

review.ground_truth: When an autocmd run from qf_jump_open_window() frees or changes the location list, qf_jump_newwin() still goes to theend with qi non-NULL and writes qfl->qf_ptr/qf_index into the freed qf_list_T.
review.reasoning: In the pre-fix code, qf_jump_open_window() can run autocommands that change or free the location list. It then returns a value that this function treats like a plain NOTDONE and jumps to theend. At theend, qi is still non-NULL, so the function writes qfl->qf_ptr and qfl->qf_index into the freed list. The fix adds a QF_ABORT return that nulls qi so that write is skipped.

description:
CWE-125: Out-of-bounds Read
This instance (CVE-2018-14017): In r_bin_java_local_variable_type_table_attr_new, the loop over the file-controlled table_length reads 10 bytes per entry via R_BIN_JAVA_USHORT(buffer, offset) without checking offset against sz, causing a heap buffer over-read.

review.ground_truth: In r_bin_java_local_variable_type_table_attr_new, the loop over the file-controlled table_length reads 10 bytes per entry via R_BIN_JAVA_USHORT(buffer, offset) without checking offset against sz, causing a heap buffer over-read.
review.reasoning: The loop count table_length comes from the file, and the loop body reads ten bytes per entry through R_BIN_JAVA_USHORT. Nothing compares offset against sz, so a large table_length makes the reads run past the end of the heap buffer. The fix adds an `offset + 10 > sz` check before those reads, which confirms this. The CVE text names a different function, but this function has the same bug pattern and receives the same fix, so it is a real out-of-bounds read here too. The initial reads at offset 6 (table_length, done before the loop) are also unchecked, but they are part of the same missing-bounds flaw.

description:
CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference
This instance (CVE-2018-15862): In LookupModMask(), str returned by xkb_atom_text(ctx, field) may be NULL for an invalid atom, and it is passed to istreq() without a NULL check, causing a NULL pointer dereference.

review.ground_truth: In LookupModMask(), str returned by xkb_atom_text(ctx, field) may be NULL for an invalid atom, and it is passed to istreq() without a NULL check, causing a NULL pointer dereference.
review.reasoning: xkb_atom_text() returns NULL for an invalid or unknown atom. The before-fix code passes str straight to istreq(), which calls strcasecmp on it, so a NULL str is dereferenced. The fix adds exactly that NULL check. Seeing that the flaw is real depends on knowing that xkb_atom_text can return NULL.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2018-15834): In read_module_referenced_functions(), the file-controlled ref_function_name_length is not bounded by R_FLIRT_NAME_MAX, so the loop writing ref_function->name[j] and the terminator store at name[ref_function_name_length] overflow the heap-allocated name buffer.

review.ground_truth: In read_module_referenced_functions(), the file-controlled ref_function_name_length is not bounded by R_FLIRT_NAME_MAX, so the loop writing ref_function->name[j] and the terminator store at name[ref_function_name_length] overflow the heap-allocated name buffer.
review.reasoning: ref_function_name_length comes from the file via read_byte or read_multiple_bytes. It is only checked for being negative, never against the size of the fixed-size ref_function->name array (R_FLIRT_NAME_MAX). The loop then writes name[j] for j up to that length, and also writes name[ref_function_name_length], past the array inside the heap-allocated RFlirtFunction. The fix adds the missing upper-bound check.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2018-18957): Ethernet_getInterfaceMACAddress() uses strcpy to copy the unbounded interfaceId string into the fixed-size stack buffer buffer.ifr_name (IFNAMSIZ), causing a stack buffer overflow for long interface names.

review.ground_truth: Ethernet_getInterfaceMACAddress() uses strcpy to copy the unbounded interfaceId string into the fixed-size stack buffer buffer.ifr_name (IFNAMSIZ), causing a stack buffer overflow for long interface names.
review.reasoning: The function copies the caller-supplied interfaceId into buffer.ifr_name with strcpy. ifr_name is IFNAMSIZ (16) bytes and buffer is a stack-local struct ifreq, so a long interface name overflows the stack. The CVE names prepareGooseBuffer, but that function only passes the interface ID down into this one, and the fix limits the copy right here. The flaw is visible in this function alone, given that interfaceId is attacker-controlled.

description:
CWE-125: Out-of-bounds Read
This instance (CVE-2020-35535): parseSonySR2() reads cbuf_SR2 at tag_dataoffset + tag_dataunitlen*c via sget2()/sgetreal() for the various Sony tags without checking that the offset lies within SR2SubIFDLength, allowing an out-of-bounds read with a crafted file.

review.ground_truth: parseSonySR2() reads cbuf_SR2 at tag_dataoffset + tag_dataunitlen*c via sget2()/sgetreal() for the various Sony tags without checking that the offset lies within SR2SubIFDLength, allowing an out-of-bounds read with a crafted file.
review.reasoning: The CVE names parseSonySRF, but the same commit added buffer checks to parseSonySR2 ("parseSonySR2: buffer size check"). In the shown function, tag_dataoffset comes from the file through tiff_sget. That offset, plus tag_dataunitlen*c, is used to index cbuf_SR2 through sget2/sgetreal without any check against SR2SubIFDLength. The initial sget2(cbuf_SR2) is also unchecked. This is a genuine out-of-bounds read in this function, which the diff fixes directly.

description:
CWE-125: Out-of-bounds Read
This instance (CVE-2018-1000852): drdynvc_process_data_first() calls drdynvc_read_variable_uint() for ChannelId (cbChId) and Length (Sp) without checking Stream_GetRemainingLength(s), so a short server PDU causes a read past the end of the stream buffer.

review.ground_truth: drdynvc_process_data_first() calls drdynvc_read_variable_uint() for ChannelId (cbChId) and Length (Sp) without checking Stream_GetRemainingLength(s), so a short server PDU causes a read past the end of the stream buffer.
review.reasoning: The function reads two variable-length unsigned integers (ChannelId sized by cbChId, Length sized by Sp) from the server-supplied stream without first checking how many bytes remain. A short PDU makes drdynvc_read_variable_uint read past the end of the stream buffer. The fix adds exactly this check against Stream_GetRemainingLength. The CVE names drdynvc_process_capability_request, but the same commit fixed this sibling function in the same way, so the flaw is genuine here too.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2023-45863): fill_kobj_path() subtracts each parent's current strlen(kobject_name()) from length and then calls memcpy(path + length, ...) and writes '/' at path[--length] without checking that length stays positive, so a name lengthened by a concurrent rename after the buffer was sized causes a write before the start of the path buffer.

review.ground_truth: fill_kobj_path() subtracts each parent's current strlen(kobject_name()) from length and then calls memcpy(path + length, ...) and writes '/' at path[--length] without checking that length stays positive, so a name lengthened by a concurrent rename after the buffer was sized causes a write before the start of the path buffer.
review.reasoning: fill_kobj_path() trusts that the caller-supplied length (computed earlier by get_kobj_path_length) still matches the current kobject names. It recomputes strlen of each name and copies backward into path with no check that length stays positive. If a concurrent rename makes a name longer between the two calls, length goes negative and memcpy and the '/' store write before the start of the buffer. The fix adds exactly that bounds check inside this function, so the flaw is here.

description:
CWE-362: Concurrent Execution using Shared Resource with Improper Synchronization ('Race Condition')
This instance (CVE-2023-45145): anetUnixServer() calls anetListen() (bind+listen) before chmod(sa.sun_path, perm), leaving a window where the Unix socket is accepting connections with umask-derived permissions so unauthorized local processes can connect.

review.ground_truth: anetUnixServer() calls anetListen() (bind+listen) before chmod(sa.sun_path, perm), leaving a window where the Unix socket is accepting connections with umask-derived permissions so unauthorized local processes can connect.
review.reasoning: The function calls anetListen(), which does bind() and listen(), and only afterwards calls chmod() on the socket path. In the window between listen() and chmod(), the socket file has permissions set by the process umask, so another local user can connect. The fix passes perm into anetListen so chmod happens before listen(). This is a timing-window (TOCTOU-style) race leading to unauthorized access, and it is visible directly in this function.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2023-5717): __perf_read_group_add() iterates the child leader's sibling_list and writes values[n++] without checking that the child's sibling count matches the parent's, so a child group larger than the parent group writes past the end of the heap values buffer sized for the parent.

review.ground_truth: __perf_read_group_add() iterates the child leader's sibling_list and writes values[n++] without checking that the child's sibling count matches the parent's, so a child group larger than the parent group writes past the end of the heap values buffer sized for the parent.
review.reasoning: The values buffer is sized by the caller, perf_read_group(), from the parent leader's read_size (its sibling count). This function walks the child (inherited) leader's sibling list with for_each_sibling_event and writes values[n++] for each sibling, with no bound check. If the child group has more siblings than the parent, those writes go past the heap buffer. The fix rejects the read when nr_siblings or group_generation differ between parent and child, so the flaw is real and lives in this loop; seeing it depends on how the caller sizes the buffer.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2023-45897): The loop in read_file_dentry_set() iterates up to the on-disk file_de->file_num_ext without bounding it to MAX_NAME_DENTRIES, so memcpy into node->name + (i-2)*ENTRY_NAME_MAX writes past the end of the node->name buffer.

review.ground_truth: The loop in read_file_dentry_set() iterates up to the on-disk file_de->file_num_ext without bounding it to MAX_NAME_DENTRIES, so memcpy into node->name + (i-2)*ENTRY_NAME_MAX writes past the end of the node->name buffer.
review.reasoning: The loop bound comes from file_de->file_num_ext, which is read from disk and never checked against the capacity of node->name. A crafted image whose SecondaryCount exceeds 1 + MAX_NAME_DENTRIES therefore makes the memcpy write past the end of the node->name buffer. This is an out-of-bounds write, so the source's CWE-125 (read) label is wrong; the fix clamps the loop bound.

description:
CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference
This instance (CVE-2023-5972): nft_inner_init() calls nla_get_be32(tb[NFTA_INNER_NUM]) without first checking that tb[NFTA_INNER_NUM] is non-NULL, so a netlink request omitting that attribute causes a NULL pointer dereference.
fix_diff:
--- func_before
+++ func_after
@@ -8,6 +8,7 @@
 	int err;
 
 	if (!tb[NFTA_INNER_FLAGS] ||
+	    !tb[NFTA_INNER_NUM] ||
 	    !tb[NFTA_INNER_HDRSIZE] ||
 	    !tb[NFTA_INNER_TYPE] ||
 	    !tb[NFTA_INNER_EXPR])

review.ground_truth: nft_inner_init() calls nla_get_be32(tb[NFTA_INNER_NUM]) without first checking that tb[NFTA_INNER_NUM] is non-NULL, so a netlink request omitting that attribute causes a NULL pointer dereference.
review.reasoning: The required-attribute check covers FLAGS, HDRSIZE, TYPE and EXPR but not NFTA_INNER_NUM. The function then calls nla_get_be32(tb[NFTA_INNER_NUM]) unconditionally, so a user netlink message that omits that attribute makes the kernel dereference a NULL pointer. The fix adds the missing presence check, which matches the CWE-476 label.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2013-7459): In ALGnew(), the IVlen check is bypassed for MODE_ECB and MODE_CTR, so memcpy(new->IV, IV, IVlen) copies a user-supplied IV of arbitrary length into the BLOCK_SIZE-sized new->IV buffer, causing a heap buffer overflow.

review.ground_truth: In ALGnew(), the IVlen check is bypassed for MODE_ECB and MODE_CTR, so memcpy(new->IV, IV, IVlen) copies a user-supplied IV of arbitrary length into the BLOCK_SIZE-sized new->IV buffer, causing a heap buffer overflow.
review.reasoning: The IV length check is skipped for MODE_ECB and MODE_CTR, so any IVlen is accepted in those modes. memcpy(new->IV, IV, IVlen) then copies attacker-controlled bytes into the fixed BLOCK_SIZE array new->IV and overflows the heap object. The fix rejects a nonzero IV in ECB/CTR, which closes the overflow. The flaw is visible in this function, given that new->IV is a BLOCK_SIZE array.

description:
CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference
This instance (CVE-2017-6197): r_read_ble8() dereferences the src pointer (*(ut8 *)src) without checking for NULL, so a caller passing a NULL buffer from a crafted binary crashes.

review.ground_truth: r_read_ble8() dereferences the src pointer (*(ut8 *)src) without checking for NULL, so a caller passing a NULL buffer from a crafted binary crashes.
review.reasoning: r_read_ble8 dereferences src with no NULL check, and the fix adds one. It is part of the r_read_* family that the CVE names. Whether a NULL pointer actually arrives depends on callers passing NULL buffers from crafted binaries. Still, the function itself is the patched site of the null dereference.

description:
CWE-125: Out-of-bounds Read
This instance (CVE-2022-41877): drive_process_irp_query_directory() passes the attacker-controlled PathLength and a path pointer into irp->input to drive_file_query_directory() without checking that PathLength bytes remain in the stream, causing an out-of-bounds read.

review.ground_truth: drive_process_irp_query_directory() passes the attacker-controlled PathLength and a path pointer into irp->input to drive_file_query_directory() without checking that PathLength bytes remain in the stream, causing an out-of-bounds read.
review.reasoning: The function reads a PathLength value supplied by the server and takes path as a pointer into the input stream. It never checks that PathLength bytes actually remain in the stream. drive_file_query_directory then reads PathLength bytes from path, which can run past the end of the input buffer, and the data can be sent back to the server. The fix adds exactly this remaining-length check in this function.

description:
CWE-125: Out-of-bounds Read
This instance (CVE-2022-39319): In urb_bulk_or_interrupt_transfer(), the attacker-controlled OutputBufferSize is not checked against Stream_GetRemainingLength(s) before Stream_Pointer(s) is passed as the OUT buffer to bulk_or_interrupt_transfer, causing an out-of-bounds read.

review.ground_truth: In urb_bulk_or_interrupt_transfer(), the attacker-controlled OutputBufferSize is not checked against Stream_GetRemainingLength(s) before Stream_Pointer(s) is passed as the OUT buffer to bulk_or_interrupt_transfer, causing an out-of-bounds read.
review.reasoning: For OUT transfers, the function passes Stream_Pointer(s) together with the server-supplied OutputBufferSize to bulk_or_interrupt_transfer. It never checks that the stream actually holds OutputBufferSize bytes. The callee therefore reads past the end of the input buffer and sends that data to the USB device or back to the server. The fix adds exactly this length check.

description:
CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference
This instance (CVE-2023-23002): qca_serdev_probe() checks the devm_gpiod_get_optional() results (qcadev->bt_en, qcadev->sw_ctrl) only with !ptr, so an ERR_PTR return is accepted as a valid GPIO descriptor and later dereferenced.

review.ground_truth: qca_serdev_probe() checks the devm_gpiod_get_optional() results (qcadev->bt_en, qcadev->sw_ctrl) only with !ptr, so an ERR_PTR return is accepted as a valid GPIO descriptor and later dereferenced.
review.reasoning: devm_gpiod_get_optional() can return an ERR_PTR on failure, but qca_serdev_probe() only tests the result for NULL. An error pointer is therefore stored in qcadev->bt_en / sw_ctrl and power_ctrl_enabled stays true. Later use of that pointer (gpiod_set_value_cansleep etc. in power on/off paths) dereferences an invalid error pointer. The flaw is an improper check of the return value, visible in this function; the downstream dereference happens in other functions, so it is NULL/ERR-pointer deref class.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2022-4904): config_sortlist() memcpy's q-str bytes of the input token into the fixed stack buffers ipbuf[16] and ipbufpfx[32] without checking the length, so an overlong sortlist entry overflows the stack.

review.ground_truth: config_sortlist() memcpy's q-str bytes of the input token into the fixed stack buffers ipbuf[16] and ipbufpfx[32] without checking the length, so an overlong sortlist entry overflows the stack.
review.reasoning: The function copies q-str bytes of the attacker-controlled sortlist string into the fixed stack buffers ipbuf[16] and ipbufpfx[32] with memcpy, and never checks the length first. Any IP or prefix token longer than the buffer overflows the stack. The fix adds exactly these length checks. A later memcpy(ipbuf, str, q-str) in the mask branch is another unchecked copy, which the fix leaves alone; it is the same bug pattern rather than a separate flaw.

description:
CWE-125: Out-of-bounds Read
This instance (CVE-2023-27600): In delete_sdp_line(), end is unconditionally incremented after the scan loop even when it stopped at stream->body.s+body.len without finding '\n', so the range passed to del_lump extends one byte past the SDP body/message buffer.

review.ground_truth: In delete_sdp_line(), end is unconditionally incremented after the scan loop even when it stopped at stream->body.s+body.len without finding '\n', so the range passed to del_lump extends one byte past the SDP body/message buffer.
review.reasoning: If the SDP stream body does not end with '\n', the forward scan stops at body.s+body.len, and the unconditional end++ then pushes end one byte past the stream body. The resulting del_lump length runs beyond the body/message, which trips the lump sanity check and aborts the server. The fix only increments end when it actually points at '\n'. The root cause is an off-by-one bound that makes the deletion range exceed the buffer.

description:
CWE-401: Missing Release of Memory after Effective Lifetime (memory leak)
This instance (CVE-2023-28096): On the fail path parse_object() frees only from `child` (the last appended element) via cJSON_Delete(child) instead of from the list head item->child, leaking all previously parsed sibling items when object parsing fails.

review.ground_truth: On the fail path parse_object() frees only from `child` (the last appended element) via cJSON_Delete(child) instead of from the list head item->child, leaking all previously parsed sibling items when object parsing fails.
review.reasoning: On the failure path parse_object() calls cJSON_Delete(child). By that point child points to the last-allocated list element, not to the list head in item->child. cJSON_Delete walks forward via ->next, so every earlier sibling, along with its key and value, is never freed. The fix deletes item->child instead, which confirms this is a memory leak on malformed objects.

description:
CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference
This instance (CVE-2023-27783): dlt_jnpr_ether_cleanup() calls tcpedit_dlt_cleanup(config->subctx) without checking that subctx is non-NULL, so the assert in tcpedit_dlt_cleanup aborts (or a NULL dereference occurs) when no sub-context was created.

review.ground_truth: dlt_jnpr_ether_cleanup() calls tcpedit_dlt_cleanup(config->subctx) without checking that subctx is non-NULL, so the assert in tcpedit_dlt_cleanup aborts (or a NULL dereference occurs) when no sub-context was created.
review.reasoning: The function passes config->subctx to tcpedit_dlt_cleanup() without checking it for NULL. subctx is only allocated when a Juniper Ethernet packet is actually decoded, so it can still be NULL at cleanup time. tcpedit_dlt_cleanup() begins with assert(ctx), which aborts the process (the CWE-617 label), or dereferences NULL if asserts are compiled out. The root cause is a missing NULL check on subctx. Also, config is read from ctx->encoder->config rather than plugin->config, which is suspicious but not the flaw this fix addresses.

description:
CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference
This instance (CVE-2023-27786): In read_hexstring(), the first strtok_r(string, ",", &token) can return NULL for an empty or all-comma input, and l2byte is passed to sscanf without a NULL check.

review.ground_truth: In read_hexstring(), the first strtok_r(string, ",", &token) can return NULL for an empty or all-comma input, and l2byte is passed to sscanf without a NULL check.
review.reasoning: The CVE names macinstring, but this fix commit adds a NULL check after strtok_r in read_hexstring as well. Here, when the input string is empty or consists only of commas, strtok_r returns NULL. That NULL l2byte is then passed straight to sscanf, a NULL dereference. The flaw is genuine, is visible in this code, and the diff repairs exactly it.

description:
CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference
This instance (CVE-2023-27786): In parse_list(), the first strtok_r(ourstr, ",", &token) can return NULL (empty or all-comma input), and the result `this` is passed to regexec() without a NULL check, causing a NULL pointer dereference.

review.ground_truth: In parse_list(), the first strtok_r(ourstr, ",", &token) can return NULL (empty or all-comma input), and the result `this` is passed to regexec() without a NULL check, causing a NULL pointer dereference.
review.reasoning: parse_list passes the result of the first strtok_r() straight to regexec() without checking it. For an empty string, or one made only of commas, strtok_r returns NULL and regexec dereferences it. The fix adds a this == NULL check. The CVE names macinstring, but this commit fixes the same strtok_r NULL pattern in parse_list too, so the flaw is real in this function.

description:
CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference
This instance (CVE-2023-1390): tipc_link_xmit() calls buf_msg(skb_peek(list)) and then msg_importance(hdr)/msg_size(hdr) without first checking whether the list is empty, so an empty list (e.g. from tipc_named_node_up) causes a NULL pointer dereference.

review.ground_truth: tipc_link_xmit() calls buf_msg(skb_peek(list)) and then msg_importance(hdr)/msg_size(hdr) without first checking whether the list is empty, so an empty list (e.g. from tipc_named_node_up) causes a NULL pointer dereference.
review.reasoning: The fix adds a check for an empty list before calling buf_msg(skb_peek(list)). In the pre-fix code, skb_peek on an empty queue returns NULL, and msg_importance(hdr)/msg_size(hdr) then dereference NULL->data. The CVE text describes a hang, but the commit fixes exactly this NULL dereference. The source's CWE-1050 label is wrong; the correct class is a NULL pointer dereference (CWE-476).

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2023-1452): In gf_text_get_utf8_line() the conversion loop writes to the 2048-byte stack array szLineConv[j] without checking j against the buffer size, so long lines or high-bit-character expansion overflow the stack buffer.

review.ground_truth: In gf_text_get_utf8_line() the conversion loop writes to the 2048-byte stack array szLineConv[j] without checking j against the buffer size, so long lines or high-bit-character expansion overflow the stack buffer.
review.reasoning: szLineConv is a fixed 2048-byte stack buffer. The loop writes into it at index j, and j is never bounded. lineSize can be larger than 2048, and in Win-CP mode a single input byte can expand to two output bytes. So a long line, or one full of high-bit bytes, drives j past the end of szLineConv and causes a stack buffer overflow. The fix adds a check that stops the loop when j nears the array length.

description:
CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference
This instance (CVE-2020-23258): jsi_ArrayReduceSubCmd computes maa from fptr->argnames (0 for builtin callbacks) and may put NULL in vobjs[2], so the builtin callback gets a short or NULL-containing argument array and dereferences a NULL argument value (e.g. in Jsi_ValueIsNumber).

review.ground_truth: jsi_ArrayReduceSubCmd computes maa from fptr->argnames (0 for builtin callbacks) and may put NULL in vobjs[2], so the builtin callback gets a short or NULL-containing argument array and dereferences a NULL argument value (e.g. in Jsi_ValueIsNumber).
review.reasoning: When the reduce callback is a builtin function, fptr->argnames is NULL, so maa becomes 0. Jsi_ObjNewArray then builds an empty argument array and passes it to the builtin. The builtin (e.g. a Number/Math function) fetches its arguments and calls Jsi_ValueIsNumber on a missing (NULL) value, which crashes. The fix forces maa=4 for FC_BUILDIN callbacks and replaces the NULL placeholder in vobjs[2] with interp->NullValue, so this is a NULL dereference rather than an out-of-bounds write.

description:
CWE-125: Out-of-bounds Read
This instance (CVE-2023-2008): udmabuf_vm_fault() indexes ubuf->pages[vmf->pgoff] without checking pgoff against ubuf->pagecount, so a user-controlled mmap offset reads past the end of the pages array.

review.ground_truth: udmabuf_vm_fault() indexes ubuf->pages[vmf->pgoff] without checking pgoff against ubuf->pagecount, so a user-controlled mmap offset reads past the end of the pages array.
review.reasoning: The fault handler indexes ubuf->pages with vmf->pgoff and never checks it against ubuf->pagecount. A user can mmap the buffer with an offset or length beyond the buffer's size, so a fault reads a page pointer past the end of the array. That bogus pointer is then passed to get_page() and installed as the faulting page. The fix adds the missing bound check.

description:
CWE-125: Out-of-bounds Read
This instance (CVE-2023-31568): PdfEncryptRC4 constructor memcpy's a fixed 32 bytes from oValue.GetRawData().data() and uValue.GetRawData().data() without checking that the /O and /U strings are at least 32 bytes, causing a heap out-of-bounds read.

review.ground_truth: PdfEncryptRC4 constructor memcpy's a fixed 32 bytes from oValue.GetRawData().data() and uValue.GetRawData().data() without checking that the /O and /U strings are at least 32 bytes, causing a heap out-of-bounds read.
review.reasoning: The constructor memcpy's a fixed 32 bytes from oValue.GetRawData() and uValue.GetRawData() without checking their sizes. A short /O or /U string in the PDF encryption dictionary makes the copy read past the end of the heap buffer behind the source string. The destination m_oValue/m_uValue is 32 bytes, so nothing is written out of bounds. The root cause is an over-read (heap overflow on read), not the CWE-787 write the label claims.

description:
CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference
This instance (CVE-2022-1725): fname_match() calls vim_regexec(rmp, name, 0) without checking that rmp->regprog is non-NULL, so a NULL regexp program is dereferenced inside the regexp engine.

review.ground_truth: fname_match() calls vim_regexec(rmp, name, 0) without checking that rmp->regprog is non-NULL, so a NULL regexp program is dereferenced inside the regexp engine.
review.reasoning: fname_match() passes rmp to vim_regexec() without first checking that rmp->regprog is non-NULL. The regexp engine dereferences rmp->regprog (for example rmp->regprog->re_in_use), so a NULL program crashes. The program can already be NULL on entry, e.g. after an earlier failed match or engine switch freed it in buflist_match. The function's own later regprog != NULL check shows it knows regprog can become NULL, and the fix adds the same guard before the first call.

description:
CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference
This instance (CVE-2023-31622): In sqlc_delete_pos(), tb returned by sch_name_to_table() may be NULL for a nonexistent table, yet the else branch passes it unchecked to sqlc_make_policy_trig() (and tc_init/tb->tb_name), causing a NULL pointer dereference.

review.ground_truth: In sqlc_delete_pos(), tb returned by sch_name_to_table() may be NULL for a nonexistent table, yet the else branch passes it unchecked to sqlc_make_policy_trig() (and tc_init/tb->tb_name), causing a NULL pointer dereference.
review.reasoning: sch_name_to_table can return NULL for a nonexistent table. The else branch then continues with tb NULL and passes it to sqlc_make_policy_trig, which dereferences it. It is also dereferenced in the tb->tb_name error message and in tc_init. The fix adds a NULL check that raises an error, so the bug is a NULL dereference, not SQL injection (CWE-89).

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2023-2597): In getCachedUTFString(), strncpy copies localLen bytes into the fixed stack buffer temp (J9SH_MAXPATH + sizeof(J9UTF8)) without checking localLen against J9SH_MAXPATH, overflowing the stack buffer.

review.ground_truth: In getCachedUTFString(), strncpy copies localLen bytes into the fixed stack buffer temp (J9SH_MAXPATH + sizeof(J9UTF8)) without checking localLen against J9SH_MAXPATH, overflowing the stack buffer.
review.reasoning: The stack buffer temp holds J9SH_MAXPATH + sizeof(J9UTF8) bytes. localLen is a U_16 that can be up to 65535, and it is never checked against J9SH_MAXPATH. strncpy(tempstr, local, localLen) therefore writes past the end of the stack buffer, which is a stack overflow (out-of-bounds write) rather than the out-of-bounds read the CWE-125 label suggests. The fix adds a heap allocation for the case localLen > J9SH_MAXPATH.

description:
CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference
This instance (CVE-2023-2838): In the input-PID loop of gf_filter_get_stats(), pidi->pid is dereferenced (pidi->pid->codecid, ->stream_type, ->name) without a NULL check, even though pidi->pid can be NULL as the earlier guarded check shows.

review.ground_truth: In the input-PID loop of gf_filter_get_stats(), pidi->pid is dereferenced (pidi->pid->codecid, ->stream_type, ->name) without a NULL check, even though pidi->pid can be NULL as the earlier guarded check shows.
review.reasoning: The fix adds a check that pidi->pid is not NULL before it is dereferenced. Earlier in the loop the code already tests pidi->pid before using it, so a NULL value is clearly possible, yet the later lines read pidi->pid->codecid, stream_type and name unguarded. That is a NULL pointer dereference. The CWE-125 label describes the reported consequence rather than the root cause.

description:
CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference
This instance (CVE-2023-33461): In iniparser_getboolean() the return value c of iniparser_getstring() is checked only against INI_INVALID_KEY, not NULL, so c[0] dereferences a NULL pointer when getstring returns NULL.

review.ground_truth: In iniparser_getboolean() the return value c of iniparser_getstring() is checked only against INI_INVALID_KEY, not NULL, so c[0] dereferences a NULL pointer when getstring returns NULL.
review.reasoning: iniparser_getstring can return NULL (e.g. when d or key is NULL, or when a key is stored with a NULL value). iniparser_getboolean only compares the result against INI_INVALID_KEY and then reads c[0], which dereferences NULL. The fix adds a NULL check to this function, so the same flaw named in the CVE for getlongint is present here too.

description:
CWE-125: Out-of-bounds Read
This instance (CVE-2023-0668): dissect_PHSCALE() indexes conf_phasor_type[] directly with the attacker-controlled byte tvb_get_guint8(tvb, offset + 2) without a bounds check, reading past the end of the value_string array and using the resulting bogus strptr as a format string argument.

review.ground_truth: dissect_PHSCALE() indexes conf_phasor_type[] directly with the attacker-controlled byte tvb_get_guint8(tvb, offset + 2) without a bounds check, reading past the end of the value_string array and using the resulting bogus strptr as a format string argument.
review.reasoning: The function takes a byte from the packet (tvb_get_guint8 at offset+2) and uses it directly as an index into the conf_phasor_type value_string array. That array covers only a few values, so any of 0-255 can be used. The ->strptr read past the array's end is an out-of-bounds read, and the bogus pointer is then dereferenced as a %s format argument. The fix replaces the direct indexing with val_to_str_const. The source label says CWE-787, but the root cause is an out-of-bounds read, not a write.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2023-34095): cpdbCreateBackendFromFile() reads the backend info file with fscanf(file, "%s", obj_path) and no width limit, so a token longer than 1023 characters overflows the 1024-byte stack buffer obj_path.

review.ground_truth: cpdbCreateBackendFromFile() reads the backend info file with fscanf(file, "%s", obj_path) and no width limit, so a token longer than 1023 characters overflows the 1024-byte stack buffer obj_path.
review.reasoning: The function calls fscanf(file, "%s", obj_path), where obj_path is a fixed stack buffer of CPDB_BSIZE (1024) bytes. The format has no width limit, so a token longer than 1023 characters in the backend info file overflows the stack buffer. The fix adds a %1023s width limit, which matches the source's CWE-121 stack overflow label. Separately, backend_name leaks on the error paths, but that is not the flaw the fix addresses.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2023-35788): fl_set_geneve_opt() computes opt = &key->enc_opts.data[key->enc_opts.len] and writes the geneve_opt header (memset, opt->length, opt->r1..r3) without first checking that enc_opts.len leaves room within FLOW_DIS_TUN_OPTS_MAX, so accumulated options (e.g. len=252) cause an out-of-bounds write.

review.ground_truth: fl_set_geneve_opt() computes opt = &key->enc_opts.data[key->enc_opts.len] and writes the geneve_opt header (memset, opt->length, opt->r1..r3) without first checking that enc_opts.len leaves room within FLOW_DIS_TUN_OPTS_MAX, so accumulated options (e.g. len=252) cause an out-of-bounds write.
review.reasoning: The function builds opt as a pointer to key->enc_opts.data[key->enc_opts.len] without checking that len leaves room for a 4-byte geneve_opt header. When len is 252 the header falls past the 256-byte buffer, and the following writes (memset, opt->length, opt->r1-r3) go out of bounds. The later new_len check only runs when DATA is present, and it comes after those writes. The fix adds a len > MAX-4 check before computing opt, so this is a genuine out-of-bounds write in this function.

description:
CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference
This instance (CVE-2019-18680): In rds_tcp_kill_sock(), the second loop over tmp_list dereferences tc->t_sock->sk without checking that tc->t_sock is non-NULL, even though connections with a NULL t_sock are moved onto the list.

review.ground_truth: In rds_tcp_kill_sock(), the second loop over tmp_list dereferences tc->t_sock->sk without checking that tc->t_sock is non-NULL, even though connections with a NULL t_sock are moved onto the list.
review.reasoning: The first loop moves every connection belonging to the dying netns onto tmp_list, and it does not filter on whether t_sock is set. The second loop then reads tc->t_sock->sk unconditionally, so a connection with t_sock == NULL causes a NULL dereference. The fix wraps the socket teardown in an if (tc->t_sock) check. The flaw is visible in this function alone.

description:
CWE-401: Missing Release of Memory after Effective Lifetime (memory leak)
This instance (CVE-2011-1488): In processBatchMultiRuleset(), snglRuleBatch is allocated by batchInit() but the loop only exits via FINALIZE to finalize_it, skipping batchFree(&snglRuleBatch), so the batch's memory is leaked on every call.

review.ground_truth: In processBatchMultiRuleset(), snglRuleBatch is allocated by batchInit() but the loop only exits via FINALIZE to finalize_it, skipping batchFree(&snglRuleBatch), so the batch's memory is leaked on every call.
review.reasoning: The function allocates snglRuleBatch with batchInit(). The only way out of the while(1) loop is FINALIZE, which jumps to finalize_it, so batchFree(&snglRuleBatch) is unreachable dead code. Every call therefore leaks the temporary batch's element array. The fix moves batchInit and batchFree inside the loop and exits with break. The CVE text mentions $RepeatedMsgReduction, which may be loosely mapped, but the leak shown here is genuine.

description:
CWE-125: Out-of-bounds Read
This instance (CVE-2017-9740): In the cmap format 4 case, the pointers idRangeOffset (derived from untrusted segCount2) and idRangeOffset + i2 + roff + ((i - start) << 1) are dereferenced via u16() without checking them against font->data + font->length, causing a heap buffer over-read.

review.ground_truth: In the cmap format 4 case, the pointers idRangeOffset (derived from untrusted segCount2) and idRangeOffset + i2 + roff + ((i - start) << 1) are dereferenced via u16() without checking them against font->data + font->length, causing a heap buffer over-read.
review.reasoning: In the format-4 branch, segCount2 and roff come from the font file and are used to compute the idRangeOffset/idDelta/startCount pointers and the glyph-index address. Neither is checked against font->data + font->length before u16() reads from them, so a crafted cmap causes a heap over-read. The fix adds exactly these bounds checks. Other branches (formats 6, 10 and 12) also read table entries without bounds checks, which is a further evident OOB read.

description:
CWE-125: Out-of-bounds Read
This instance (CVE-2017-3735): X509v3_addr_get_afi() reads f->addressFamily->data[1] without checking that f->addressFamily->length is at least 2, causing a one-byte out-of-bounds read for short addressFamily octet strings.

review.ground_truth: X509v3_addr_get_afi() reads f->addressFamily->data[1] without checking that f->addressFamily->length is at least 2, causing a one-byte out-of-bounds read for short addressFamily octet strings.
review.reasoning: The function reads data[0] and data[1] of the addressFamily ASN1_OCTET_STRING without checking that length >= 2. A one-byte octet string therefore leads to an out-of-bounds read of data[1]. The fix adds the length < 2 check. This is the CVE flaw itself.

description:
CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference
This instance (CVE-2021-28236): In dxfb_tables_write(), ctrl returned by dwg_get_first_object() (possibly NULL) and its ctrl->tio.object are dereferenced to initialize _ctrl (e.g. ctrl->tio.object->tio.VPORT_CONTROL) before the 'if (ctrl && ...)' NULL check, causing a NULL pointer dereference on crafted DWG files lacking a table control object.

review.ground_truth: In dxfb_tables_write(), ctrl returned by dwg_get_first_object() (possibly NULL) and its ctrl->tio.object are dereferenced to initialize _ctrl (e.g. ctrl->tio.object->tio.VPORT_CONTROL) before the 'if (ctrl && ...)' NULL check, causing a NULL pointer dereference on crafted DWG files lacking a table control object.
review.reasoning: Each table block calls dwg_get_first_object(), which can return NULL. The code then dereferences ctrl->tio.object->tio.XXX_CONTROL before the 'if (ctrl && ...)' NULL check runs, so the check comes too late. It also never checks tio.object for NULL. The fix moves the _ctrl assignment inside the guard and adds the missing checks. The flaw is clearly visible in this function and matches the CWE-476 label.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2021-41499): Server_message() calls vsprintf into the fixed 256-byte stack array buffer with no length limit, so overlong formatted arguments (e.g. a long audio file name) overflow the stack buffer.

review.ground_truth: Server_message() calls vsprintf into the fixed 256-byte stack array buffer with no length limit, so overlong formatted arguments (e.g. a long audio file name) overflow the stack buffer.
review.reasoning: Server_message formats caller-supplied varargs into a fixed 256-byte stack buffer with an unbounded vsprintf. The CVE names Server_debug, but the same commit fixed every logging function, and Server_message shows the identical pattern. Any message longer than 255 bytes, such as one containing a long file name, overflows the stack buffer.

description:
CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference
This instance (CVE-2021-44925): DumpLSRAddReplaceInsert() passes com->node to gf_svg_get_attribute_name() without checking it for NULL, so a LASeR command with no target node causes a NULL pointer dereference.

review.ground_truth: DumpLSRAddReplaceInsert() passes com->node to gf_svg_get_attribute_name() without checking it for NULL, so a LASeR command with no target node causes a NULL pointer dereference.
review.reasoning: The fix adds a NULL check on com->node before calling gf_svg_get_attribute_name, which dereferences the node to read its tag.
