A LASeR command parsed from a malformed stream can have a NULL target node. In that case the dumper passes NULL straight into the call and crashes, which matches the CVE. The flaw is in the caller passing an unchecked pointer, and the shown function contains it.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2021-45258): SFS_GetString() passes the fixed 1000-byte stack buffer name to gf_bifs_dec_name() with no length limit, so an overlong name from the bitstream overflows the stack buffer.

review.ground_truth: SFS_GetString() passes the fixed 1000-byte stack buffer name to gf_bifs_dec_name() with no length limit, so an overlong name from the bitstream overflows the stack buffer.
review.reasoning: gf_bifs_dec_name copies bytes from the bitstream into the buffer until it reads a NUL terminator, and it is given no size limit. SFS_GetString passes a 1000-byte stack buffer, so a long name in the stream writes past the end of name. The fix adds a size argument (1000) at this call site. The CVE text names gf_bifs_dec_proto_list, but the same stack overflow pattern applies here and this call site was changed by the fix.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2021-45258): gf_bifs_dec_name() writes bitstream bytes into name[i] until a NUL byte with no bound on i, overflowing the caller's fixed-size (stack) name buffer.

review.ground_truth: gf_bifs_dec_name() writes bitstream bytes into name[i] until a NUL byte with no bound on i, overflowing the caller's fixed-size (stack) name buffer.
review.reasoning: gf_bifs_dec_name copies bytes read from the bitstream into the caller's buffer until it reads a NUL byte, with no bound on the index. Callers such as gf_bifs_dec_proto_list pass fixed-size stack buffers, so an overlong name in the stream writes past the end of the stack buffer. The fix adds a size parameter and truncates the name, which confirms this is the flaw.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2021-45258): gf_bifs_dec_route() passes the 1000-byte stack buffer `name` to gf_bifs_dec_name() without a size limit, so an over-long DEF'ed route name in the bitstream overflows the stack buffer.

review.ground_truth: gf_bifs_dec_route() passes the 1000-byte stack buffer `name` to gf_bifs_dec_name() without a size limit, so an over-long DEF'ed route name in the bitstream overflows the stack buffer.
review.reasoning: The fix changes gf_bifs_dec_name to take a buffer size, because it copied bitstream bytes into the destination until a NUL terminator with no bound. This function passes its 1000-byte stack buffer `name` to that unbounded decoder, so a long route name in the bitstream overflows the stack. The CVE names gf_bifs_dec_proto_list, but the same pattern is present here and is fixed by the same commit.

description:
CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference
This instance (CVE-2021-45266): In lsr_translate_anim_trans_values(), for the rotate transform with coded_type 8, f = gf_list_get(l, 0) can return NULL when the decoded value list is empty, and it is dereferenced unchecked in p->angle = *f.

review.ground_truth: In lsr_translate_anim_trans_values(), for the rotate transform with coded_type 8, f = gf_list_get(l, 0) can return NULL when the decoded value list is empty, and it is dereferenced unchecked in p->angle = *f.
review.reasoning: The fix adds a NULL check on f = gf_list_get(l, 0) before dereferencing it to set p->angle. An empty list decoded from the bitstream for a rotate value makes gf_list_get return NULL, which is then dereferenced. The CVE names lsr_read_anim_values_ex, but the fix is in this function, which is called on those values, and the NULL dereference is plainly visible here.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2021-40574): In gf_text_process_sub(), the loop copying characters from szLine after '{' into the 20-byte stack buffer szTime has no length bound, so a long start-time field in a SUB line overflows szTime.

review.ground_truth: In gf_text_process_sub(), the loop copying characters from szLine after '{' into the 20-byte stack buffer szTime has no length bound, so a long start-time field in a SUB line overflows szTime.
review.reasoning: The diff adds a bound check (i>=19) on the copy into szTime[20] in gf_text_process_sub. Without it, a long run of characters between braces in a line (up to 2048 bytes) overflows the 20-byte stack buffer szTime. The CVE's double-free description is a consequence label; the actual fixed root cause is a stack buffer overflow. The second copy loop into szTime (end time) is equally unbounded, and the szText copy relies on j staying within len.

description:
CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference
This instance (CVE-2022-0240): prepare_singleton_class() dereferences o->c (o->c->tt) without checking that o->c is non-NULL, crashing when called on an object whose class pointer is NULL.

review.ground_truth: prepare_singleton_class() dereferences o->c (o->c->tt) without checking that o->c is non-NULL, crashing when called on an object whose class pointer is NULL.
review.reasoning: The fix adds checks for obj->c in callers (e.g., mrb_singleton_class_ptr) and only an mrb_assert in this function. The NULL deref itself happens here, at o->c->tt, when o->c is NULL (such as for hidden objects whose class pointer is NULL). The function has no check of its own, so this is a genuine null deref at this site, though the root fix lives in the callers. Within this function the only change is an assert, so this is borderline, but the dereference site is here.

description:
CWE-125: Out-of-bounds Read
This instance (CVE-2020-19861): In ldns_nsec3_salt_data(), salt_length is read from ldns_rdf_data(salt_rdf)[0] and used in memcpy from &ldns_rdf_data(salt_rdf)[1] without checking salt_length+1 <= ldns_rdf_size(salt_rdf), causing a heap out-of-bounds read.

review.ground_truth: In ldns_nsec3_salt_data(), salt_length is read from ldns_rdf_data(salt_rdf)[0] and used in memcpy from &ldns_rdf_data(salt_rdf)[1] without checking salt_length+1 <= ldns_rdf_size(salt_rdf), causing a heap out-of-bounds read.
review.reasoning: The salt length is taken from the first byte of the rdf data. The memcpy then copies salt_length bytes starting at offset 1, but nothing checks that salt_length+1 fits within ldns_rdf_size(salt_rdf). An rdf whose size is smaller than its embedded length byte therefore causes a heap over-read. The fix adds exactly this bounds check.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2021-46238): In gf_dump_vrml_route(), node names returned by gf_node_get_name_and_id()/gf_node_get_name() are strcpy'd into the fixed 512-byte stack buffers fromNode/toNode without any length check, causing a stack buffer overflow for long DEF names.

review.ground_truth: In gf_dump_vrml_route(), node names returned by gf_node_get_name_and_id()/gf_node_get_name() are strcpy'd into the fixed 512-byte stack buffers fromNode/toNode without any length check, causing a stack buffer overflow for long DEF names.
review.reasoning: The function copies node names with strcpy into the fixed 512-byte stack buffers fromNode and toNode. Those names come from the input file and have no length limit, so a long DEF name overflows the stack. The fix stops copying and points directly at the name strings instead. The CVE text names gf_node_get_name, but the overflow it describes is this stack buffer overflow on the name it returns.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2022-0359): In init_ccline(), Ex mode allocates cmdbuff with a fixed 250 bytes regardless of indent, so vim_memset(ccline.cmdbuff, ' ', indent) and ccline.cmdbuff[indent] = NUL overflow the heap buffer when indent is large (e.g. a large 'tabstop').

review.ground_truth: In init_ccline(), Ex mode allocates cmdbuff with a fixed 250 bytes regardless of indent, so vim_memset(ccline.cmdbuff, ' ', indent) and ccline.cmdbuff[indent] = NUL overflow the heap buffer when indent is large (e.g. a large 'tabstop').
review.reasoning: In Ex mode the command buffer is always allocated at 250 bytes, whatever the indent is. When firstc <= 0, vim_memset writes indent spaces and then a NUL at cmdbuff[indent]. A large 'tabstop' gives a large indent, so these writes run past the 250-byte heap buffer. The fix sizes the allocation from indent (indent + 50).

description:
CWE-125: Out-of-bounds Read
This instance (CVE-2022-21722): parse_rtcp_report() casts pkt+sizeof(pjmedia_rtcp_common) to sr (for RTCP_SR) or rr (for RTCP_RR) and reads their fields without verifying that size is at least sizeof(common)+sizeof(sr/rr), so a truncated RTCP packet causes an out-of-bounds read.

review.ground_truth: parse_rtcp_report() casts pkt+sizeof(pjmedia_rtcp_common) to sr (for RTCP_SR) or rr (for RTCP_RR) and reads their fields without verifying that size is at least sizeof(common)+sizeof(sr/rr), so a truncated RTCP packet causes an out-of-bounds read.
review.reasoning: For an RTCP_SR packet, the function sets sr to pkt + sizeof(common) and then reads sr->ntp_sec and sr->ntp_frac without checking that size covers common + sr. For an RTCP_RR packet, it sets rr and reads rr->total_lost_*, jitter, lsr and dlsr without checking that size covers common + rr. A truncated incoming RTCP packet therefore causes reads past the buffer. The fix adds exactly these two size checks, so the flaw is present in the code as shown.

description:
CWE-125: Out-of-bounds Read
This instance (CVE-2015-7673): parse_rle_data_pseudocolor() indexes ctx->cmap->cols[*s] with an attacker-controlled pixel byte without checking it against the colormap size, reading past the heap-allocated colormap in both the RLE and raw packet paths.

review.ground_truth: parse_rle_data_pseudocolor() indexes ctx->cmap->cols[*s] with an attacker-controlled pixel byte without checking it against the colormap size, reading past the heap-allocated colormap in both the RLE and raw packet paths.
review.reasoning: The fix routes colormap lookups through colormap_get_color(), which checks the index against the colormap's real number of colors. In the original code, the pixel byte *s from the file is used directly as an index into ctx->cmap->cols[]. That array is allocated with the colormap size given in the TGA header, which can be smaller than 256 entries, so this is an out-of-bounds heap read. The CVE text instead describes using memory after a failed allocation, which happens elsewhere. Still, this function does contain a real out-of-bounds read that the change repairs.

description:
CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference
This instance (CVE-2006-7203): In compat_sys_mount(), data_page can be NULL (0) when no mount data is supplied, yet it is passed unchecked to do_smb_super_data_conv/do_ncp_super_data_conv/do_nfs4_super_data_conv, which dereference it.

review.ground_truth: In compat_sys_mount(), data_page can be NULL (0) when no mount data is supplied, yet it is passed unchecked to do_smb_super_data_conv/do_ncp_super_data_conv/do_nfs4_super_data_conv, which dereference it.
review.reasoning: copy_mount_options sets data_page to 0 when the user passes a NULL data pointer. The function then passes data_page unchecked to do_smb_super_data_conv, do_ncp_super_data_conv or do_nfs4_super_data_conv, which dereference it. The fix adds a data_page check before these calls. This is a genuine NULL pointer dereference, triggerable by a local user via a 32-bit compat mount.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2008-1514): In __poke_user_compat(), an addr in the padding between regs.orig_gpr2 and regs.fp_regs reaches the fp_regs branch, where offset = addr - &dummy32->regs.fp_regs underflows and the write *(__u32 *)(&child->thread.fp_regs + offset) = tmp goes out of bounds.

review.ground_truth: In __poke_user_compat(), an addr in the padding between regs.orig_gpr2 and regs.fp_regs reaches the fp_regs branch, where offset = addr - &dummy32->regs.fp_regs underflows and the write *(__u32 *)(&child->thread.fp_regs + offset) = tmp goes out of bounds.
review.reasoning: In the pre-fix code, an addr inside the padding hole between orig_gpr2 and fp_regs in struct user32 falls into the fp_regs branch. There offset = addr - &fp_regs underflows to a huge value, and the 32-bit write to child->thread.fp_regs + offset lands far outside the structure, causing the kernel panic. The fix adds an early return for that range, so the flaw is real and is in this function. The root cause is a missing lower-bound check that lets the write go out of bounds; the CWE-399 label is generic.

description:
CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference
This instance (CVE-2019-12108): In GetOutboundPinholeTimeout(), the argument check tests ext_port instead of rem_port, so a request missing RemotePort leaves rem_port NULL and it is dereferenced by atoi(rem_port).

review.ground_truth: In GetOutboundPinholeTimeout(), the argument check tests ext_port instead of rem_port, so a request missing RemotePort leaves rem_port NULL and it is dereferenced by atoi(rem_port).
review.reasoning: The validation checks ext_port, which is not a local variable here, instead of rem_port. rem_port can therefore be NULL when it is passed to atoi(rem_port), which is a NULL pointer dereference. The code as shown would not compile with ext_port undeclared, but it is the pre-fix state and the bug is clearly the missing NULL check on rem_port before atoi. The CVE text says int_port, but in the code int_port is checked; rem_port is the one left unchecked.

description:
CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference
This instance (CVE-2008-2812): x25_asy_timeout() calls the optional tty operation sl->tty->driver->chars_in_buffer without checking it is non-NULL, causing a NULL function pointer call for tty drivers that do not implement it.

review.ground_truth: x25_asy_timeout() calls the optional tty operation sl->tty->driver->chars_in_buffer without checking it is non-NULL, causing a NULL function pointer call for tty drivers that do not implement it.
review.reasoning: The function calls sl->tty->driver->chars_in_buffer(sl->tty) without checking whether the tty driver implements that optional operation. If it does not, the kernel calls a NULL function pointer. The fix adds a NULL check before the call, so the bug matches the CVE.

description:
CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference
This instance (CVE-2008-2812): set_baud() invokes the optional tty->driver->set_termios function pointer without checking it for NULL, so a tty driver lacking set_termios causes a NULL function pointer call.

review.ground_truth: set_baud() invokes the optional tty->driver->set_termios function pointer without checking it for NULL, so a tty driver lacking set_termios causes a NULL function pointer call.
review.reasoning: set_baud() in drivers/net/wireless/strip.c calls tty->driver->set_termios without checking that the pointer is set. Some tty drivers do not implement set_termios, so the optional function pointer can be NULL. That makes this a call through a NULL pointer and a crash. The fix adds exactly that check, which matches the CVE description.

description:
CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference
This instance (CVE-2008-2812): ax_xmit() calls ax->tty->driver->chars_in_buffer(ax->tty) on transmit timeout without checking whether the optional chars_in_buffer function pointer is NULL.

review.ground_truth: ax_xmit() calls ax->tty->driver->chars_in_buffer(ax->tty) on transmit timeout without checking whether the optional chars_in_buffer function pointer is NULL.
review.reasoning: The optional tty driver op chars_in_buffer is called without first checking that it is non-NULL. Some tty drivers leave this pointer NULL, so a transmit timeout ends up calling through a NULL function pointer. The fix adds exactly this NULL check before the call in ax_xmit. Seeing this needs the assumption that the op is optional, which is well known for tty drivers.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2008-5025): hfs_cat_find_brec() copies rec.thread.CName.len bytes from the on-disk thread record into fd->search_key->cat.CName.name via memcpy without checking that len <= HFS_NAMELEN, overflowing the name buffer.

review.ground_truth: hfs_cat_find_brec() copies rec.thread.CName.len bytes from the on-disk thread record into fd->search_key->cat.CName.name via memcpy without checking that len <= HFS_NAMELEN, overflowing the name buffer.
review.reasoning: The length field rec.thread.CName.len comes from the on-disk thread record and can be up to 255. It is copied into fd->search_key->cat.CName.name, which is HFS_NAMELEN (31) bytes, with no bounds check. The memcpy therefore writes past the destination array, and it also reads past rec.thread.CName.name on the stack. The fix adds a len > HFS_NAMELEN check, so the flaw is real and lives in this function.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2009-0269): In ecryptfs_follow_link() the readlink return value rc is used as an index in buf[rc] = '\0' before checking rc < 0, so an error return writes outside the kmalloc'd buffer.

review.ground_truth: In ecryptfs_follow_link() the readlink return value rc is used as an index in buf[rc] = '\0' before checking rc < 0, so an error return writes outside the kmalloc'd buffer.
review.reasoning: buf[rc] = '\0' runs before the check for a negative readlink return. On error, rc is a negative errno, so the store lands before the start of the heap buffer. There is a second problem: if readlink returns len (PAGE_SIZE), buf[PAGE_SIZE] is one byte past the end. That is the same line, so it is the same flaw rather than a separate one.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2009-0322): read_rbu_packet_size() uses sprintf() into buffer ignoring count, so a zero-byte (or short) read writes and returns more bytes than requested, causing an oops.

review.ground_truth: read_rbu_packet_size() uses sprintf() into buffer ignoring count, so a zero-byte (or short) read writes and returns more bytes than requested, causing an oops.
review.reasoning: The function sprintf()s the packet size into buffer without honoring count. When count is 0, the sysfs bin read path then gets a return value larger than requested. That is a write past the permitted buffer length, and the copy logic oopses. The fix uses scnprintf(buffer, count, ...), which bounds the output and returns 0 for a zero count.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2009-1439): In CIFSTCon(), tcon->nativeFileSystem is allocated with kzalloc(length + 2), where length is a UTF-16 character count, and cifs_strfromUCS_le() then writes the converted string into it, overflowing the heap buffer when a server sends a long nativeFileSystem field.

review.ground_truth: In CIFSTCon(), tcon->nativeFileSystem is allocated with kzalloc(length + 2), where length is a UTF-16 character count, and cifs_strfromUCS_le() then writes the converted string into it, overflowing the heap buffer when a server sends a long nativeFileSystem field.
review.reasoning: In the Unicode branch, tcon->nativeFileSystem is allocated with only length + 2 bytes, where length is the count of UTF-16 characters. cifs_strfromUCS_le() then converts those length characters into the local codepage, and a multibyte codepage can emit several bytes per character. The converted string can therefore exceed the allocation and overflow the heap buffer. The fix enlarges the allocation to 2*(length+1).

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2009-1633): decode_unicode_ssetup allocates ses->serverDomain with only 2*(len+1) bytes, but cifs_strfromUCS_le can emit up to 4 bytes per Unicode character, so a malicious server's domain string overflows the heap buffer (worsened by the unconditional data++ misalignment of the string area).

review.ground_truth: decode_unicode_ssetup allocates ses->serverDomain with only 2*(len+1) bytes, but cifs_strfromUCS_le can emit up to 4 bytes per Unicode character, so a malicious server's domain string overflows the heap buffer (worsened by the unconditional data++ misalignment of the string area).
review.reasoning: The serverDomain buffer is allocated as 2*(len+1) bytes. cifs_strfromUCS_le can then write up to 4 bytes per UCS-2 character, in UTF-8 or another multi-byte nls charset, so a malicious server's domain string can overflow the heap allocation. The unconditional data++ misalignment makes such multi-byte characters more likely, but the root cause is the undersized destination buffer. The fix resizes it to 4*len+2 bytes, the same sizing already used for serverOS and serverNOS.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2009-2406): parse_tag_11_packet() memcpy()s *tag_11_contents_size (body_size - 14, from the attacker-controlled packet length) bytes into contents without checking it against max_contents_bytes, overflowing the caller's key signature buffer.

review.ground_truth: parse_tag_11_packet() memcpy()s *tag_11_contents_size (body_size - 14, from the attacker-controlled packet length) bytes into contents without checking it against max_contents_bytes, overflowing the caller's key signature buffer.
review.reasoning: The function copies body_size-14 bytes, a length taken from the file, into contents with memcpy. It never compares that length against max_contents_bytes. The caller passes a fixed-size stack key signature buffer, so a crafted Tag 11 packet overflows the stack. The fix adds exactly this bounds check.

description:
CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference
This instance (CVE-2009-2908): ecryptfs_unlink() calls vfs_unlink() on lower_dentry without taking a reference via dget(), so d_delete() turns the lower dentry negative (d_inode = NULL) while open files still use it, leading to a NULL d_inode dereference in later read/write/getxattr paths.

review.ground_truth: ecryptfs_unlink() calls vfs_unlink() on lower_dentry without taking a reference via dget(), so d_delete() turns the lower dentry negative (d_inode = NULL) while open files still use it, leading to a NULL d_inode dereference in later read/write/getxattr paths.
review.reasoning: ecryptfs_unlink() calls vfs_unlink() on the lower dentry without first taking a reference on it. When the lower dentry's d_count is 1, d_delete() turns it into a negative dentry, so its d_inode becomes NULL. Later read/write paths (ecryptfs_read_update_atime, ecryptfs_getxattr) still hold that lower dentry through an open file and dereference its NULL d_inode. The fix adds dget()/dput() around the unlink so the dentry is not made negative. The root cause is a missing reference that leads to a NULL dereference elsewhere.

description:
CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference
This instance (CVE-2009-3726): nfs4_proc_lock() passes ctx->state to nfs4_proc_getlk/nfs4_proc_unlck/nfs4_proc_setlk without checking it for NULL, so a file opened without NFSv4 state causes a NULL pointer dereference.

review.ground_truth: nfs4_proc_lock() passes ctx->state to nfs4_proc_getlk/nfs4_proc_unlck/nfs4_proc_setlk without checking it for NULL, so a file opened without NFSv4 state causes a NULL pointer dereference.
review.reasoning: The function takes ctx->state, which can be NULL when a buggy server's wrong attributes cause a fallback lookup and the file ends up opened without NFSv4 state. That pointer is passed unchecked to nfs4_proc_getlk, nfs4_proc_unlck and nfs4_proc_setlk, which dereference it. The fix adds NULL checks on state before each of those calls. The root cause (state can be NULL) lives in nfs_atomic_lookup, but the dereference this CVE names is here.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2009-4004): kvm_vcpu_ioctl_x86_setup_mce() takes bank_num from user-supplied mcg_cap (up to 255) without bounding it to KVM_MAX_MCE_BANKS, so the loop writing vcpu->arch.mce_banks[bank*4] writes past the end of the allocated bank array.

review.ground_truth: kvm_vcpu_ioctl_x86_setup_mce() takes bank_num from user-supplied mcg_cap (up to 255) without bounding it to KVM_MAX_MCE_BANKS, so the loop writing vcpu->arch.mce_banks[bank*4] writes past the end of the allocated bank array.
review.reasoning: bank_num comes from user-controlled mcg_cap & 0xff and can be as large as 255. The mce_banks array is allocated for only KVM_MAX_MCE_BANKS (32) banks of 4 u64 each. The loop writes mce_banks[bank*4] for every bank below bank_num, so a large count writes past the allocation. The fix adds an upper bound check on bank_num.

description:
CWE-125: Out-of-bounds Read
This instance (CVE-2009-3080): gdth_read_event() only checks eindex >= MAX_EVENTS, so a negative user-supplied handle indexes ebuffer[eindex] before the start of the array and its contents are memcpy'd out.

review.ground_truth: gdth_read_event() only checks eindex >= MAX_EVENTS, so a negative user-supplied handle indexes ebuffer[eindex] before the start of the array and its contents are memcpy'd out.
review.reasoning: The handle comes from user IOCTL as a signed int. The only check is eindex >= MAX_EVENTS, so a negative handle other than -1 passes and indexes ebuffer[eindex] before the array. That element is then memcpy'd to estr and returned to the user, which is an out-of-bounds read. The fix adds an eindex < 0 check.

description:
CWE-125: Out-of-bounds Read
This instance (CVE-2023-40083): In StartAdvertisingSet() the GAP-data parsing loops take `len` from the advertise, scan-response and periodic data and copy `[begin, begin+len+1)` into a new vector without checking that `offset+len+1` fits within the source vector, so a malformed length reads beyond the buffer.

review.ground_truth: In StartAdvertisingSet() the GAP-data parsing loops take `len` from the advertise, scan-response and periodic data and copy `[begin, begin+len+1)` into a new vector without checking that `offset+len+1` fits within the source vector, so a malformed length reads beyond the buffer.
review.reasoning: The fix commit itself is only a refactor that moves these loops into parse_gap_data(). The CVE's missing bounds check is in that same loop logic, though, and the logic is present inline here. In each of the three loops, `len` is read from the data and `end = begin + len + 1` is never checked against the vector's end. Constructing `std::vector(begin, end)` then reads past the end of `advertise_data`, `scan_response_data` or `periodic_data` whenever the declared length exceeds the remaining bytes.

description:
CWE-125: Out-of-bounds Read
This instance (CVE-2023-40083): In StartAdvertising, the loops over advertise_data and scan_response_data compute end = begin + len + 1 from an untrusted length byte without checking it against the vector size, so constructing data_copy reads past the end of the buffer.

review.ground_truth: In StartAdvertising, the loops over advertise_data and scan_response_data compute end = begin + len + 1 from an untrusted length byte without checking it against the vector size, so constructing data_copy reads past the end of the buffer.
review.reasoning: The function reads a length byte at advertise_data[offset] and builds a vector copy from begin to begin+len+1 without checking that offset+len+1 <= advertise_data.size(). A crafted length makes the range constructor read past the end of the vector. The commit only moves this loop into parse_gap_data, but the CVE describes this same missing bounds check, and it is present in the inlined loops shown here.

description:
CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference
This instance (CVE-2022-25892): In PDFParser::ParseLastXrefPosition(), anObject returned by mObjectParser.ParseNewObject() is dereferenced via anObject->GetType() without checking for NULL, so a crafted PDF trailer that yields no object crashes the parser.

review.ground_truth: In PDFParser::ParseLastXrefPosition(), anObject returned by mObjectParser.ParseNewObject() is dereferenced via anObject->GetType() without checking for NULL, so a crafted PDF trailer that yields no object crashes the parser.
review.reasoning: ParseNewObject() returns NULL when it cannot parse an object, for example on a crafted or truncated trailer. The pre-fix code calls anObject->GetType() right away with no NULL check, so a malicious PDF crashes the parser, which is the reported DoS. The fix adds the missing NULL check.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2023-6377): RecalculateMasterButtons() increases master->button->numButtons to maxbuttons without reallocating master->button->xkb_acts, so later XKB accesses indexed by numButtons go past the undersized xkb_acts array.

review.ground_truth: RecalculateMasterButtons() increases master->button->numButtons to maxbuttons without reallocating master->button->xkb_acts, so later XKB accesses indexed by numButtons go past the undersized xkb_acts array.
review.reasoning: RecalculateMasterButtons() can raise master->button->numButtons to maxbuttons without growing master->button->xkb_acts. Because that array keeps its old, smaller size, later XKB code that indexes it by numButtons (for example the memcpy in XkbSetDeviceInfo, or XkbGetDeviceInfo queries) reads and writes out of bounds. The fix reallocates xkb_acts inside this function, so the flaw is real here. The root cause is a buffer left out of sync with the size field, and the resulting access is both a read and a write. The CVE describes both, and the commit stresses the write, so CWE-787 fits better than the CWE-125 label.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2023-42799): parseUrlAddrFromRtspUrlString() uses strcpy(destination, rtspUrlScratchBuffer + prefixLen) to copy the attacker-controlled host portion of the RTSP URL into a fixed-size destination buffer without any length check, causing a buffer overflow.

review.ground_truth: parseUrlAddrFromRtspUrlString() uses strcpy(destination, rtspUrlScratchBuffer + prefixLen) to copy the attacker-controlled host portion of the RTSP URL into a fixed-size destination buffer without any length check, causing a buffer overflow.
review.reasoning: The function strcpy()s the host portion of a server-supplied RTSP URL into the caller's fixed-size destination without knowing its size. A long host string from a malicious server overflows the buffer. The fix adds a destinationLength parameter and switches to a bounded copy. The destination size lives in the caller, but the unbounded strcpy of attacker-controlled data is evident from this function alone.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2023-42801): extractVersionQuadFromString() copies the server-controlled input string into the fixed 128-byte stack buffer versionString with an unbounded strcpy, so input of 128 bytes or more overflows the stack buffer.

review.ground_truth: extractVersionQuadFromString() copies the server-controlled input string into the fixed 128-byte stack buffer versionString with an unbounded strcpy, so input of 128 bytes or more overflows the stack buffer.
review.reasoning: The function does strcpy(versionString, string) into a 128-byte stack buffer with no length check. The string is a server-supplied version string, so a malicious host can overflow the stack buffer. The fix removes the copy entirely, which confirms this is the flaw.

description:
CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference
This instance (CVE-2023-50471): cJSON_InsertItemInArray() dereferences newitem (newitem->next/newitem->prev) without a NULL check, and dereferences newitem->prev->next when after_inserted->prev is NULL for a non-child item, causing a NULL pointer dereference.

review.ground_truth: cJSON_InsertItemInArray() dereferences newitem (newitem->next/newitem->prev) without a NULL check, and dereferences newitem->prev->next when after_inserted->prev is NULL for a non-child item, causing a NULL pointer dereference.
review.reasoning: The function writes through newitem->next and newitem->prev without first checking that newitem is non-NULL. The fix adds the newitem == NULL check, plus a guard for a corrupted array item. In the corrupted case, after_inserted->prev is NULL even though after_inserted is not the array's first child, so newitem->prev->next dereferences NULL. Both paths are NULL dereferences, matching the CVE's segfault and the CWE-476 label.

description:
CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference
This instance (CVE-2023-37185): zfp_rate_decompress() dereferences sc = dparams->schunk (sc->typesize) without checking that dparams->schunk is non-NULL.

review.ground_truth: zfp_rate_decompress() dereferences sc = dparams->schunk (sc->typesize) without checking that dparams->schunk is non-NULL.
review.reasoning: The CVE names zfp_prec_decompress, but the same commit adds the identical NULL check for dparams->schunk to zfp_rate_decompress. This function reads sc->typesize directly from sc = dparams->schunk without checking whether schunk is NULL. A decompression call made without a super-chunk context, as happens in plain chunk decompression, would dereference NULL. The flaw is genuinely present here and is the same bug class the fix repairs.

description:
CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference
This instance (CVE-2024-0727): PKCS12_unpack_authsafes() passes p12->authsafes->d.data, which can be NULL in a malformed PKCS12 file, to ASN1_item_unpack_ex() without a NULL check, causing a NULL pointer dereference.

review.ground_truth: PKCS12_unpack_authsafes() passes p12->authsafes->d.data, which can be NULL in a malformed PKCS12 file, to ASN1_item_unpack_ex() without a NULL check, causing a NULL pointer dereference.
review.reasoning: In PKCS12_unpack_authsafes(), p12->authsafes->d.data is optional in the ASN.1 template and can be NULL even when the content type is data. It is passed straight to ASN1_item_unpack_ex(), which dereferences the octet string's data and length, so the pointer is used with no NULL check. The fix adds exactly that check.

description:
CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference
This instance (CVE-2024-0727): PKCS12_unpack_p7data() passes p7->d.data to ASN1_item_unpack_ex() without checking for NULL, so a PKCS12 ContentInfo of type data with absent content causes a NULL pointer dereference.

review.ground_truth: PKCS12_unpack_p7data() passes p7->d.data to ASN1_item_unpack_ex() without checking for NULL, so a PKCS12 ContentInfo of type data with absent content causes a NULL pointer dereference.
review.reasoning: PKCS12_unpack_p7data() checks only that the ContentInfo type is data. It then passes p7->d.data to ASN1_item_unpack_ex(), but that optional field can be NULL in a malformed PKCS12 file. ASN1_item_unpack_ex() dereferences the octet string's data and length, so a NULL value crashes. The fix adds exactly this check, and the CVE names this API.

description:
CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference
This instance (CVE-2024-0727): PKCS12_unpack_p7data() passes p7->d.data to ASN1_item_unpack() without checking it for NULL; the optional ContentInfo content can be absent in a malicious PKCS12 file, so it is dereferenced as NULL.

review.ground_truth: PKCS12_unpack_p7data() passes p7->d.data to ASN1_item_unpack() without checking it for NULL; the optional ContentInfo content can be absent in a malicious PKCS12 file, so it is dereferenced as NULL.
review.reasoning: The PKCS7 ContentInfo d.data field is optional and can be NULL even when the type is data. The function passes p7->d.data straight to ASN1_item_unpack, which dereferences the octet string, causing a NULL dereference. The fix adds a NULL check right at that call. The NULL dereference itself happens in the callee (ASN1_item_unpack reads oct->data), so seeing it needs a reasonable assumption about that callee.

description:
CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference
This instance (CVE-2024-0727): In newpass_p12(), for an NID_pkcs7_encrypted authsafe, p7->d.encrypted (optional ContentInfo content that may be NULL) is dereferenced as p7->d.encrypted->enc_data->algorithm in the alg_get() call without a NULL check.

review.ground_truth: In newpass_p12(), for an NID_pkcs7_encrypted authsafe, p7->d.encrypted (optional ContentInfo content that may be NULL) is dereferenced as p7->d.encrypted->enc_data->algorithm in the alg_get() call without a NULL check.
review.reasoning: In newpass_p12(), p7->d.encrypted is dereferenced via p7->d.encrypted->enc_data->algorithm without a NULL check. The PKCS7 ContentInfo content is optional, so a crafted PKCS12 file can have the encrypted type with NULL content. PKCS12_unpack_p7encdata may return NULL in that case, but the dereference happens before the bags==NULL check, so the crash is reachable. The fix adds exactly this NULL check.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2024-22667): did_set_langmap() uses unbounded sprintf() to write the user-controlled remaining langmap string p (via e_langmap_extra_characters_after_semicolon_str) into the fixed-size caller-provided args->os_errbuf, overflowing the stack buffer.

review.ground_truth: did_set_langmap() uses unbounded sprintf() to write the user-controlled remaining langmap string p (via e_langmap_extra_characters_after_semicolon_str) into the fixed-size caller-provided args->os_errbuf, overflowing the stack buffer.
review.reasoning: The second sprintf writes the user-controlled remainder of 'langmap' (p, which is unbounded in length) into args->os_errbuf. That error buffer is a fixed-size stack buffer owned by the caller, so a long langmap value overflows it. The fix replaces this call with snprintf bounded by os_errbuflen. The first sprintf only writes transchar(from), which is short and bounded, and the diff leaves it alone.

description:
CWE-362: Concurrent Execution using Shared Resource with Improper Synchronization ('Race Condition')
This instance (CVE-2015-3150): for_each_problem_in_dir() checks access with dump_dir_accessible_by_uid(full_name) and then separately opens the path with dd_opendir(full_name), a TOCTOU race in which the directory can be replaced between check and use.

review.ground_truth: for_each_problem_in_dir() checks access with dump_dir_accessible_by_uid(full_name) and then separately opens the path with dd_opendir(full_name), a TOCTOU race in which the directory can be replaced between check and use.
review.reasoning: The function checks access by path with dump_dir_accessible_by_uid(full_name) and then opens the same path again with dd_opendir(full_name). Between the two, the directory entry can be swapped, for example for a symlink, which is a classic TOCTOU race. The fix opens an fd once and does both the check and the open on that fd. The CWE-20 label is generic; the real issue is a race condition (CWE-367). This instance only does a read-only open while enumerating problems, but it is the same race pattern the fix addresses.

description:
CWE-362: Concurrent Execution using Shared Resource with Improper Synchronization ('Race Condition')
This instance (CVE-2015-3150): open_directory_for_modification_of_element() checks permissions with dump_dir_accessible_by_uid(problem_id) on a path and then separately opens it with dd_opendir(problem_id), a TOCTOU race that lets a local user swap the directory (e.g. via symlink) between check and use.

review.ground_truth: open_directory_for_modification_of_element() checks permissions with dump_dir_accessible_by_uid(problem_id) on a path and then separately opens it with dd_opendir(problem_id), a TOCTOU race that lets a local user swap the directory (e.g. via symlink) between check and use.
review.reasoning: The function checks access with dump_dir_accessible_by_uid(problem_id) on a path and then opens the same path again with dd_opendir(problem_id). Between the two calls an attacker can swap the directory, for example with a symlink, so the check and the open act on different objects. That is a classic TOCTOU race. The fix opens an fd once, checks the fd and then opens the dump dir from that fd, which confirms the root cause is a race, not generic input validation.

description:
CWE-125: Out-of-bounds Read
This instance (CVE-2020-7044): wassp_match_strval() uses `max_entry < in_type` instead of `<=`, so in_type equal to max_entry indexes in_ptr->entry[] one past its end, an off-by-one out-of-bounds read.

review.ground_truth: wassp_match_strval() uses `max_entry < in_type` instead of `<=`, so in_type equal to max_entry indexes in_ptr->entry[] one past its end, an off-by-one out-of-bounds read.
review.reasoning: The bounds check `in_ptr->max_entry < in_type` lets `in_type == max_entry` through, so `entry[in_type]` reads one element past the end of the table. max_entry is the table's element count, as the fix to `<=` confirms. This is an off-by-one that leads to an out-of-bounds read. Negative in_type is also unchecked, though in_type typically comes from a packet field.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2019-9500): In brcmf_wowl_nd_results(), the firmware-supplied netinfo->SSID_len is used unchecked as the memcpy length into the 32-byte cfg->wowl.nd->ssid.ssid buffer, allowing a heap buffer overflow when it exceeds IEEE80211_MAX_SSID_LEN.

review.ground_truth: In brcmf_wowl_nd_results(), the firmware-supplied netinfo->SSID_len is used unchecked as the memcpy length into the 32-byte cfg->wowl.nd->ssid.ssid buffer, allowing a heap buffer overflow when it exceeds IEEE80211_MAX_SSID_LEN.
review.reasoning: netinfo->SSID_len comes from firmware event data and is used directly as the memcpy length into cfg->wowl.nd->ssid.ssid, which holds only IEEE80211_MAX_SSID_LEN (32) bytes. SSID_len is a u8, so values up to 255 can overflow the heap buffer. The fix clamps the length to the maximum before the copy. This is a missing bounds check that leads to an out-of-bounds write.

description:
CWE-125: Out-of-bounds Read
This instance (CVE-2020-7060): In the CP950 PUA branch, the misgrouped condition (the c1==0xc6 clause is ORed outside the `w <= 0 &&`) lets the lookup loop finish without a match, leaving k == table size, so cp950_pua_tbl[k] is read past the end of the global table.

review.ground_truth: In the CP950 PUA branch, the misgrouped condition (the c1==0xc6 clause is ORed outside the `w <= 0 &&`) lets the lookup loop finish without a match, leaving k == table size, so cp950_pua_tbl[k] is read past the end of the global table.
review.reasoning: The PUA condition is mis-parenthesized: it reads `(w <= 0 && (...)) || (c1 == 0xc6 && ...)`, so the second branch is taken even when w > 0. A c1/c combination that matches no cp950_pua_tbl range then lets the search loop finish with k equal to the table size. The code goes on to read cp950_pua_tbl[k], one entry past the end of the global array. The fix moves the check into is_in_cp950_pua() so it is ANDed with w <= 0, which addresses the reported global buffer over-read.

description:

description:

Nothing bounds len, which comes from strchr or strlen on attacker-controlled attribute text. It then also writes value_string[len] = 0. description:
CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference
This instance (CVE-2020-25866): On revisited frames, decompress() dereferences saved_data (from p_get_proto_data) without a NULL check, but no data was saved because the first-pass inflate into the fixed BLIP_INFLATE_BUFFER_SIZE buffer failed and returned NULL early.

review.ground_truth: On revisited frames, decompress() dereferences saved_data (from p_get_proto_data) without a NULL check, but no data was saved because the first-pass inflate into the fixed BLIP_INFLATE_BUFFER_SIZE buffer failed and returned NULL early.
review.reasoning: In the visited path, p_get_proto_data() can return NULL, because on the first pass an inflate error (e.g. a 16 KB buffer too small for the uncompressed data) returns NULL before any proto data is saved. saved_data->buf is then dereferenced without a check. The first-pass failure also returns NULL, and the caller dereferences it, but that crash is outside this function. Within this function the unchecked saved_data dereference is clearly visible, and the fix adds a NULL check for it.

description:
CWE-362: Concurrent Execution using Shared Resource with Improper Synchronization ('Race Condition')
This instance (CVE-2020-27670): set_iommu_pde_present() updates the live PTE through separate non-atomic bitfield writes (pte->fc, pte->mfn, pte->iw, pte->ir, pte->next_level, pte->pr), so the IOMMU can concurrently observe a half-updated entry instead of one written by a single atomic store.

review.ground_truth: set_iommu_pde_present() updates the live PTE through separate non-atomic bitfield writes (pte->fc, pte->mfn, pte->iw, pte->ir, pte->next_level, pte->pr), so the IOMMU can concurrently observe a half-updated entry instead of one written by a single atomic store.
review.reasoning: The function rewrites a live AMD IOMMU PTE one bitfield at a time. The compiler can reorder or split these stores, so the IOMMU hardware, which walks the tables concurrently, can see a half-updated entry, e.g. a new mfn with old permissions while pr is set. The fix builds the entry in a local variable and publishes it with a single write_atomic. This is a concurrency/atomicity flaw (race with the hardware walker) in this function, and it is visible locally.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2020-27678): The loop in parse_user_name() copies characters from user_input into the fixed-size stack buffer username[PAM_MAX_RESP_SIZE] without checking index against PAM_MAX_RESP_SIZE, so an overlong user name overflows the stack buffer.

review.ground_truth: The loop in parse_user_name() copies characters from user_input into the fixed-size stack buffer username[PAM_MAX_RESP_SIZE] without checking index against PAM_MAX_RESP_SIZE, so an overlong user name overflows the stack buffer.
review.reasoning: The copy loop writes user_input characters into the fixed stack buffer username[PAM_MAX_RESP_SIZE] and stops only at whitespace or NUL. It never checks index against the buffer size, so a long input overflows the stack. The input can exceed the buffer when it comes from callers such as pam_get_user, or from a conversation function that returns an overlong response. The fix adds an index bound to the loop. A secondary problem exists: with exactly PAM_MAX_RESP_SIZE characters, username is unterminated, so strcpy would read past it. That is part of the same missing-bound flaw.

description:

description:

description:

description:

This instance (CVE-2020-28346): In vq_getchain(), the indirect-descriptor pointer vindir returned by paddr_guest2host() for a guest-controlled vdir->addr is dereferenced (vp = &vindir[next]; vp->flags) without a NULL check, and _vq_record() failures that leave iov_base NULL are ignored.

description:

review.reasoning: When ioc_size exceeds 128 bytes, mbuf holds a kvmalloc'd argument buffer. If the ioctl also has array args, mbuf is then overwritten by a second kvmalloc for the array. Only the latter allocation is kvfree'd at the out label, so the first one leaks. The flaw is visible directly in this function, and the fix adds a separate array_buf variable and frees both.

description:

description:

It adds a len > 6 check before buf[3..6] is read in the 0xfb (calls) case, so this is an out-of-bounds read, not a write; the CWE-787 label is wrong on mechanism. The function only checks len >= 1. description:

review.reasoning: CPU_ALLOC can return NULL on allocation failure. The code does not check plinux_set, so the NULL pointer goes to sched_getaffinity and then CPU_ISSET_S dereferences it. The fix adds a NULL check on plinux_set and a check that kernel_nr_cpus is not negative. The NULL dereference is visible directly in this function.

description:

description:

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2022-47518): In wilc_wfi_cfg_parse_ch_attr, e->no_of_channels from the received frame is not validated against the remaining channel-list attribute size, so memset(e->ch_list, sta_ch, e->no_of_channels) writes beyond the buffer.

review.reasoning: The loop walks channel-list elements using the attacker-controlled e->no_of_channels and never checks it against the attribute length. memset(e->ch_list, sta_ch, e->no_of_channels) can therefore write past the end of the frame buffer. The loop also omits the element header size when advancing, and it bounds against the full attr_len rather than the bytes that follow the elem member. description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2018-1000091): cmd_client() concatenates all argv strings into the fixed 256-byte stack buffer 'buffer' using strcat without any length check, causing a stack buffer overflow with long arguments.

review.ground_truth: cmd_client() concatenates all argv strings into the fixed 256-byte stack buffer 'buffer' using strcat without any length check, causing a stack buffer overflow with long arguments.
review.reasoning: The loop joins argv into the 256-byte stack buffer with repeated strcat calls and never checks the total length, so long arguments overflow the stack. The fix replaces the loop with a bounded append_strings call. A second overflow is also visible: strcpy(addr.sun_path, path) copies the -p argument into the fixed-size sun_path array with no length check. The fix leaves that strcpy alone, but it is an evident additional out-of-bounds write.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2012-2763): readstr_upto() writes g_unichar_to_utf8 output into sc->strbuff via p in a loop that stops only on a delimiter or NUL, never on the buffer size, so a long input string overflows the fixed-size strbuff.

review.ground_truth: readstr_upto() writes g_unichar_to_utf8 output into sc->strbuff via p in a loop that stops only on a delimiter or NUL, never on the buffer size, so a long input string overflows the fixed-size strbuff.
review.reasoning: The do/while loop keeps writing UTF-8 encoded characters from inchar() into sc->strbuff through p until it sees a delimiter or NUL. It never checks p against the buffer size, so a long token overflows strbuff. The fix adds a bound check on p - sc->strbuff. The flaw is visible in this function, given that strbuff is a fixed-size array.

description:
CWE-401: Missing Release of Memory after Effective Lifetime (memory leak)
This instance (CVE-2018-9274): file_description is allocated by input_file_description() before the err check but only g_free'd in the err < 0 branch, so it leaks whenever err is non-negative.

review.ground_truth: file_description is allocated by input_file_description() before the err check but only g_free'd in the err < 0 branch, so it leaks whenever err is non-negative.
review.reasoning: The function allocates file_description with input_file_description() before checking err. It is freed only inside the err < 0 branch, so the else branch (err >= 0) leaks it. The fix moves the allocation into the err < 0 branch. This is a genuine memory leak that can be seen from the function alone, assuming input_file_description returns heap memory, which the g_free in the other branch confirms.

description:
CWE-401: Missing Release of Memory after Effective Lifetime (memory leak)
This instance (CVE-2018-10205): hyper_rescan_scsi() never frees the scandir()-allocated list array or its list[i] entries, because the only free(list) is unreachable after the return statement.

review.ground_truth: hyper_rescan_scsi() never frees the scandir()-allocated list array or its list[i] entries, because the only free(list) is unreachable after the return statement.
review.reasoning: scandir() allocates the list array and every dirent entry in it. In the original code, free(list) sits after the return, so it is dead code and never runs. The individual entries list[i] are never freed either, so every call leaks memory. The fix frees each entry and then the array.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2018-10753): delayed_output() points the global outbuf/mbf at a fixed 20*1024-byte stack array tmpbuf, while draw_sym_near()/a2b() write up to outbufsz bytes, so large delayed output overflows the stack buffer.

review.ground_truth: delayed_output() points the global outbuf/mbf at a fixed 20*1024-byte stack array tmpbuf, while draw_sym_near()/a2b() write up to outbufsz bytes, so large delayed output overflows the stack buffer.
review.reasoning: The function redirects the global output buffer (outbuf/mbf) to a fixed 20 KB stack array, tmpbuf, and then calls draw_sym_near(). The output routines (a2b) assume outbuf has outbufsz bytes, so many elements such as slurs write past the end of the stack array. The fix replaces it with a heap buffer of outbufsz bytes. The flaw is in this function's buffer sizing, but seeing the overflow requires knowing that the callees bound their writes by outbufsz, not by tmpbuf's real size.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2018-11595): jshPinFunctionToString() calls strncat(buf, ..., bufSize) with the full buffer size instead of the remaining space (bufSize - strlen(buf) - 1), so successive appends of devStr, the device number, the space and infoStr can write past the end of buf.

review.ground_truth: jshPinFunctionToString() calls strncat(buf, ..., bufSize) with the full buffer size instead of the remaining space (bufSize - strlen(buf) - 1), so successive appends of devStr, the device number, the space and infoStr can write past the end of buf.
review.reasoning: strncat's third argument is the maximum number of characters to append, not the destination size, so passing bufSize lets the appends write past buf when it already holds data. itostr also writes without any bounds check. The fix changes the limits to the remaining space. The function is a genuine instance of the strncat misuse in that fix commit, though the CVE text mentions syntax parsing, which may refer to another site. Whether it can actually overflow depends on caller buffer sizes (the strings are short), but the code flaw is real.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2018-11684): includeFile() copies includedFile->length characters into the stack buffer includeThis[MAXSTRING] and writes a NUL terminator at includeThis[k] without checking that k < MAXSTRING, so it writes past the end of the stack buffer.

review.ground_truth: includeFile() copies includedFile->length characters into the stack buffer includeThis[MAXSTRING] and writes a NUL terminator at includeThis[k] without checking that k < MAXSTRING, so it writes past the end of the stack buffer.
review.reasoning: includeThis is a stack buffer of size MAXSTRING. Characters are copied into it for k < includedFile->length with no check against that size. CharsString's chars array is also MAXSTRING long, so length can reach MAXSTRING. Then includeThis[k] = 0 writes one byte past the end of the buffer. The fix adds a k >= MAXSTRING check before the terminator write, which confirms the stack overflow lives in this function.

description:
CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference
This instance (CVE-2022-34520): oneshotall_buffer() appends the result of get_the_meta() to the returned list without checking it for NULL, so the caller r_bin_file_xtr_load_buffer dereferences a NULL RBinXtrData element.

review.ground_truth: oneshotall_buffer() appends the result of get_the_meta() to the returned list without checking it for NULL, so the caller r_bin_file_xtr_load_buffer dereferences a NULL RBinXtrData element.
review.reasoning: In oneshotall_buffer, get_the_meta() can return NULL on a crafted file, and the NULL is still appended to the list. r_bin_file_xtr_load_buffer later iterates that list and dereferences the NULL element. The fix returns NULL when meta is NULL. The root cause is in this function (appending an unchecked NULL), but the dereference happens in the caller.

description:
CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference
This instance (CVE-2022-1671): rxrpc_free_preparse_s() calls sec->free_preparse_server_key(prep) after checking only that sec is non-NULL, so with rxrpc_no_security, whose free_preparse_server_key op is NULL, it calls a NULL function pointer.

review.ground_truth: rxrpc_free_preparse_s() calls sec->free_preparse_server_key(prep) after checking only that sec is non-NULL, so with rxrpc_no_security, whose free_preparse_server_key op is NULL, it calls a NULL function pointer.
review.reasoning: The function calls sec->free_preparse_server_key without checking that the function pointer is non-NULL. The rxrpc_no_security ops table does not implement it, so after preparse with a security index of 0 the free path jumps to address 0. The fix adds exactly that check here. The CVE text names rxrpc_preparse_s, but this sibling function has the same flaw and was patched by the same commit.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2020-10931): In try_read_command_binary(), memcpy copies the attacker-controlled extlen (up to 255) bytes from the packet into the stack array extbuf, which has only BIN_MAX_EXTLEN bytes reserved after the header, with no check that extlen <= BIN_MAX_EXTLEN, overflowing the stack buffer.

review.ground_truth: In try_read_command_binary(), memcpy copies the attacker-controlled extlen (up to 255) bytes from the packet into the stack array extbuf, which has only BIN_MAX_EXTLEN bytes reserved after the header, with no check that extlen <= BIN_MAX_EXTLEN, overflowing the stack buffer.
review.reasoning: extlen is an attacker-controlled uint8_t taken from the binary header, so it can be as large as 255. extbuf only reserves BIN_MAX_EXTLEN (20) bytes after the header. The memcpy copies extlen bytes into extbuf with no bound, causing a stack buffer overflow. The fix clamps the copy length to BIN_MAX_EXTLEN.

description:
CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference
This instance (CVE-2020-1967): In tls1_check_sig_alg(), the result of tls1_lookup_sigalg() on a peer-supplied peer_cert_sigalgs[i] value is dereferenced (sigalg->sigandhash) without a NULL check, so an unrecognised signature algorithm from the peer causes a NULL pointer dereference.

review.ground_truth: In tls1_check_sig_alg(), the result of tls1_lookup_sigalg() on a peer-supplied peer_cert_sigalgs[i] value is dereferenced (sigalg->sigandhash) without a NULL check, so an unrecognised signature algorithm from the peer causes a NULL pointer dereference.
review.reasoning: This is the well-known CVE-2020-1967 bug. tls1_lookup_sigalg() returns NULL when the peer sends a signature_algorithms_cert codepoint that OpenSSL does not recognise. The loop then dereferences sigalg->sigandhash without a NULL check. The fix adds exactly that check. Seeing the flaw requires knowing that the lookup can return NULL, which is a reasonable assumption about the callee.

description:
CWE-362: Concurrent Execution using Shared Resource with Improper Synchronization ('Race Condition')
This instance (CVE-2020-11884): enable_sacf_uaccess() reads and loads control registers 1 and 7 and sets the CIF_ASCE_PRIMARY/SECONDARY flags without disabling interrupts, so a concurrent page table upgrade IPI (set_user_asce) can interleave and leave CR1/CR7 inconsistent.

review.ground_truth: enable_sacf_uaccess() reads and loads control registers 1 and 7 and sets the CIF_ASCE_PRIMARY/SECONDARY flags without disabling interrupts, so a concurrent page table upgrade IPI (set_user_asce) can interleave and leave CR1/CR7 inconsistent.
review.reasoning: The fix wraps the control-register switching sequence in enable_sacf_uaccess() with local_irq_save/restore. Without it, a concurrent page table upgrade IPI (__crst_table_upgrade -> set_user_asce) can fire mid-sequence. That IPI reloads CR1 and modifies the CIF flags and lowcore user_asce while this function is reading and setting them. The result is inconsistent CR1/CR7 state, so in secondary space mode instructions are fetched through the user page table. This is a genuine race visible in this function: no interrupt protection around the non-atomic read-modify-write of control registers.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2019-20839): ConnectClientToUnixSock() strcpy()s the caller-supplied sockFile into the fixed-size stack buffer addr.sun_path without checking its length, so a long socket filename overflows the stack.

review.ground_truth: ConnectClientToUnixSock() strcpy()s the caller-supplied sockFile into the fixed-size stack buffer addr.sun_path without checking its length, so a long socket filename overflows the stack.
review.reasoning: strcpy copies sockFile into the fixed-size addr.sun_path (about 108 bytes) on the stack without checking its length. A long socket filename therefore overflows the stack buffer. The fix adds exactly this length check, and the flaw is visible directly in this function.

description:
CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference
This instance (CVE-2012-4233): In XclImpDrawObjBase::ReadObj8(), xDrawObj stays empty when the record is too short or the OBJCMO subrecord id/size check fails, yet xDrawObj->mnTab and xDrawObj->ImplReadObj8() are then called without a NULL check.

review.ground_truth: In XclImpDrawObjBase::ReadObj8(), xDrawObj stays empty when the record is too short or the OBJCMO subrecord id/size check fails, yet xDrawObj->mnTab and xDrawObj->ImplReadObj8() are then called without a NULL check.
review.reasoning: If GetRecLeft() < 10, or the subrecord is not OBJCMO, or its size is under 6, xDrawObj is never assigned. It is then dereferenced unconditionally at xDrawObj->mnTab, which matches the xls NULL dereference described in the CVE. The fix adds a placeholder object whenever xDrawObj is still empty, so the shown pre-fix code is genuinely vulnerable.

description:
CWE-362: Concurrent Execution using Shared Resource with Improper Synchronization ('Race Condition')
This instance (CVE-2017-15951): keyring_search_iterator() tests KEY_FLAG_NEGATIVE in kflags and then separately reads key->reject_error (unioned with the payload), so a concurrent instantiation/update can change the key between the two reads and a payload pointer is returned as the error code.

review.ground_truth: keyring_search_iterator() tests KEY_FLAG_NEGATIVE in kflags and then separately reads key->reject_error (unioned with the payload), so a concurrent instantiation/update can change the key between the two reads and a payload pointer is returned as the error code.
review.reasoning: This is the core site of the CVE. The search iterator reads key->flags to see whether KEY_FLAG_NEGATIVE is set, and only afterwards reads key->reject_error. reject_error shares a union with the payload pointers. If a concurrent key_update/instantiate turns the negative key positive between those two reads, the 'error' read is really a payload pointer, which is then returned as ERR_PTR. The fix collapses flags and error into one atomically read state field.

description:
CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference
This instance (CVE-2017-16526): uwbd_start() checks kthread_run()'s return for NULL instead of IS_ERR(), so on failure it dereferences the ERR_PTR value via rc->uwbd.task->pid and leaves the error pointer stored in rc->uwbd.task.

review.ground_truth: uwbd_start() checks kthread_run()'s return for NULL instead of IS_ERR(), so on failure it dereferences the ERR_PTR value via rc->uwbd.task->pid and leaves the error pointer stored in rc->uwbd.task.
review.reasoning: kthread_run() returns ERR_PTR(-EINTR) on failure, never NULL, so the NULL check never fires. The else branch then dereferences the error pointer (rc->uwbd.task->pid), and the ERR_PTR is also left stored in rc->uwbd.task for uwbd_stop to use later. This is an invalid-pointer dereference from a wrong return-value check. NULL-deref (CWE-476) is the closest category, more specific than the CWE-119 label.

description:
CWE-362: Concurrent Execution using Shared Resource with Improper Synchronization ('Race Condition')
This instance (CVE-2017-12146): driver_override_store() reads and replaces pdev->driver_override and then kfree()s the old value without holding device_lock, so a concurrent show or store can use the freed string or double-free it.

review.ground_truth: driver_override_store() reads and replaces pdev->driver_override and then kfree()s the old value without holding device_lock, so a concurrent show or store can use the freed string or double-free it.
review.reasoning: The store function reads old = pdev->driver_override and replaces it without holding device_lock, then kfree(old). A concurrent driver_override_show (or a second store) can still be using the old string after it is freed, or two stores can free the same pointer twice. The fix adds device_lock around the read-and-swap. Root cause is missing locking, i.e. a race.

description:
CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference
This instance (CVE-2017-14505): DrawGetStrokeDashArray() writes through q (initialized from dasharray) without checking whether AcquireQuantumMemory() returned NULL, causing a NULL pointer dereference on allocation failure.

review.ground_truth: DrawGetStrokeDashArray() writes through q (initialized from dasharray) without checking whether AcquireQuantumMemory() returned NULL, causing a NULL pointer dereference on allocation failure.
review.reasoning: The function calls AcquireQuantumMemory for dasharray and then writes through q without checking whether the allocation returned NULL. The fix adds exactly that NULL check. This is a genuine unchecked-allocation NULL dereference, visible directly in the function's own code.

description:
CWE-908: Use of Uninitialized Resource
This instance (CVE-2017-0380): In rend_service_intro_established(), the uninitialized stack buffer serviceid is passed to log_warn() in the find_intro_point()==NULL error path before base32_encode() fills it, leaking stack contents to the log.

review.ground_truth: In rend_service_intro_established(), the uninitialized stack buffer serviceid is passed to log_warn() in the find_intro_point()==NULL error path before base32_encode() fills it, leaking stack contents to the log.
review.reasoning: The stack buffer serviceid is uninitialized when the intro == NULL branch passes it to log_warn via safe_str_client(serviceid). It is only filled by base32_encode after that branch. The fix moves the encode earlier. This is use of uninitialized memory that leaks to the log; CWE-532 names the consequence, while CWE-457/908 names the root cause.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2012-3364): nci_extract_rf_params_nfcf_passive_poll() copies sensf_res_len bytes, taken unchecked from the incoming frame, into the fixed-size nfcf_poll->sensf_res array via memcpy without clamping to NFC_SENSF_RES_MAXSIZE, overflowing it.

review.ground_truth: nci_extract_rf_params_nfcf_passive_poll() copies sensf_res_len bytes, taken unchecked from the incoming frame, into the fixed-size nfcf_poll->sensf_res array via memcpy without clamping to NFC_SENSF_RES_MAXSIZE, overflowing it.
review.reasoning: The function takes sensf_res_len straight from the incoming frame and passes it to memcpy into the fixed-size nfcf_poll->sensf_res array (NFC_SENSF_RES_MAXSIZE) without any bound check. The fix clamps the length to that maximum. This is a genuine write past a fixed-size buffer, and it is visible within this function.

description:
CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference
This instance (CVE-2013-0166): ASN1_item_verify() dereferences pkey->ameth->pkey_id (and passes pkey to EVP_VerifyFinal) without checking that pkey is non-NULL, so a NULL key from an invalid OCSP signer certificate crashes the process.

review.ground_truth: ASN1_item_verify() dereferences pkey->ameth->pkey_id (and passes pkey to EVP_VerifyFinal) without checking that pkey is non-NULL, so a NULL key from an invalid OCSP signer certificate crashes the process.
review.reasoning: ASN1_item_verify dereferences pkey->ameth->pkey_id without checking pkey for NULL. The OCSP verify path (OCSP_basic_verify) can pass a NULL key obtained from X509_get_pubkey on an invalid key, which crashes here. The CWE-310 label is generic; the root cause is a NULL dereference. The main fix is in the OCSP caller, but this function's missing check is also patched and lies directly on the crash site.

description:
CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference
This instance (CVE-2013-1415): In pkinit_check_kdc_pkid(), when d2i_PKCS7_ISSUER_AND_SERIAL() fails and returns NULL, the goto cleanup path dereferences is->issuer and is->serial on the NULL pointer is.

review.ground_truth: In pkinit_check_kdc_pkid(), when d2i_PKCS7_ISSUER_AND_SERIAL() fails and returns NULL, the goto cleanup path dereferences is->issuer and is->serial on the NULL pointer is.
review.reasoning: When d2i_PKCS7_ISSUER_AND_SERIAL fails, is is NULL and the code jumps to cleanup. The cleanup block then dereferences is->issuer and is->serial, which is a NULL dereference triggered by a malformed kdcPkId. The fix returns early instead of jumping to cleanup. This is clearly visible within the function.

description:
CWE-125: Out-of-bounds Read
This instance (CVE-2022-2124): In current_quote(), the loop `while (i <= col_end)` scanning for quotechar indexes line[i] up to a column taken from the Visual/cursor positions without stopping at the line's NUL, so it reads past the end of the line buffer when the line was shortened after selection.

review.ground_truth: In current_quote(), the loop `while (i <= col_end)` scanning for quotechar indexes line[i] up to a column taken from the Visual/cursor positions without stopping at the line's NUL, so it reads past the end of the line buffer when the line was shortened after selection.
review.reasoning: The loop `while (i <= col_end)` scans line[i] from VIsual.col to the cursor column. It does not check for the terminating NUL. If the line was shortened after the Visual area was selected, the stored columns can lie past the end of the line, and the loop reads beyond the buffer. The fix adds a NUL check inside the loop, which matches this read past the end of the string (CWE-126).

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2019-12835): xml_memory_writer::write memcpy's size bytes to p_write and advances it without checking remaining buffer capacity, so escaped XML output larger than the original input overflows the destination buffer.

review.ground_truth: xml_memory_writer::write memcpy's size bytes to p_write and advances it without checking remaining buffer capacity, so escaped XML output larger than the original input overflows the destination buffer.
review.reasoning: xml_memory_writer::write copies serialized XML into a fixed buffer through p_write with no bounds check. The output can be larger than the input because characters get escaped (e.g. & becomes &), so the copy can run past the buffer. The fix replaces the raw buffer with a vector that grows as needed. Seeing that the buffer is fixed-size and that the output can grow needs a small assumption about the surrounding writer class.

description:
CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference
This instance (CVE-2012-6139): In xsltDocumentFunction's nodeset branch, obj returned by valuePop(ctxt) is dereferenced (obj->nodesetval) without a NULL check, crashing when an uninitialized variable is passed to document().

review.ground_truth: In xsltDocumentFunction's nodeset branch, obj returned by valuePop(ctxt) is dereferenced (obj->nodesetval) without a NULL check, crashing when an uninitialized variable is passed to document().
review.reasoning: The fix adds NULL checks on obj after valuePop in the nodeset branch. When an uninitialized variable is passed to document(), the code dereferences obj->nodesetval with no NULL check and crashes. The flaw is a NULL pointer dereference, it is in this function, and the CVE text confirms it. The trigger depends on valuePop/variable semantics returning NULL, so locality is partial.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2013-3670): In rle_unpack(), the RLE branch checks `dest_end - pd < i` instead of `< 2*l`, so the loop writing two bytes per iteration for l iterations writes past dest_end.

review.ground_truth: In rle_unpack(), the RLE branch checks `dest_end - pd < i` instead of `< 2*l`, so the loop writing two bytes per iteration for l iterations writes past dest_end.
review.reasoning: In the non-0x80 branch the destination check compares dest_end - pd against i (the running count) instead of 2*l, so the loop can write 2*l bytes past dest_end. It also reads 2*l source bytes with the unchecked get_byteu after verifying only 2 bytes remain, and the loop reuses i as its counter, clobbering the running total. The primary flaw is the out-of-bounds write to dest, which the fix repairs by checking 2*l and reading only two source bytes.

description:
CWE-416: Use After Free
This instance (CVE-2013-4127): vhost_net_ubuf_put_and_wait() unconditionally calls kfree(ubufs) after waiting for the refcount to drop, while its caller vhost_net_flush() keeps using the ubufs object afterward, causing a use-after-free.

review.ground_truth: vhost_net_ubuf_put_and_wait() unconditionally calls kfree(ubufs) after waiting for the refcount to drop, while its caller vhost_net_flush() keeps using the ubufs object afterward, causing a use-after-free.
review.reasoning: vhost_net_ubuf_put_and_wait() drops the reference, waits for the refcount to hit zero, and then calls kfree(ubufs). Its caller vhost_net_flush() keeps using ubufs after this call (it re-initializes the kref), which touches freed memory. The fix removes the kfree from this function and adds a separate put-wait-and-free API for callers that actually want the free. The dereference after free is in the caller, but the premature free that the fix removes is here.

description:
CWE-416: Use After Free
This instance (CVE-2013-2884): Element::setAttributeNode() calls attachToElement(this) on an Attr from another document without adopting it into this element's tree scope, so its stale ownerDocument can be used after that document is destroyed.

review.ground_truth: Element::setAttributeNode() calls attachToElement(this) on an Attr from another document without adopting it into this element's tree scope, so its stale ownerDocument can be used after that document is destroyed.
review.reasoning: Element::setAttributeNode() attaches an Attr node to this element but never re-adopts it into the element's document. If the Attr came from another document, such as an iframe, its ownerDocument/tree scope still points at the old document. When that document goes away, the stale pointer is used after free. The fix adds treeScope()->adoptIfNeeded(attrNode). The CWE-399 label is generic; the actual mechanism is a lifetime error leading to use-after-free.

description:
CWE-416: Use After Free
This instance (CVE-2013-2925): handleDidTimeout() ignores whether internalAbort() caused script reentry via m_loader->cancel(), then continues with handleDidFailGeneric()/changeState(DONE) on an XHR whose state or loader a reentrant open()/send() changed, causing a use-after-free.

review.ground_truth: handleDidTimeout() ignores whether internalAbort() caused script reentry via m_loader->cancel(), then continues with handleDidFailGeneric()/changeState(DONE) on an XHR whose state or loader a reentrant open()/send() changed, causing a use-after-free.
review.reasoning: The fix makes handleDidTimeout bail out when internalAbort() reports that m_loader->cancel() caused reentry. Before the fix, script run synchronously during cancel (e.g. onload) could call open() or send() on the same XHR. The function then kept going with stale state: it set m_exceptionCode, called handleDidFailGeneric() and changeState(DONE). Those calls act on a loader or state the reentrant call has replaced, which leads to the use-after-free in the CVE. The protect RefPtr keeps the XHR object alive, but not the state the reentrant call replaced.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2013-4514): In wvlan_set_station_nickname(), memcpy(lp->StationName, extra, wrqu->data.length) copies a user-controlled length into the fixed-size StationName buffer without bounding it by sizeof(lp->StationName), causing a buffer overflow.

review.ground_truth: In wvlan_set_station_nickname(), memcpy(lp->StationName, extra, wrqu->data.length) copies a user-controlled length into the fixed-size StationName buffer without bounding it by sizeof(lp->StationName), causing a buffer overflow.
review.reasoning: The function copies wrqu->data.length bytes from the user-supplied extra into the fixed-size lp->StationName with memcpy() and never checks the length against the buffer size. A nickname longer than the buffer overflows it. The fix clamps the length to sizeof(lp->StationName).

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2013-0868): In generate_joint_tables(), the index i is never checked against 1<<VLC_BITS. Invalid/zero code lengths in s->len therefore let the nested loops write len[i], bits[i], symbols[i] and map[i] past the end of the stack arrays and pix_bgr_map.

review.ground_truth: In generate_joint_tables(), the index i is never checked against 1<<VLC_BITS. Invalid/zero code lengths in s->len therefore let the nested loops write len[i], bits[i], symbols[i] and map[i] past the end of the stack arrays and pix_bgr_map.
review.reasoning: The fix adds asserts that i stays below 1<<VLC_BITS before writing len[i], bits[i], symbols[i] and map[i]. When the Huffman lengths are invalid (for example len==0, or a set that does not satisfy the Kraft inequality, left unchecked because init_vlc's return was ignored), the number of combinations that fit within VLC_BITS can exceed the 2^VLC_BITS stack arrays. The function then writes past the end of these arrays. The flaw is visible in this function, but depends on unvalidated s->len values set elsewhere.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2013-0856): The warm-up loop in lpc_prediction() iterates i up to lpc_order without checking i < nb_samples, so when nb_samples < lpc_order it writes buffer_out[i] (and reads error_buffer[i]) beyond the sample buffers.

review.ground_truth: The warm-up loop in lpc_prediction() iterates i up to lpc_order without checking i < nb_samples, so when nb_samples < lpc_order it writes buffer_out[i] (and reads error_buffer[i]) beyond the sample buffers.
review.reasoning: The warm-up loop runs i from 1 to lpc_order and never checks it against nb_samples. When nb_samples is smaller than lpc_order (up to 30), it reads error_buffer[i] and writes buffer_out[i] past the nb_samples-sized buffers. The fix adds the condition i < nb_samples. The root cause is a missing bound check that lets the write go out of bounds; the CWE-20 label is generic.

description:
CWE-416: Use After Free
This instance (CVE-2014-1735): In handleSpeakingCompleted(), m_utteranceQueue.removeFirst() may release the last reference to utterance, which is then used by fireEvent() after being freed, because no protecting reference is held.

review.ground_truth: In handleSpeakingCompleted(), m_utteranceQueue.removeFirst() may release the last reference to utterance, which is then used by fireEvent() after being freed, because no protecting reference is held.
review.reasoning: When m_utteranceQueue holds the last reference to the utterance, m_utteranceQueue.removeFirst() can drop the refcount to zero and free it. fireEvent() then uses the raw utterance pointer after it has been freed. The fix adds a RefPtr protect so the object stays alive until the event has fired. The flaw is in this function, but seeing it requires knowing that the queue may hold the only reference.

description:
CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference
This instance (CVE-2014-2986): In the GICD_ICFGR+2..GICD_ICFGRN case of vgic_distr_mmio_write(), vgic_lock_rank(v, rank) dereferences the rank returned by vgic_irq_rank() before checking it for NULL, so a guest write to an out-of-range ICFGR register causes a NULL pointer dereference.
