review.ground_truth: In the GICD_ICFGR+2..GICD_ICFGRN case of vgic_distr_mmio_write(), vgic_lock_rank(v, rank) dereferences the rank returned by vgic_irq_rank() before checking it for NULL, so a guest write to an out-of-range ICFGR register causes a NULL pointer dereference.
review.reasoning: In the GICD_ICFGR SPI case, vgic_lock_rank(v, rank) is called before the NULL check on rank. vgic_irq_rank() returns NULL when the IRQ is outside the range the guest handles, so the lock call dereferences a NULL pointer (&rank->lock) and crashes the host. The fix moves the check before the lock. The flaw is a NULL dereference, not generic input validation, so CWE-476 fits better than the CWE-20 label.

description:
CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference
This instance (CVE-2014-3967): In hvm_inject_msi(), the pointer returned by pirq_info(d, pirq) for a guest-chosen pirq is dereferenced (info->arch.hvm.emuirq) and passed to send_guest_pirq() without a NULL check, though it is NULL for a non-allocated pIRQ and is not re-fetched after map_domain_emuirq_pirq().

review.ground_truth: In hvm_inject_msi(), the pointer returned by pirq_info(d, pirq) for a guest-chosen pirq is dereferenced (info->arch.hvm.emuirq) and passed to send_guest_pirq() without a NULL check, though it is NULL for a non-allocated pIRQ and is not re-fetched after map_domain_emuirq_pirq().
review.reasoning: pirq_info() returns NULL for a pIRQ that has not been allocated. The function then dereferences info->arch.hvm.emuirq without checking for NULL. It also keeps using the stale info after map_domain_emuirq_pirq() and passes it to send_guest_pirq(). The pirq value comes from the guest-controlled MSI address and dest field, so a guest can pick an unallocated pIRQ and crash the host. The CWE-Other label is generic; this is a NULL pointer dereference.

description:
CWE-125: Out-of-bounds Read
This instance (CVE-2014-3480): cdf_count_chain() bounds-checks sid against maxsector = sat_len * size, a byte count rather than the number of sector-ID entries, and uses '>' instead of '>='. A crafted sid therefore passes and sat->sat_tab[sid] is read out of bounds.

review.ground_truth: cdf_count_chain() bounds-checks sid against maxsector = sat_len * size, a byte count rather than the number of sector-ID entries, and uses '>' instead of '>='. A crafted sid therefore passes and sat->sat_tab[sid] is read out of bounds.
review.reasoning: In the pre-fix code, maxsector is computed as sat_len * size. That is the SAT size in bytes, not the number of 4-byte cdf_secid_t entries. The check also uses '>' instead of '>='. So a crafted sid well beyond the sat_tab array passes the check and is used to index sat->sat_tab[sid], reading out of bounds. The fix divides by sizeof(maxsector) and uses '>='.

description:
CWE-362: Concurrent Execution using Shared Resource with Improper Synchronization ('Race Condition')
This instance (CVE-2020-15567): ept_next_level() passes the live EPT entry pointer ept_entry to ept_set_middle_entry(), which modifies the PTE in place with non-atomic bitfield writes, so hardware may observe a partially written entry instead of the entry being built locally and installed with atomic_write_ept_entry().

review.ground_truth: ept_next_level() passes the live EPT entry pointer ept_entry to ept_set_middle_entry(), which modifies the PTE in place with non-atomic bitfield writes, so hardware may observe a partially written entry instead of the entry being built locally and installed with atomic_write_ept_entry().
review.reasoning: This function passes the live PTE pointer ept_entry to ept_set_middle_entry, which fills in the entry with a series of non-atomic bitfield writes while the EPT table may be in use by hardware. That is the XSA-328 pattern, and the fix builds the entry in the local copy e and then installs it with atomic_write_ept_entry. The commit message argues this particular call site was not exploitable because the new table page is zeroed. Still, the non-atomic modification of a live PTE is present here and is part of the XSA-328 fix set. The root cause is a race: hardware can observe a partially written PTE.

description:
CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference
This instance (CVE-2020-16118): imap_mbox_connect() passes handle->last_msg to strncmp() without a NULL check, and it is NULL when the server greets with PREAUTH, which does not set last_msg.

review.ground_truth: imap_mbox_connect() passes handle->last_msg to strncmp() without a NULL check, and it is NULL when the server greets with PREAUTH, which does not set last_msg.
review.reasoning: After the initial greeting step returns IMR_UNTAGGED, imap_mbox_connect passes handle->last_msg straight to strncmp without checking it. A PREAUTH greeting is handled by ir_preauth, which does not store last_msg, so the pointer can still be NULL at that point. The fix adds a NULL check before the strncmp. Seeing that last_msg can be NULL requires knowing how the response parser behaves, so the flaw is only partly visible from this function.

description:
CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference
This instance (CVE-2020-16269): get_die_name() calls strdup on die->attr_values[name_attr_idx].string.content without checking for NULL, which happens when a malformed DW_AT_name references an invalid .debug_str offset.

review.ground_truth: get_die_name() calls strdup on die->attr_values[name_attr_idx].string.content without checking for NULL, which happens when a malformed DW_AT_name references an invalid .debug_str offset.
review.reasoning: get_die_name() passes die->attr_values[name_attr_idx].string.content to strdup without checking it for NULL. A malformed DW_AT_name with an invalid .debug_str offset leaves that content NULL, so strdup dereferences a NULL pointer and crashes. The fix adds exactly this NULL check and falls back to create_type_name_from_offset. Knowing the content can be NULL depends on how the parser fills attributes elsewhere, so the flaw is only partly visible from this function.

description:
CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference
This instance (CVE-2020-16293): do_compose_group() selects compose_group_nonknockout_nonblend_isolated_allmask_common when maskbuf is non-NULL but maskbuf->data is NULL (has_mask false), passing a NULL mask_row_ptr that the callee dereferences.

review.ground_truth: do_compose_group() selects compose_group_nonknockout_nonblend_isolated_allmask_common when maskbuf is non-NULL but maskbuf->data is NULL (has_mask false), passing a NULL mask_row_ptr that the callee dereferences.
review.reasoning: When maskbuf is non-NULL but maskbuf->data is NULL, has_mask stays false and mask_row_ptr stays NULL. The old condition (has_mask || maskbuf) still sends this case to compose_group_nonknockout_nonblend_isolated_allmask_common whenever the mask rect covers the area. That routine dereferences mask_row_ptr unconditionally, so it reads a NULL pointer. The fix requires both has_mask and maskbuf before choosing the mask path. The bad dispatch is in this function; the actual dereference happens in the callee.

description:
CWE-125: Out-of-bounds Read
This instance (CVE-2020-16296): The loop in GetNumWrongData() dereferences curPtr[count] and curPtr[count+1] before checking count against maxnum, so it reads past the end of the buffer.

review.ground_truth: The loop in GetNumWrongData() dereferences curPtr[count] and curPtr[count+1] before checking count against maxnum, so it reads past the end of the buffer.
review.reasoning: The while condition reads curPtr[count] and curPtr[count+1] before checking maxnum > count. On the last iteration, count can equal maxnum, so the loop reads curPtr[maxnum]; earlier, count+1 can reach maxnum. Either way it reads past the buffer of maxnum bytes. These are reads, not writes, so the CWE-787 label is off; this is an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125).

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2023-21250): In gatt_end_operation()'s GATTC_OPTYPE_READ branch, memcpy copies p_clcb->counter bytes into the fixed-size stack buffer cb_data.att_value.value without checking that the length is at most GATT_MAX_ATTR_LEN, overflowing it.

review.ground_truth: In gatt_end_operation()'s GATTC_OPTYPE_READ branch, memcpy copies p_clcb->counter bytes into the fixed-size stack buffer cb_data.att_value.value without checking that the length is at most GATT_MAX_ATTR_LEN, overflowing it.
review.reasoning: In the READ branch, cb_data.att_value.len is set from p_clcb->counter, and memcpy copies that many bytes into the fixed att_value.value array (GATT_MAX_ATTR_LEN = 512). Nothing checks the length against the array size, and counter can reach the MTU size of 517. The fix clamps the length, so this is a genuine stack buffer overflow in this function. Knowing that counter can exceed 512 depends on callers, so locality is partial.

description:
CWE-416: Use After Free
This instance (CVE-2016-1635): OnDocumentElementCreated passes the raw context() ScriptContext pointer and the JS callback into a self-owned LoadWatcher, which later invokes the callback (possibly re-entrantly) after that ScriptContext may already have been destroyed, causing a use-after-free.

review.ground_truth: OnDocumentElementCreated passes the raw context() ScriptContext pointer and the JS callback into a self-owned LoadWatcher, which later invokes the callback (possibly re-entrantly) after that ScriptContext may already have been destroyed, causing a use-after-free.
review.reasoning: Before the fix, OnDocumentElementCreated creates a self-deleting LoadWatcher that holds a raw pointer to the ScriptContext (context()) and calls the JS function synchronously. The context can be destroyed before the watcher fires, and the callback can re-enter. The fix stops capturing the context: the callback is bound through a WeakPtr to the natives object, and it is posted asynchronously when the document element already exists. So the flaw is a lifetime/re-entrancy use-after-free rooted in this function's capture of context(), though seeing it needs knowledge of how LoadWatcher behaves.

description:
CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference
This instance (CVE-2016-3119): In process_db_args(), the return value of strtok_r(db_args[i], "=", &arg_val) can be NULL for an empty DB argument and is passed unchecked to strcmp(arg, TKTPOLICY_ARG), causing a NULL pointer dereference.

review.ground_truth: In process_db_args(), the return value of strtok_r(db_args[i], "=", &arg_val) can be NULL for an empty DB argument and is passed unchecked to strcmp(arg, TKTPOLICY_ARG), causing a NULL pointer dereference.
review.reasoning: When db_args[i] is an empty string (or consists only of '=' characters), strtok_r() returns NULL. The result is then passed straight to strcmp(arg, TKTPOLICY_ARG), which dereferences a NULL pointer. An authenticated user can trigger this remotely through modify_principal, crashing kadmind. The fix substitutes an empty string when arg is NULL, so the flaw is visible within this function alone.

description:
CWE-125: Out-of-bounds Read
This instance (CVE-2017-18379): nvmet_fc_find_target_queue() indexes assoc->queues[qid] with a qid extracted from the attacker-controlled connection_id without checking it against NVMET_NR_QUEUES, causing an out-of-bounds read of the queues array.

review.ground_truth: nvmet_fc_find_target_queue() indexes assoc->queues[qid] with a qid extracted from the attacker-controlled connection_id without checking it against NVMET_NR_QUEUES, causing an out-of-bounds read of the queues array.
review.reasoning: qid is taken from the remote-supplied connection_id. It is then used to index assoc->queues[qid] with no bounds check. The array has NVMET_NR_QUEUES+1 entries, so a qid larger than that reads past the array. The read pointer is then dereferenced and refcounted. The fix adds a range check on qid before the lookup.

description:
CWE-125: Out-of-bounds Read
This instance (CVE-2016-4542): exif_process_TIFF_in_JPEG() reads the TIFF header values via php_ifd_get16u(CharBuf+2) and php_ifd_get32u(CharBuf+4) without checking that length >= 8, causing an out-of-bounds heap read on short EXIF data.

review.ground_truth: exif_process_TIFF_in_JPEG() reads the TIFF header values via php_ifd_get16u(CharBuf+2) and php_ifd_get32u(CharBuf+4) without checking that length >= 8, causing an out-of-bounds heap read on short EXIF data.
review.reasoning: The function reads CharBuf+2 (16-bit) and CharBuf+4 (32-bit) without first checking that length is at least 8. A crafted EXIF section shorter than 8 bytes therefore causes a heap out-of-bounds read. The fix adds a length < 8 check, which matches the fix commit for bug #72094 even though the CVE text names exif_process_IFD_TAG. The 2-byte memcmp at the top also runs before any length check, but it is covered by the same flaw.

description:
CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference
This instance (CVE-2016-4581): In propagate_one(), the backtracking loop advances last_source = last_source->mnt_master and last_dest = last_source->mnt_parent without stopping at first_source, so when the first propagated copy is a slave it walks past the chain and dereferences a NULL mnt_master.

review.ground_truth: In propagate_one(), the backtracking loop advances last_source = last_source->mnt_master and last_dest = last_source->mnt_parent without stopping at first_source, so when the first propagated copy is a slave it walks past the chain and dereferences a NULL mnt_master.
review.reasoning: The pre-fix loop walks back up the propagation chain with last_source = last_source->mnt_master. It stops only when last_dest->mnt_master equals p, and it never checks whether it has reached first_source. When the first propagated copy is a slave, this walk runs past first_source. last_source->mnt_master then becomes NULL and is dereferenced. The fix replaces the loop with one that stops at first_source and compares the parent's master instead.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2016-2487): setDecodeArgs() sets the decoder output plane pointers into outHeader->pBuffer (Y, then UV at pBuf+sizeY and pBuf+sizeY+sizeUV) without checking that outHeader->nAllocLen is at least sizeY + 2*sizeUV, so the decoder writes past the end of an undersized client-supplied output buffer.

review.ground_truth: setDecodeArgs() sets the decoder output plane pointers into outHeader->pBuffer (Y, then UV at pBuf+sizeY and pBuf+sizeY+sizeUV) without checking that outHeader->nAllocLen is at least sizeY + 2*sizeUV, so the decoder writes past the end of an undersized client-supplied output buffer.
review.reasoning: The function hands outHeader->pBuffer to the HEVC decoder as Y/U/V output planes of total size sizeY*1.5. It never checks outHeader->nAllocLen against that size. A crafted app can supply a small OMX output buffer, and the decoder then writes past its end. The fix adds exactly this nAllocLen check, so the flaw is real and present in the shown code.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2022-47519): In wilc_wfi_cfg_parse_ch_attr(), op_ch_idx is accepted for an IEEE80211_P2P_ATTR_OPER_CHANNEL attribute without validating that attr_len (and len) covers a struct wilc_attr_oper_ch, so the writes to op_ch->op_class/op_ch->op_channel can go past the end of buf.

review.ground_truth: In wilc_wfi_cfg_parse_ch_attr(), op_ch_idx is accepted for an IEEE80211_P2P_ATTR_OPER_CHANNEL attribute without validating that attr_len (and len) covers a struct wilc_attr_oper_ch, so the writes to op_ch->op_class/op_ch->op_channel can go past the end of buf.
review.reasoning: The parsing loop records op_ch_idx for an IEEE80211_P2P_ATTR_OPER_CHANNEL attribute without checking that its attr_len, or the remaining buffer, can hold a struct wilc_attr_oper_ch. The function then writes op_ch->op_class and op_ch->op_channel at that offset. A short attribute placed at the end of the frame makes these writes land past the buffer. The fix adds the attribute length validation that closes this.

description:
CWE-125: Out-of-bounds Read
This instance (CVE-2019-5718): In get_t61_string(), when the current byte *c is a T.61 diacritic ((*c & 0xf0) == 0xc0), c[1] is read without checking i < length - 1, so a trailing diacritic byte causes a one-byte read past the end of ptr.

review.ground_truth: In get_t61_string(), when the current byte *c is a T.61 diacritic ((*c & 0xf0) == 0xc0), c[1] is read without checking i < length - 1, so a trailing diacritic byte causes a one-byte read past the end of ptr.
review.reasoning: In the loop, when *c is a combining diacritic (0xC0-0xCF), the code reads c[1] without checking that i+1 < length. If the last byte of the buffer is a diacritic, c[1] reads one byte past the end of ptr. The fix adds the i < length - 1 guard, which confirms an out-of-bounds read in this function.

description:
CWE-125: Out-of-bounds Read
This instance (CVE-2019-7153): In processFunctions(), the function export index taken from exportIndexes[curr] is passed to getFunctionIndexName() without checking it against wasm.functions.size(), so a crafted index reads past the functions vector and dereferences an invalid or null Function pointer.

review.ground_truth: In processFunctions(), the function export index taken from exportIndexes[curr] is passed to getFunctionIndexName() without checking it against wasm.functions.size(), so a crafted index reads past the functions vector and dereferences an invalid or null Function pointer.
review.reasoning: The fix adds a bounds check on the function export index before it is passed to getFunctionIndexName(). That callee indexes wasm.functions[index] and dereferences the element's name. A crafted binary can supply an export index past the end of the vector. The result is an out-of-bounds read of the vector whose garbage or null pointer is then dereferenced, which the CVE reports as a NULL dereference. The root cause is the missing index validation in this function.

description:
CWE-125: Out-of-bounds Read
This instance (CVE-2019-1000006): _skip_hostname() advances bufpos by attacker-controlled label length bytes (*bufpos + 1) and dereferences it without any bound on the packet length, reading past the end of the received DNS buffer.

review.ground_truth: _skip_hostname() advances bufpos by attacker-controlled label length bytes (*bufpos + 1) and dereferences it without any bound on the packet length, reading past the end of the received DNS buffer.
review.reasoning: _skip_hostname walks the DNS name labels by adding each label length byte to bufpos. It never checks against the end of the received buffer, so a malicious response makes it read past the buffer. The function itself only reads; any overflow happens in the caller, which uses the returned length. The root cause here is the unbounded read, so this is an out-of-bounds read rather than the labelled CWE-787 write.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2018-20760): The return value of gf_utf8_wcstombs() (which can be -1 or reach the buffer size) is cast to u32 and used unchecked as the index in szLineConv[i] = 0, writing out of bounds of the 1024-byte stack buffer.

review.ground_truth: The return value of gf_utf8_wcstombs() (which can be -1 or reach the buffer size) is cast to u32 and used unchecked as the index in szLineConv[i] = 0, writing out of bounds of the 1024-byte stack buffer.
review.reasoning: gf_utf8_wcstombs() can return -1 on a conversion error, and it may also return the full 1024 buffer length. The result is cast to u32 and used directly as the index in szLineConv[i] = 0. A -1 becomes 0xFFFFFFFF, so the write lands far outside the stack buffer; a return of 1024 is an off-by-one write. The fix adds a bounds check on i before the write. Separately, the non-UTF8 branch can expand each byte into two in szLineConv (up to about 2*lineSize) with no bound against its 1024-byte size, which is an additional evident overflow.

description:
CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference
This instance (CVE-2019-9208): In dissect_tcap_AUDT_application_context_name(), p_tcap_private (taken from actx->value_ptr) is dereferenced to set ->oid and ->acv without a NULL check, so a malformed packet that leaves value_ptr NULL causes a NULL pointer write.

review.ground_truth: In dissect_tcap_AUDT_application_context_name(), p_tcap_private (taken from actx->value_ptr) is dereferenced to set ->oid and ->acv without a NULL check, so a malformed packet that leaves value_ptr NULL causes a NULL pointer write.
review.reasoning: The function reads actx->value_ptr into p_tcap_private and then writes its oid and acv fields without checking it for NULL. With malformed packets value_ptr can be NULL, and the ASAN trace shows a write at offset 0x8. The fix adds exactly this NULL check. The trace names the AARQ variant, but the same fix guards this AUDT variant identically.

description:
CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference
This instance (CVE-2019-9208): In dissect_tcap_AARQ_application_context_name(), p_tcap_private (taken from actx->value_ptr) is dereferenced to write ->oid and ->acv without a NULL check, crashing when value_ptr was not set for a malformed packet.

review.ground_truth: In dissect_tcap_AARQ_application_context_name(), p_tcap_private (taken from actx->value_ptr) is dereferenced to write ->oid and ->acv without a NULL check, crashing when value_ptr was not set for a malformed packet.
review.reasoning: The function takes p_tcap_private from actx->value_ptr and then writes its oid and acv fields with no NULL check. The ASAN trace shows a WRITE to address 0x8 in exactly this function, which matches writing to a field of a NULL struct. The fix wraps the writes in a NULL check. The pointer can be NULL when the dissector is reached through a path that never set value_ptr, such as a malformed packet, so seeing that it can be NULL partly depends on the callers.

description:
CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference
This instance (CVE-2019-9208): In dissect_tcap_AARE_application_context_name(), p_tcap_private (taken from actx->value_ptr) is dereferenced to set oid and acv without a NULL check, crashing when no TCAP private data was set for a malformed packet.

review.ground_truth: In dissect_tcap_AARE_application_context_name(), p_tcap_private (taken from actx->value_ptr) is dereferenced to set oid and acv without a NULL check, crashing when no TCAP private data was set for a malformed packet.
review.reasoning: The function takes p_tcap_private from actx->value_ptr and writes its oid and acv fields without a NULL check. value_ptr can be NULL for malformed packets. The ASAN trace points at the AARQ variant, but the same fix adds the identical check here in the AARE variant, so the same flaw is present in this function. Whether value_ptr can be NULL depends on the caller's setup, so seeing it requires a reasonable assumption about callers.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2019-11221): gf_bt_report() uses vsprintf() to format caller-supplied format/arguments (possibly containing parsed file strings) into the fixed 2048-byte stack buffer szMsg with no length limit, allowing a stack buffer overflow.

review.ground_truth: gf_bt_report() uses vsprintf() to format caller-supplied format/arguments (possibly containing parsed file strings) into the fixed 2048-byte stack buffer szMsg with no length limit, allowing a stack buffer overflow.
review.reasoning: The CVE names gf_import_message() in media_import.c, but the fix commit replaced vsprintf with vsnprintf in several functions, and gf_bt_report() has the same pattern. It formats a caller-supplied format string and varargs into the fixed 2048-byte stack buffer szMsg with unbounded vsprintf. Callers pass strings taken from the parsed BT/WRL file, so long input could overflow szMsg. Whether real inputs can exceed 2048 bytes depends on the callers (tokens may be length-limited), but the fix addresses exactly this unbounded write.

description:
CWE-362: Concurrent Execution using Shared Resource with Improper Synchronization ('Race Condition')
This instance (CVE-2014-1832): verifyDirectoryPermissions() performs its own symlink-following stat(path) separately from the caller's earlier lstat check, creating a TOCTOU window where a local attacker can replace the server instance directory with a symlink so that checks pass on a different target.

review.ground_truth: verifyDirectoryPermissions() performs its own symlink-following stat(path) separately from the caller's earlier lstat check, creating a TOCTOU window where a local attacker can replace the server instance directory with a symlink so that checks pass on a different target.
review.reasoning: The earlier fix had the caller lstat() the instance directory to reject symlinks, and then this function did its own separate stat() on the same path. stat() follows symlinks, so an attacker can swap the directory for a symlink between the two calls and pass the permission and owner checks against an attacker-chosen target. The fix removes the second stat() and checks the caller's lstat buffer instead, which closes the TOCTOU window that lives in this function.

description:
CWE-125: Out-of-bounds Read
This instance (CVE-2015-1224): CopyAPlane() reads vpx_image_alpha->planes[VPX_PLANE_Y] using vpx_image->stride[VPX_PLANE_Y] and vpx_image->d_h instead of the alpha image's own stride and height, so an alpha plane that is smaller or has a smaller stride is read out of bounds.

review.ground_truth: CopyAPlane() reads vpx_image_alpha->planes[VPX_PLANE_Y] using vpx_image->stride[VPX_PLANE_Y] and vpx_image->d_h instead of the alpha image's own stride and height, so an alpha plane that is smaller or has a smaller stride is read out of bounds.
review.reasoning: CopyAPlane reads the alpha plane buffer (vpx_image_alpha->planes[VPX_PLANE_Y]) using the main image's Y stride and d_h rather than the alpha image's own stride and height. A crafted VP8 stream with a smaller alpha plane, or one with a smaller stride, therefore makes the copy read past the end of the alpha buffer. The fix switches to the alpha image's own stride and height, and VpxDecode now rejects mismatched dimensions. The missing size check sits in the caller, but the mismatched read is plainly visible in this function.

description:
CWE-908: Use of Uninitialized Resource
This instance (CVE-2015-2044): When bytes != 1, handle_pit_io() returns X86EMUL_OKAY without setting *val, so a guest read of the wrong size gets back uninitialized hypervisor memory.

review.ground_truth: When bytes != 1, handle_pit_io() returns X86EMUL_OKAY without setting *val, so a guest read of the wrong size gets back uninitialized hypervisor memory.
review.reasoning: On a wrong-sized access (bytes != 1), handle_pit_io returns X86EMUL_OKAY without writing *val. For a read, the uninitialized value is then handed back to the guest, leaking hypervisor stack data. The fix sets *val = ~0 in that path. Note that the (port & 3) == 3 read path also leaves *val unset, but the diff addresses the bad-size case.

description:
CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference
This instance (CVE-2015-0289): PKCS7_dataVerify() dereferences p7->d.sign->cert / p7->d.signed_and_enveloped->cert without checking that p7->d.ptr is non-NULL, so a PKCS#7 structure with missing outer content causes a NULL pointer dereference.

review.ground_truth: PKCS7_dataVerify() dereferences p7->d.sign->cert / p7->d.signed_and_enveloped->cert without checking that p7->d.ptr is non-NULL, so a PKCS#7 structure with missing outer content causes a NULL pointer dereference.
review.reasoning: PKCS#7 content is optional in the ASN.1 encoding, so a parsed PKCS7 can have p7->d.ptr == NULL. PKCS7_dataVerify checks only the type and then dereferences p7->d.sign->cert or p7->d.signed_and_enveloped->cert with no NULL check. The fix adds checks for p7 == NULL and p7->d.ptr == NULL before those dereferences, which matches the CVE's NULL pointer dereference.

description:
CWE-416: Use After Free
This instance (CVE-2015-1237): frameDetached() calls frame->close() to destroy the WebFrame but does not clear the member frame_, leaving a dangling pointer that OnMessageReceived later dereferences when IPC messages arrive during or after detach.

review.ground_truth: frameDetached() calls frame->close() to destroy the WebFrame but does not clear the member frame_, leaving a dangling pointer that OnMessageReceived later dereferences when IPC messages arrive during or after detach.
review.reasoning: In frameDetached(), frame->close() destroys the WebFrame, but the main-frame RenderFrameImpl is not deleted and its frame_ member still points at the freed frame. When OnMessageReceived later handles an IPC message, it dereferences that stale frame_ pointer. The fix sets frame_ = nullptr right after close(). This function is where the dangling pointer is created, and it is a genuine half of the use-after-free; the dereference itself happens in OnMessageReceived.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2015-3456): In fdctrl_write_data() the command/parameter path writes fdctrl->fifo[fdctrl->data_pos++] = value without bounding data_pos to FD_SECTOR_LEN, so guest writes for commands like READ_ID or DRIVE_SPECIFICATION run past the fifo buffer.

review.ground_truth: In fdctrl_write_data() the command/parameter path writes fdctrl->fifo[fdctrl->data_pos++] = value without bounding data_pos to FD_SECTOR_LEN, so guest writes for commands like READ_ID or DRIVE_SPECIFICATION run past the fifo buffer.
review.reasoning: This is the VENOM bug. In command/parameter mode the function writes fdctrl->fifo[fdctrl->data_pos++] = value with no bound on data_pos. Some commands (READ_ID, DRIVE_SPECIFICATION) leave data_pos/data_len in a state where the guest keeps writing past the 512-byte FIFO, so guest-controlled bytes overwrite adjacent heap memory. The fix reduces the index modulo FD_SECTOR_LEN; the int-to-uint32_t change for pos is a side detail, not the root cause.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2015-1252): DoWrite() calls memcpy(dest, src, num) without bounding num by the remaining buffer space (data_size_ - position_) or handling wrap, so a large write from Write() overflows buffer_data_->data.

review.ground_truth: DoWrite() calls memcpy(dest, src, num) without bounding num by the remaining buffer space (data_size_ - position_) or handling wrap, so a large write from Write() overflows buffer_data_->data.
review.reasoning: The pre-fix DoWrite copies num bytes to dest with no check against the remaining space in the buffer (data_size_ - position_). When Write() passes a write larger than what is left after a wrap, the memcpy runs past the end of buffer_data_->data. The fix moves the wrap and space_left bounding into DoWrite itself, which confirms this memcpy is where the out-of-bounds write happens. The faulty size and dest come from the caller, Write().

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2015-2666): The while loop in get_matching_model_microcode() calls _save_mc(mc_saved_tmp, ucode_ptr, &mc_saved_count) without checking mc_saved_count against ARRAY_SIZE(mc_saved_tmp), so crafted microcode with many matching patches writes past the on-stack mc_saved_tmp array.

review.ground_truth: The while loop in get_matching_model_microcode() calls _save_mc(mc_saved_tmp, ucode_ptr, &mc_saved_count) without checking mc_saved_count against ARRAY_SIZE(mc_saved_tmp), so crafted microcode with many matching patches writes past the on-stack mc_saved_tmp array.
review.reasoning: The while loop in get_matching_model_microcode() keeps calling _save_mc() for every matching microcode patch in the initrd. It never checks mc_saved_count against MAX_UCODE_COUNT, the size of the on-stack array mc_saved_tmp. _save_mc() appends a new entry at mc_saved_tmp[mc_saved_count] whenever the patch is not a replacement, so a crafted initrd with many distinct matching patches writes past the stack array. The fix adds exactly that bound to the loop condition.

description:
CWE-416: Use After Free
This instance (CVE-2015-1277): SerializeChangedNodes() iterates the cached `children` vector from tree_->GetChildren() and calls tree_->GetId(child) and recursively serializes each child without checking tree_->IsValid(child), so accessibility objects destroyed during serialization are used after free.

review.ground_truth: SerializeChangedNodes() iterates the cached `children` vector from tree_->GetChildren() and calls tree_->GetId(child) and recursively serializes each child without checking tree_->IsValid(child), so accessibility objects destroyed during serialization are used after free.
review.reasoning: The fix adds a tree_->IsValid(child) check right before each child is used, and moves the recursive serialization into the loop. That only makes sense if the cached children vector can hold accessibility objects that became invalid or were destroyed after GetChildren() returned, for example because serializing the node or a sibling triggers layout or tree changes. The pre-fix code trusts the cached list and calls GetId() and SerializeChangedNodes() on those stale objects, which is a use-after-free. Seeing this requires knowing that SerializeNode or recursion can invalidate source objects.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2014-9731): udf_pc_to_char() writes symlink path components ("/", "../", "./", and udf_get_filename output plus '/') into the 'to' buffer without tracking or checking its remaining length, so a crafted symlink overflows the destination page.

review.ground_truth: udf_pc_to_char() writes symlink path components ("/", "../", "./", and udf_get_filename output plus '/') into the 'to' buffer without tracking or checking its remaining length, so a crafted symlink overflows the destination page.
review.reasoning: udf_pc_to_char writes the decoded path components into the 'to' page buffer with no length limit at all. A crafted symlink made of many "../" components or long names can write past the end of the page. CWE-17 is a generic, deprecated label; the root cause is an out-of-bounds write. The flaw is visible here because the function never receives or checks a destination size.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2011-4128): gnutls_session_get_data() overwrites *session_data_size with psession.size before the bounds check, making the check ineffective, so memcpy(session_data, psession.data, psession.size) overflows the caller's buffer when the packed session (e.g. large SessionTicket) exceeds its real size.

review.ground_truth: gnutls_session_get_data() overwrites *session_data_size with psession.size before the bounds check, making the check ineffective, so memcpy(session_data, psession.data, psession.size) overflows the caller's buffer when the packed session (e.g. large SessionTicket) exceeds its real size.
review.reasoning: The function assigns *session_data_size = psession.size before the size check, so the check psession.size > *session_data_size is always false. The memcpy then copies the full packed session, which can contain a large server-controlled SessionTicket, into the caller's buffer of the original smaller size. The fix moves the assignment to after the check, so this is a genuine heap/stack buffer overflow.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2013-2850): In iscsi_add_notunderstood_response(), strncpy(extra_response->key, key, strlen(key) + 1) copies an attacker-controlled key of unchecked length into the fixed-size key array, overflowing the heap-allocated iscsi_extra_response.

review.ground_truth: In iscsi_add_notunderstood_response(), strncpy(extra_response->key, key, strlen(key) + 1) copies an attacker-controlled key of unchecked length into the fixed-size key array, overflowing the heap-allocated iscsi_extra_response.
review.reasoning: The function copies the remote-supplied key into the fixed-size extra_response->key array with strncpy() bounded by strlen(key)+1, not by the destination size. A key longer than 64 bytes, which is only rejected elsewhere, overflows the kzalloc'd struct on the heap. The value is length-checked against VALUE_MAXLEN, but the key is not. This is a heap buffer overflow, which matches the fix that switches to strlcpy bounded by sizeof.

description:
CWE-908: Use of Uninitialized Resource
This instance (CVE-2018-9511): In ipSecSetEncapSocketOwner(), the local socklen_t optlen is passed uninitialized as the in/out length argument to getsockopt(UDP_ENCAP), so the call may fail or leave optval unset, and the UDP-encap check and fchown are skipped or behave unpredictably.

review.ground_truth: In ipSecSetEncapSocketOwner(), the local socklen_t optlen is passed uninitialized as the in/out length argument to getsockopt(UDP_ENCAP), so the call may fail or leave optval unset, and the UDP-encap check and fchown are skipped or behave unpredictably.
review.reasoning: optlen is passed to getsockopt uninitialized. getsockopt treats it as an input buffer length, so a garbage value (zero, negative or too small) can make the call fail or leave optval unset. optval is then compared against the encap constants, so the encap-socket ownership change can fail or behave unpredictably. That is the denial of IPsec described. The fix initializes optlen to sizeof(optval).

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2013-1929): In tg3_read_vpd(), the firmware-supplied VENDOR0 field length len is not limited to sizeof(tp->fw_ver), so memcpy(tp->fw_ver, &vpd_data[j], len) and the following strncat bounded by vpdlen - len - 1 overflow the 32-byte fw_ver buffer in the tg3 struct.

review.ground_truth: In tg3_read_vpd(), the firmware-supplied VENDOR0 field length len is not limited to sizeof(tp->fw_ver), so memcpy(tp->fw_ver, &vpd_data[j], len) and the following strncat bounded by vpdlen - len - 1 overflow the 32-byte fw_ver buffer in the tg3 struct.
review.reasoning: The VENDOR0 field length len comes from firmware (up to 255 bytes) and is only checked against block_end, not against sizeof(tp->fw_ver) (32 bytes). memcpy(tp->fw_ver, &vpd_data[j], len) can therefore write past the fw_ver array into the rest of the tg3 struct. The strncat that follows uses a bound based on vpdlen rather than the destination size, so it can overflow too. The fix clamps len to the buffer size and uses snprintf.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2016-1245): rtadv_read() passes BUFSIZ (system-dependent, e.g. 8192) as the length to rtadv_recv_packet() for the stack buffer buf sized RTADV_MSG_SIZE (4096), allowing a received ICMPv6 RS/RA packet to overflow the stack buffer.

review.ground_truth: rtadv_read() passes BUFSIZ (system-dependent, e.g. 8192) as the length to rtadv_recv_packet() for the stack buffer buf sized RTADV_MSG_SIZE (4096), allowing a received ICMPv6 RS/RA packet to overflow the stack buffer.
review.reasoning: The stack buffer buf is declared with RTADV_MSG_SIZE (4096) bytes, but rtadv_recv_packet is passed BUFSIZ as the receive length. BUFSIZ is 8192 on glibc. The kernel's recvmsg can therefore write up to 8192 bytes into the 4096-byte stack buffer, overflowing it. The fix passes sizeof(buf) instead, and the size mismatch is visible within this function.

description:
CWE-125: Out-of-bounds Read
This instance (CVE-2013-1798): In ioapic_read_indirect(), redir_index is derived from the guest-controlled ioapic->ioregsel and used to index ioapic->redirtbl[] with only a no-op ASSERT, allowing an out-of-bounds read past the redirection table.

review.ground_truth: In ioapic_read_indirect(), redir_index is derived from the guest-controlled ioapic->ioregsel and used to index ioapic->redirtbl[] with only a no-op ASSERT, allowing an out-of-bounds read past the redirection table.
review.reasoning: In the default case, redir_index is computed from the guest-controlled ioregsel. The only check on it is ASSERT(redir_index < IOAPIC_NUM_PINS), which compiles away in non-debug builds. The value then indexes ioapic->redirtbl, so a guest can read past the array and either leak host memory or oops the host. The fix replaces the ASSERT with a real bounds check.

description:
CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference
This instance (CVE-2013-1774): chase_port() dereferences tty (&tty->write_wait in add_wait_queue/remove_wait_queue) without checking that tty_port_tty_get() returned non-NULL, which happens when the port is hung up or disconnected.

review.ground_truth: chase_port() dereferences tty (&tty->write_wait in add_wait_queue/remove_wait_queue) without checking that tty_port_tty_get() returned non-NULL, which happens when the port is hung up or disconnected.
review.reasoning: tty_port_tty_get() returns NULL while the port is hanging up or the device is disconnected. chase_port() then uses tty->write_wait in add_wait_queue() without checking for NULL, which crashes the kernel. The fix adds that NULL check, so this is a real NULL pointer dereference; the CWE-264 label is wrong.

description:
CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference
This instance (CVE-2015-3194): In rsa_pss_decode(), param (pss->maskGenAlgorithm->parameter) is dereferenced via param->type without a NULL check when an MGF1 mask generation algorithm is supplied without parameters.

review.ground_truth: In rsa_pss_decode(), param (pss->maskGenAlgorithm->parameter) is dereferenced via param->type without a NULL check when an MGF1 mask generation algorithm is supplied without parameters.
review.reasoning: pss->maskGenAlgorithm->parameter is optional in ASN.1, so it can be NULL when the MGF1 algorithm has no parameters. The code dereferences param->type without checking for NULL. The fix adds exactly that check. The flaw is local and real.

description:
CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference
This instance (CVE-2015-3194): rsa_mgf1_decode() dereferences alg->parameter (alg->parameter->type) without checking it for NULL, so a PSS signature whose MGF1 AlgorithmIdentifier omits the parameter crashes.

review.ground_truth: rsa_mgf1_decode() dereferences alg->parameter (alg->parameter->type) without checking it for NULL, so a PSS signature whose MGF1 AlgorithmIdentifier omits the parameter crashes.
review.reasoning: The function dereferences alg->parameter->type without checking that alg->parameter is non-NULL. An optional ASN.1 parameter that is absent from the MGF1 AlgorithmIdentifier in a PSS signature leaves the pointer NULL. The fix adds exactly that check, so the shown code contains the real flaw.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2011-1180): In iriap_getvaluebyclass_indication(), the peer-supplied name_len and attr_len bytes (up to 255) are passed to memcpy into the 60-byte stack arrays name[] and attr[], and used as the index for the NUL terminator, without any bound check, causing a stack buffer overflow.

review.ground_truth: In iriap_getvaluebyclass_indication(), the peer-supplied name_len and attr_len bytes (up to 255) are passed to memcpy into the 60-byte stack arrays name[] and attr[], and used as the index for the NUL terminator, without any bound check, causing a stack buffer overflow.
review.reasoning: name_len and attr_len come from the peer as single bytes, so each can be up to 255. They are used in memcpy into the stack arrays name[60] and attr[60] with no check against the array sizes, which overflows the stack. The fix adds bound checks before each copy. The memcpy also reads from skb->data without checking skb->len, which is an evident out-of-bounds read on the source side as well.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2014-8884): memcpy(&b[4], cmd->msg, cmd->msg_len) copies a user-controlled msg_len into the 10-byte stack array b without checking that msg_len <= 6, overflowing the stack buffer.

review.ground_truth: memcpy(&b[4], cmd->msg, cmd->msg_len) copies a user-controlled msg_len into the 10-byte stack array b without checking that msg_len <= 6, overflowing the stack buffer.
review.reasoning: The stack array b is 10 bytes long, and the function copies cmd->msg_len bytes into it starting at &b[4]. msg_len comes from the user's ioctl and is never checked, so any value above 6 writes past the end of b on the stack. The fix adds the missing bound check. This is a genuine stack buffer overflow, and it is visible within this function alone.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2014-3184): ch_report_fixup() checks *rsize >= 17 but then writes rdesc[17], an off-by-one out-of-bounds write when the report descriptor is exactly 17 bytes.

review.ground_truth: ch_report_fixup() checks *rsize >= 17 but then writes rdesc[17], an off-by-one out-of-bounds write when the report descriptor is exactly 17 bytes.
review.reasoning: The check `*rsize >= 17` lets through a 17-byte descriptor. The function then writes rdesc[17], one byte past the end of that buffer. This is an off-by-one in the bounds check that causes an out-of-bounds write, and the fix changes the check to >= 18.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2014-3184): pl_report_fixup() checks only *rsize >= 60 yet reads rdesc[60]/rdesc[61] and writes rdesc[60], so a 60- or 61-byte report descriptor is accessed and written past its end (off-by-one size check).
fix_diff:
--- vulnerable
+++ fixed
@@ -2,5 +2,5 @@
  		unsigned int *rsize)
  {
-	if (*rsize >= 60 && rdesc[39] == 0x2a && rdesc[40] == 0xf5 &&
+	if (*rsize >= 62 && rdesc[39] == 0x2a && rdesc[40] == 0xf5 &&
  			rdesc[41] == 0x00 && rdesc[59] == 0x26 &&
  			rdesc[60] == 0xf9 && rdesc[61] == 0x00) {

review.ground_truth: pl_report_fixup() checks only *rsize >= 60 yet reads rdesc[60]/rdesc[61] and writes rdesc[60], so a 60- or 61-byte report descriptor is accessed and written past its end (off-by-one size check).
review.reasoning: The size check is *rsize >= 60, but the code then reads rdesc[60] and rdesc[61] and writes rdesc[60]. A 60- or 61-byte descriptor passes the check and is accessed past its end. The fix raises the check to >= 62. The write to rdesc[60] is the out-of-bounds write described in the CVE; the reads come from the same insufficient check.

description:
CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference
This instance (CVE-2013-7339): In rds_ib_laddr_check(), cm_id->device is dereferenced (cm_id->device->node_type) after a successful rdma_bind_addr() without checking that it is non-NULL, though binding can leave the device NULL.
fix_diff:
--- vulnerable
+++ fixed
@@ -20,5 +20,6 @@
  	/* due to this, we will claim to support iWARP devices unless we
  	   check node_type. */
-	if (ret || cm_id->device->node_type != RDMA_NODE_IB_CA)
+	if (ret || !cm_id->device ||
+	    cm_id->device->node_type != RDMA_NODE_IB_CA)
  		ret = -EADDRNOTAVAIL;

review.ground_truth: In rds_ib_laddr_check(), cm_id->device is dereferenced (cm_id->device->node_type) after a successful rdma_bind_addr() without checking that it is non-NULL, though binding can leave the device NULL.
review.reasoning: After rdma_bind_addr() succeeds, cm_id->device can still be NULL, for example when binding to an address with no RDMA device behind it. The condition then dereferences cm_id->device->node_type without a NULL check. The fix adds that check. The source label CWE-399 is generic; the real mechanism is a NULL pointer dereference (CWE-476).

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2017-9618): xps_load_sfnt_name() copies a font-controlled record length (u16(record+8)) of bytes into the fixed-size namep buffer via memcpy/namep[length] and the namep[k] loops without bounding length to the buffer size, overflowing namep.

review.ground_truth: xps_load_sfnt_name() copies a font-controlled record length (u16(record+8)) of bytes into the fixed-size namep buffer via memcpy/namep[length] and the namep[k] loops without bounding length to the buffer size, overflowing namep.
review.reasoning: The fix adds a buflen parameter and clamps the per-record length to buflen-1. Before the fix, the attacker-controlled 16-bit length from each name record is used directly to copy into the fixed-size caller buffer namep: via memcpy(namep, ..., length), namep[length]=0, and the UCS-2/UCS-4 loops writing namep[k]. That is a stack/heap buffer overflow (write) in this function. The source of each copy (namedata + stringoffset + offset) is also not bounds-checked against font->length, which is a separate out-of-bounds read the fix does not address.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2015-6031): IGDstartelt() memcpy's the XML element name of length l into the fixed-size datas->cureltname and writes cureltname[l]='\0' without checking l against MINIUPNPC_URL_MAXSIZE, so an oversized element name overflows the buffer.

review.ground_truth: IGDstartelt() memcpy's the XML element name of length l into the fixed-size datas->cureltname and writes cureltname[l]='\0' without checking l against MINIUPNPC_URL_MAXSIZE, so an oversized element name overflows the buffer.
review.reasoning: IGDstartelt copies the element name into the fixed-size cureltname buffer with memcpy using the attacker-controlled length l, and then writes a terminator at cureltname[l]. Nothing bounds l in this function. The fix clamps l to MINIUPNPC_URL_MAXSIZE-1, which confirms a stack/struct buffer overflow (out-of-bounds write) present in the code as shown.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2015-2666): The while loop in get_matching_model_microcode() keeps calling _save_mc() to append patches into the fixed-size stack array mc_saved_tmp[MAX_UCODE_COUNT] without checking that mc_saved_count stays below the array size, so a crafted initrd with many matching patches overflows the stack.

review.ground_truth: The while loop in get_matching_model_microcode() keeps calling _save_mc() to append patches into the fixed-size stack array mc_saved_tmp[MAX_UCODE_COUNT] without checking that mc_saved_count stays below the array size, so a crafted initrd with many matching patches overflows the stack.
review.reasoning: The loop over the initrd microcode blob calls _save_mc(mc_saved_tmp, ucode_ptr, &mc_saved_count) for every matching-model patch. Nothing caps mc_saved_count at MAX_UCODE_COUNT, so a blob with many matching patches writes past the end of the stack array mc_saved_tmp. The fix adds a bounds condition to the loop. Seeing the write requires knowing that _save_mc appends at index mc_saved_count, which is a reasonable assumption.

description:
CWE-125: Out-of-bounds Read
This instance (CVE-2014-9584): In the SIG('E','R') case, the loop prints rr->u.ER.data[p] for p < rr->u.ER.len_id without checking len_id against rr->len or the buffer size, reading kernel memory past the record.

review.ground_truth: In the SIG('E','R') case, the loop prints rr->u.ER.data[p] for p < rr->u.ER.len_id without checking len_id against rr->len or the buffer size, reading kernel memory past the record.
review.reasoning: In the ER case, the loop prints rr->u.ER.data[p] for p up to rr->u.ER.len_id, which comes from the image. It is never checked against rr->len or the remaining buffer. A crafted image can therefore make the kernel read and log memory past the rock ridge buffer. The fix adds a check that len_id plus the header fits within rr->len.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2016-7115): In handle_packet(), the MT_CPTYPE_PASSSALT branch calls memcpy(pass_salt, cpkt.data, cpkt.length) using the server-controlled cpkt.length without checking it against the 16-byte pass_salt buffer, causing a buffer overflow.

review.ground_truth: In handle_packet(), the MT_CPTYPE_PASSSALT branch calls memcpy(pass_salt, cpkt.data, cpkt.length) using the server-controlled cpkt.length without checking it against the 16-byte pass_salt buffer, causing a buffer overflow.
review.reasoning: In the MT_CPTYPE_PASSSALT branch, memcpy copies cpkt.length bytes, a length taken from the server's packet, into the fixed 16-byte global pass_salt with no bounds check. A malicious server can therefore overflow the buffer. The fix forces the copy to exactly 16 bytes. The flaw is visible in this function, given that pass_salt is a fixed 16-byte array.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2021-40568): In svc_parse_slice(), pps_id is only checked against an upper bound (>255) and not for negative values, so a negative pps_id indexes avc->pps[pps_id] out of bounds and si->pps->id is written outside the array.

review.ground_truth: In svc_parse_slice(), pps_id is only checked against an upper bound (>255) and not for negative values, so a negative pps_id indexes avc->pps[pps_id] out of bounds and si->pps->id is written outside the array.
review.reasoning: pps_id is a signed s32 holding the result of gf_bs_read_ue_log, which can come out negative for a malformed exp-Golomb code. The original check only rejects values above 255, so a negative pps_id passes. It is then used to index avc->pps and written through via si->pps->id, an out-of-bounds write. The fix adds the pps_id<0 check, which matches this flaw.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2021-40574): In gf_text_get_utf8_line(), the conversion loop writes szLineConv[j] with no check against the 1024-byte stack buffer while non-UTF8 high-bit bytes expand to two output bytes, so long lines overflow szLineConv.

review.ground_truth: In gf_text_get_utf8_line(), the conversion loop writes szLineConv[j] with no check against the 1024-byte stack buffer while non-UTF8 high-bit bytes expand to two output bytes, so long lines overflow szLineConv.
review.reasoning: The fix doubles the stack buffer szLineConv from 1024 to 2048. In the unicode_type<=1 path, each high-bit input byte from szLine (up to lineSize, often 2048 in callers) can emit two output bytes into szLineConv with no bound on j, so j can run past 1024 and overflow the stack buffer. The 'double free' in the CVE text is a downstream effect of the resulting memory corruption, not the root cause. The flaw is a real stack buffer overflow (oob_write), not CWE-415.

description:
CWE-125: Out-of-bounds Read
This instance (CVE-2021-29532): BuildFeatureReaders() indexes ragged_values_list/ragged_splits_list[next_ragged], sparse_indices_list/sparse_values_list[next_sparse] and dense_list[next_dense] according to the attacker-controlled input_order_ without checking the indices against the list sizes, causing a heap out-of-bounds read.

review.ground_truth: BuildFeatureReaders() indexes ragged_values_list/ragged_splits_list[next_ragged], sparse_indices_list/sparse_values_list[next_sparse] and dense_list[next_dense] according to the attacker-controlled input_order_ without checking the indices against the list sizes, causing a heap out-of-bounds read.
review.reasoning: The loop walks the user-supplied input_order_ string and indexes ragged_values_list, ragged_splits_list, sparse_indices_list, sparse_values_list and dense_list with the counters next_ragged, next_sparse and next_dense. Nothing checks those counters against the list sizes, so an attacker can make the kernel read past the heap-allocated input lists. The fix adds exactly these bounds checks. The source CWE-369 label is wrong: there is no division here, and the correct class is an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125).

description:
CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference
This instance (CVE-2020-23914): perform_core() does not reject a grammar whose start rule (grammar[data.start]) has ignoreSemanticValue set, so parsing yields a null AST that is later dereferenced in AstOptimizer::optimize().

review.ground_truth: perform_core() does not reject a grammar whose start rule (grammar[data.start]) has ignoreSemanticValue set, so parsing yields a null AST that is later dereferenced in AstOptimizer::optimize().
review.reasoning: The fix adds a check in perform_core() that rejects grammars whose start rule carries the '~' ignore operator. Without that check, such a grammar is accepted. Parsing then discards the start rule's semantic value, so the resulting AST root is null, and AstOptimizer::optimize() dereferences it. The dereference happens in another function, but the missing validation that the fix repairs lives here.

description:
CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference
This instance (CVE-2021-30015): av1dmx_parse_flush_sample() calls gf_filter_pck_new_alloc(ctx->opid, ...) without checking that ctx->opid is non-NULL, so the NULL output pid is dereferenced when no output PID was configured.

review.ground_truth: av1dmx_parse_flush_sample() calls gf_filter_pck_new_alloc(ctx->opid, ...) without checking that ctx->opid is non-NULL, so the NULL output pid is dereferenced when no output PID was configured.
review.reasoning: The function passes ctx->opid to gf_filter_pck_new_alloc without checking it. opid can be NULL when no sequence header was seen, so no output PID was created. The callee then dereferences the NULL pid and crashes. The fix adds a NULL check on ctx->opid, so this is a NULL dereference, not CWE-787.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2020-15007): M_LoadDefaults() calls fscanf with an unbounded "%[^\n]" conversion into the 100-byte stack buffer strparm, so a long config line overflows the stack.

review.ground_truth: M_LoadDefaults() calls fscanf with an unbounded "%[^\n]" conversion into the 100-byte stack buffer strparm, so a long config line overflows the stack.
review.reasoning: The format "%[^\n]" reads an unbounded line into the 100-byte stack buffer strparm, which is a stack buffer overflow. The fix adds a 99-character width limit. The function has other issues as well. The newstring = malloc(len) allocation with strcpy is fine in size, since strparm+1 has len-1 characters after the last one is zeroed. However, if len==1, then strparm[len-1] is strparm[0], which is still in bounds. scantokey[parm] indexes with a parm value taken from the config file and never checked, which is a possible OOB read.

description:
CWE-125: Out-of-bounds Read
This instance (CVE-2018-14017): In r_bin_java_line_number_table_attr_new the loop over the attacker-controlled line_number_table_length reads start_pc/line_number via R_BIN_JAVA_USHORT(buffer, offset) without checking offset against sz, causing a heap buffer over-read.

review.ground_truth: In r_bin_java_line_number_table_attr_new the loop over the attacker-controlled line_number_table_length reads start_pc/line_number via R_BIN_JAVA_USHORT(buffer, offset) without checking offset against sz, causing a heap buffer over-read.
review.reasoning: The function reads linenum_len (attacker-controlled) four-byte entries from buffer, but the only validation is linenum_len > sz. That check compares an entry count against the byte size, so a count up to sz still lets 4*count bytes be read past the end of the buffer. The loop never checks offset against sz before calling R_BIN_JAVA_USHORT, which gives a heap over-read. The fix adds a per-iteration offset bound check, so the flaw is in this function.

description:
CWE-416: Use After Free
This instance (CVE-2020-35980): CleanWriters() deletes writer->stco and writer->stsc with gf_isom_box_del() without first removing them from writer->stbl->child_boxes, leaving dangling pointers in the sample table that are later accessed or freed again when the write aborts mid-way.

review.ground_truth: CleanWriters() deletes writer->stco and writer->stsc with gf_isom_box_del() without first removing them from writer->stbl->child_boxes, leaving dangling pointers in the sample table that are later accessed or freed again when the write aborts mid-way.
review.reasoning: CleanWriters frees writer->stco and writer->stsc. These boxes may already have been inserted into writer->stbl->child_boxes during the file write. If the write fails partway, the sample table still holds pointers to the freed boxes, and they are freed or used again when the stbl is destroyed. The fix removes them from child_boxes before deleting them. This is a genuine use-after-free/double-free, rooted in a lifetime error in this function.

description:
CWE-125: Out-of-bounds Read
This instance (CVE-2021-31256): In the fast path where SampleToChunk->nb_entries equals SampleSize->sampleCount, stco->offsets[sampleNumber-1] and co64->offsets[sampleNumber-1] are read without checking sampleNumber against the chunk offset box's nb_entries, causing a heap out-of-bounds read.

review.ground_truth: In the fast path where SampleToChunk->nb_entries equals SampleSize->sampleCount, stco->offsets[sampleNumber-1] and co64->offsets[sampleNumber-1] are read without checking sampleNumber against the chunk offset box's nb_entries, causing a heap out-of-bounds read.
review.reasoning: The fix adds a bounds check on stco/co64 nb_entries before indexing offsets[sampleNumber-1] in the fast path, where the stsc entry count equals the sample count. That path never checks sampleNumber against the chunk offset table size, so a crafted file with fewer chunk offsets reads past the offsets array. The CVE's 'memory leak' wording and the CWE-416 label are both wrong; the root cause is an out-of-bounds heap read. The fast path also indexes SampleToChunk->entries[sampleNumber-1] without checking sampleNumber against sampleCount, which may be a further OOB read.

description:
CWE-125: Out-of-bounds Read
This instance (CVE-2017-14646): In AP4_AvccAtom's constructor, the sequence/picture parameter loops read param_length from the payload and call SetData(&payload[cursor]+2, param_length) without checking cursor+2+param_length against payload_size, causing a heap buffer over-read.

review.ground_truth: In AP4_AvccAtom's constructor, the sequence/picture parameter loops read param_length from the payload and call SetData(&payload[cursor]+2, param_length) without checking cursor+2+param_length against payload_size, causing a heap buffer over-read.
review.reasoning: The constructor reads param_length from the attacker-controlled payload and calls SetData(&payload[cursor]+2, param_length). It never checks cursor or cursor+param_length against payload_size, so SetData's memcpy reads past the heap payload buffer. The flaw is an over-read (CWE-125), not a write as the CWE-787 label claims. The fix adds bounds checks against payload_size.

description:
CWE-908: Use of Uninitialized Resource
This instance (CVE-2020-7042): ssl_verify_cert() passes the uninitialized stack buffer common_name as the hostname to X509_check_host() instead of tunnel->config->gateway_host, so the certificate hostname check runs on uninitialized memory.

review.ground_truth: ssl_verify_cert() passes the uninitialized stack buffer common_name as the hostname to X509_check_host() instead of tunnel->config->gateway_host, so the certificate hostname check runs on uninitialized memory.
review.reasoning: In the HAVE_X509_CHECK_HOST branch, X509_check_host() is passed the stack buffer common_name, which is never initialized, instead of tunnel->config->gateway_host. The hostname check therefore compares the certificate against garbage. A valid certificate fails the check, and a malformed one might match. This is visible within the function itself. The root cause is uninitialized memory use, and its consequence is improper certificate hostname validation (CWE-295).

description:
CWE-401: Missing Release of Memory after Effective Lifetime (memory leak)
This instance (CVE-2021-39176): The UCharsetDetector allocated by ucsdet_open() in DetectCharacterEncoding is never released with ucsdet_close(), on either the error-return paths or the success path, leaking memory on every call.

review.ground_truth: The UCharsetDetector allocated by ucsdet_open() in DetectCharacterEncoding is never released with ucsdet_close(), on either the error-return paths or the success path, leaking memory on every call.
review.reasoning: The function opens an ICU charset detector with ucsdet_open() and never calls ucsdet_close(). It leaks on every error path after the open, and also on the success path. Each call leaks memory, so a caller who keeps invoking it can exhaust memory. This matches the fix commit, which adds proper closing of charsetDetector.

description:
CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference
This instance (CVE-2020-13848): FindServiceEventURLPath() calls strlen(eventURLPath) and parse_uri() without checking that eventURLPath is non-NULL, so a crafted request that yields a NULL path causes a NULL pointer dereference.

review.ground_truth: FindServiceEventURLPath() calls strlen(eventURLPath) and parse_uri() without checking that eventURLPath is non-NULL, so a crafted request that yields a NULL path causes a NULL pointer dereference.
review.reasoning: The fix adds a NULL check for eventURLPath before strlen() and parse_uri(). The pre-fix code passes eventURLPath straight to strlen(). A crafted SSDP/GENA request can leave that path NULL in the caller, which crashes the process. The CVE explicitly names FindServiceEventURLPath as the dual of the FindServiceControlURLPath bug.

description:
CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference
This instance (CVE-2020-13848): FindServiceControlURLPath() passes controlURLPath to strlen() and parse_uri() without checking it for NULL, so a crafted request supplying a NULL control URL path causes a NULL pointer dereference.

review.ground_truth: FindServiceControlURLPath() passes controlURLPath to strlen() and parse_uri() without checking it for NULL, so a crafted request supplying a NULL control URL path causes a NULL pointer dereference.
review.reasoning: The function calls strlen(controlURLPath) and parse_uri on controlURLPath without first checking it for NULL. A crafted request can reach this code with a NULL path, and the strlen call then crashes. The fix adds a !controlURLPath check. The flaw is visible locally, though knowing that callers can pass NULL is an assumption about the calling code.

description:
CWE-416: Use After Free
This instance (CVE-2021-38383): In net_bind(), after freeaddrinfo(servinfo) frees the list, ptr->ai_addr and ptr->ai_addrlen are still read and written via getsockname(), net_port_get() and net_address_get().

review.ground_truth: In net_bind(), after freeaddrinfo(servinfo) frees the list, ptr->ai_addr and ptr->ai_addrlen are still read and written via getsockname(), net_port_get() and net_address_get().
review.reasoning: freeaddrinfo(servinfo) frees the whole addrinfo list, including the node ptr points to. The code then still uses ptr->ai_addr and ptr->ai_addrlen in getsockname(), net_port_get() and net_address_get(), which is a clear use-after-free visible in this function alone. The fix replaces those uses with a local net_sockaddr.

description:
CWE-401: Missing Release of Memory after Effective Lifetime (memory leak)
This instance (CVE-2019-19067): In acp_hw_init(), error returns after mfd_add_hotplug_devices() or pm_genpd_add_device() failure, after a soft-reset/clock timeout, or after a later kcalloc failure return without kfree'ing adev->acp.acp_genpd, acp_cell, acp_res and i2s_pdata, leaking them.

review.ground_truth: In acp_hw_init(), error returns after mfd_add_hotplug_devices() or pm_genpd_add_device() failure, after a soft-reset/clock timeout, or after a later kcalloc failure return without kfree'ing adev->acp.acp_genpd, acp_cell, acp_res and i2s_pdata, leaking them.
review.reasoning: The function allocates acp_genpd, acp_cell, acp_res and i2s_pdata, but several error returns skip freeing them. If acp_cell allocation fails, acp_genpd leaks. If acp_res or i2s_pdata allocation fails, acp_genpd also leaks. If mfd_add_hotplug_devices or pm_genpd_add_device fails, or either timeout loop expires, all four buffers leak. The fix adds a common failure label that frees all of them, so this is a genuine memory leak present in the shown code.

description:
CWE-362: Concurrent Execution using Shared Resource with Improper Synchronization ('Race Condition')
This instance (CVE-2022-3303): snd_pcm_oss_sync() calls snd_pcm_oss_make_ready() outside runtime->oss.params_lock and only takes the mutex afterwards, so a concurrent stream re-setup in that window leaves runtime->oss.buffer/params inconsistent (e.g. NULL) when they are used under the lock.

review.ground_truth: snd_pcm_oss_sync() calls snd_pcm_oss_make_ready() outside runtime->oss.params_lock and only takes the mutex afterwards, so a concurrent stream re-setup in that window leaves runtime->oss.buffer/params inconsistent (e.g. NULL) when they are used under the lock.
review.reasoning: snd_pcm_oss_sync() calls snd_pcm_oss_make_ready() before taking runtime->oss.params_lock. Another thread can reconfigure the stream in that gap, so the code under the lock works on inconsistent state, for example a NULL runtime->oss.buffer. The fix moves the make_ready call inside the mutex using the _locked variant. This is a genuine locking race (TOCTOU) in this function, so the CWE-362 label holds.

description:
CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference
This instance (CVE-2019-15219): In sisusb_probe(), when usb_register_dev() fails, the error path calls dev_err(&sisusb->sisusb_dev->dev, ...) while sisusb->sisusb_dev is still NULL (from kzalloc), because it is only assigned after registration.

review.ground_truth: In sisusb_probe(), when usb_register_dev() fails, the error path calls dev_err(&sisusb->sisusb_dev->dev, ...) while sisusb->sisusb_dev is still NULL (from kzalloc), because it is only assigned after registration.
review.reasoning: sisusb is allocated with kzalloc, so sisusb->sisusb_dev is NULL at the time of the usb_register_dev() call. If registration fails, the error path runs dev_err(&sisusb->sisusb_dev->dev, ...), which dereferences that NULL pointer. The fix moves the assignment of sisusb_dev ahead of registration, so the flaw is real and visible in this function alone.

description:
CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference
This instance (CVE-2019-19925): In zipfileUpdate(), zPath from sqlite3_value_text(apVal[2]) is NULL when the inserted name is NULL, and it is passed to strlen() and dereferenced (zPath[nPath-1]) without a NULL check.

review.ground_truth: In zipfileUpdate(), zPath from sqlite3_value_text(apVal[2]) is NULL when the inserted name is NULL, and it is passed to strlen() and dereferenced (zPath[nPath-1]) without a NULL check.
review.reasoning: In the insert/update branch, zPath = sqlite3_value_text(apVal[2]) can return NULL when the inserted name is NULL. The code then calls strlen(zPath) right away and later indexes zPath[nPath-1], with no NULL check. The fix makes zPath an empty string when it is NULL. The CWE-434 label (unrestricted file upload) is wrong; the real flaw is a NULL pointer dereference (CWE-476).

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2020-0110): psi_write() writes buf[buf_size - 1] = '\0' without checking that buf_size (min(nbytes, sizeof(buf))) is non-zero, so a zero-byte write stores out of bounds of the stack buffer buf.

review.ground_truth: psi_write() writes buf[buf_size - 1] = '\0' without checking that buf_size (min(nbytes, sizeof(buf))) is non-zero, so a zero-byte write stores out of bounds of the stack buffer buf.
review.reasoning: When nbytes is 0, buf_size is 0 and buf[buf_size - 1] wraps to buf[SIZE_MAX], a write far outside the 32-byte stack buffer. The fix adds a check that nbytes is non-zero. The flaw is fully visible in this function. The root cause is unsigned wraparound of the index, but the effect is an out-of-bounds write on the stack; the missing bounds check fits oob_write, matching the CWE-787 label.

description:
CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference
This instance (CVE-2022-0419): In load_buffer() the beach error path unconditionally writes obj->cache_buf = NULL even though obj is NULL when prelink_range is missing or after R_FREE(obj), causing a NULL pointer dereference.

review.ground_truth: In load_buffer() the beach error path unconditionally writes obj->cache_buf = NULL even though obj is NULL when prelink_range is missing or after R_FREE(obj), causing a NULL pointer dereference.
review.reasoning: When get_prelink_info_range_from_mach0 returns NULL, the code jumps to beach with obj still NULL, and beach then writes obj->cache_buf = NULL. That is a NULL dereference. The other error paths reach beach after R_FREE(obj), which also leaves obj NULL. The fix guards the write with if (obj), so this is exactly the bug repaired.

description:
CWE-401: Missing Release of Memory after Effective Lifetime (memory leak)
This instance (CVE-2019-18807): In sja1105_static_config_upload(), the kcalloc'd config_buf is leaked because the error paths after static_config_buf_prepare_for_upload() and sja1105_inhibit_tx() failures return directly instead of jumping to the kfree at out.

review.ground_truth: In sja1105_static_config_upload(), the kcalloc'd config_buf is leaked because the error paths after static_config_buf_prepare_for_upload() and sja1105_inhibit_tx() failures return directly instead of jumping to the kfree at out.
review.reasoning: config_buf is allocated with kcalloc, but the two early error returns skip the kfree at label out. One follows a static_config_buf_prepare_for_upload failure and the other a sja1105_inhibit_tx failure. The fix replaces both returns with goto out. This is a genuine memory leak, visible from this function alone.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2014-0144): curl_read_cb() does memcpy(s->orig_buf + s->buf_off, ptr, realsize) without checking realsize against the remaining space (s->buf_len - s->buf_off), so a server sending more data than requested overflows the orig_buf heap buffer.

review.ground_truth: curl_read_cb() does memcpy(s->orig_buf + s->buf_off, ptr, realsize) without checking realsize against the remaining space (s->buf_len - s->buf_off), so a server sending more data than requested overflows the orig_buf heap buffer.
review.reasoning: The libcurl write callback copies realsize bytes into s->orig_buf at offset s->buf_off and never checks the copy against s->buf_len. A server can send more data than was requested, which overflows the heap buffer. The fix clamps realsize to the space left in the buffer. Root cause is a missing bounds check before a write, so the mechanism is oob_write.

description:
CWE-401: Missing Release of Memory after Effective Lifetime (memory leak)
This instance (CVE-2021-28651): urnParseReply() allocates a temporary copy of the reply with xstrdup(inbuf) into buf for strtok parsing and never frees it before returning, leaking memory on every parsed URN response.

review.ground_truth: urnParseReply() allocates a temporary copy of the reply with xstrdup(inbuf) into buf for strtok parsing and never frees it before returning, leaking memory on every parsed URN response.
review.reasoning: buf is allocated with xstrdup(inbuf) and tokenized in place by strtok, but it is never freed before the function returns list. The fix adds xfree(buf). Every URN reply parsed leaks a copy of the reply body, so an attacker can force repeated leaks and exhaust memory. The list-growth logic (n<<=2, copying i entries into an n+1 buffer) looks correct, so there is no separate out-of-bounds access.

description:
CWE-401: Missing Release of Memory after Effective Lifetime (memory leak)
This instance (CVE-2019-19069): In fastrpc_dma_buf_attach(), the kzalloc'd attachment 'a' is not freed when dma_get_sgtable() fails, so the error path returns -EINVAL and leaks the memory.

review.ground_truth: In fastrpc_dma_buf_attach(), the kzalloc'd attachment 'a' is not freed when dma_get_sgtable() fails, so the error path returns -EINVAL and leaks the memory.
review.reasoning: The attachment struct 'a' is allocated with kzalloc. When dma_get_sgtable() fails, the function returns -EINVAL without freeing 'a'. The fix adds kfree(a) on that path. This is a genuine memory leak, visible from this function alone.

description:
CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write
This instance (CVE-2019-9500): In brcmf_wowl_nd_results(), the firmware-controlled netinfo->SSID_len is used unchecked as the memcpy length into the 32-byte cfg->wowl.nd->ssid.ssid buffer, causing a heap buffer overflow when it exceeds IEEE80211_MAX_SSID_LEN.

review.ground_truth: In brcmf_wowl_nd_results(), the firmware-controlled netinfo->SSID_len is used unchecked as the memcpy length into the 32-byte cfg->wowl.nd->ssid.ssid buffer, causing a heap buffer overflow when it exceeds IEEE80211_MAX_SSID_LEN.
review.reasoning: The SSID_len field comes from firmware-supplied event data and is used directly as the memcpy length into cfg->wowl.nd->ssid.ssid, which is a fixed 32-byte (IEEE80211_MAX_SSID_LEN) buffer. Nothing bounds the length, so a malicious event writes past the end of the heap buffer. The fix clamps SSID_len to IEEE80211_MAX_SSID_LEN. The flaw is visible in this function, given that ssid is the standard 32-byte cfg80211_ssid array.

description:
CWE-125: Out-of-bounds Read
This instance (CVE-2017-5336): In cdk_pk_get_keyid(), the result of _gnutls_mpi_print(pk->mpi[0], p, &n) is unchecked and n is not verified to be >= 8, so the reads p[n-8]..p[n-1] go outside the stack buffer p when the RSA modulus is shorter than 8 bytes or the print fails.

review.ground_truth: In cdk_pk_get_keyid(), the result of _gnutls_mpi_print(pk->mpi[0], p, &n) is unchecked and n is not verified to be >= 8, so the reads p[n-8]..p[n-1] go outside the stack buffer p when the RSA modulus is shorter than 8 bytes or the print fails.
review.reasoning: In the v3 RSA branch, the return value of _gnutls_mpi_print() is ignored and n is never checked to be at least 8. The code then reads p[n-8] through p[n-1]. If the MPI is shorter than 8 bytes, n-8 wraps around because n is a size_t, so the index lands outside the stack buffer p. If the print call fails, n and p may hold garbage. The fix adds the rc<0 || n<8 check, so the flaw is a stack out-of-bounds read.

description:
CWE-416: Use After Free
This instance (CVE-2021-20231): In key_share_send_params(), lengthp points into extdata->data before _gnutls_buffer_append_prefix/client_gen_key_share may realloc the buffer, so the final _gnutls_write_uint16(..., lengthp) writes through a dangling pointer into freed memory.

review.ground_truth: In key_share_send_params(), lengthp points into extdata->data before _gnutls_buffer_append_prefix/client_gen_key_share may realloc the buffer, so the final _gnutls_write_uint16(..., lengthp) writes through a dangling pointer into freed memory.
review.reasoning: The function caches lengthp = &extdata->data[extdata->length] before appending to the buffer. The later appends (the prefix and client_gen_key_share) can realloc extdata->data, leaving lengthp dangling. _gnutls_write_uint16 then writes through the stale pointer into freed memory. The fix stores an offset instead and recomputes the pointer after the appends, so the flaw is real and lives in this function.

description:
CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference
This instance (CVE-2022-1620): In fname_match(), after the first vim_regexec() fails and can leave rmp->regprog NULL for an invalid pattern, the function calls vim_regexec() again on the home_replace_save() result without checking rmp->regprog, causing a NULL pointer dereference.

review.ground_truth: In fname_match(), after the first vim_regexec() fails and can leave rmp->regprog NULL for an invalid pattern, the function calls vim_regexec() again on the home_replace_save() result without checking rmp->regprog, causing a NULL pointer dereference.
review.reasoning: If the regexp program fails during the first vim_regexec() call (an invalid pattern), rmp->regprog can be freed and set to NULL. fname_match() then calls vim_regexec() a second time with the home-replaced name, and that call dereferences the NULL regprog in vim_regexec_string. The fix adds a check that rmp->regprog is non-NULL before the retry. Seeing this requires knowing that vim_regexec can clear regprog, so it is only partly local.

description:
